1966 to 2026

The complete timeline

Every sourced entry in the archive, 832 of them, in the order they happened. Under each year sit a further 2318 lines from the Herald index: headlines the project has recorded but not yet worked into the record. On a phone, one decade at a time reads better.

1960s 1970s 1980s 1990s 2000s 2010s 2020s The complete timeline

1966-67Jim Haynes (president)

April 1966President Kelly Thompson approves the constitution. The proposed constitution of the Associated Students of Western Kentucky University was completed in late March and approved on 1 April. The copy held by WKU Archives is dated 7 April 1966. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Constitution
April 1966Thompson's approval letter is addressed to committee chair Reed Morgan. The archived copy of Thompson's approval letter names the organizing committee that drafted the constitution: Reed Morgan as chair, John Lovett as vice chair. Morgan's committee did the drafting; Jim Haynes was elected to lead the government it created six weeks later. In the recordUA3/3/1, Letter to Organizational Committee for a Western Student Organization, 1 Apr 1966
26 April 1966Students ratify the constitution, 1,812 to 726. A four-day referendum. 2,538 students voted - a larger raw turnout than most SGA elections have managed since. In the recordWKU SGA history
18 May 1966Jim Haynes elected first president. Seven weeks from presidential approval to a seated student president. Western Kentucky State College became Western Kentucky University on 16 June, so the university and its student government are almost exactly the same age. In the recordWKU SGA history
29 September 1966The new government opens its first full year. The Herald's first issue of the fall reported the student senate ratifying a government appointment as the Associated Students began their first full academic year. Students had approved the constitution and elected officers the previous spring. In the recordHerald 46:1, 29 Sep 1966
27 October 1966Doing well, but lacking communication. Midway through the fall semester the Herald judged that Associated Students leaders were performing well but were failing to communicate with the students they represented. It was the first public report card on the year-old government. In the recordHerald 46:5, 27 Oct 1966
10 November 1966Government and administration meet on campus problems. The Herald reported Student Government Association leaders meeting with President Kelly Thompson to discuss campus problems, an early instance of the year-old government dealing directly with the administration. In the recordHerald 46:7, 10 Nov 1966
9 March 1967Herald warns of a 'popularity bandwagon' in the spring election. A week before the presidential campaign opened, the Herald ran a piece by Fran Salyers arguing that popularity, not merit, was set to decide the Associated Students election. In the recordHerald 46:16, 9 Mar 1967
16 March 1967Two vie for the presidency. The Herald reported two candidates seeking the Associated Students presidency, with campaigns for the organization's second presidential election set to open the following Monday. In the recordHerald 46:17, 16 Mar 1967
4 May 1967Swearing-in set for May 10. The Herald announced that newly elected Associated Student officers would be sworn in on May 10, 1967, completing the organization's first full transfer of leadership. In the recordHerald 46:22, 4 May 1967
12 May 1967First year judged: organization, progress, apathy. Reviewing the government's first year, the Herald found organization and progress alongside persistent student apathy. The same issue carried president-elect William Menser's plans for 1967-68 and a letter arguing that the Associated Students really worked. In the recordHerald 46:23, 12 May 1967
18 May 1967Herald presses students to vote as the year closes. Days after the outgoing administration's year-end review, the Herald ran a piece headlined 'Goof Government Needs Student Vote,' pressing students toward greater turnout as Menser's incoming administration took over. In the recordHerald 46:24, 18 May 1967
30 May 1967Dean Keown proposes a budget for the new government. Dean of Students Charles Keown sent President Kelly Thompson a memo proposing a student fee structure to create a budget for the Associated Student Government. He attached fee models gathered from universities across the South and Midwest. In the recordUA3/3/1 Keown memo, 30 May 1967

1967-68William Menser (president)

14 September 1967Menser and President Thompson open the school year together. The first Herald of the 1967-68 year carried a joint welcome to students headlined "Dr. Kelly Thompson, William Menser Welcome Students." The same issue ran an item headed "Associated Student Government Events Set," laying out the organisation's calendar for the coming term. In the recordHerald 47:1, 14 Sep 1967
14 October 1967Rodes-Harlin Hall opens as a nine-story women's dorm. The Herald covered the opening of Rodes-Harlin Hall, a new nine-story women's residence hall, as campus construction continued to expand housing capacity. In the recordHerald 47:6, 14 Oct 1967
2 November 1967Herald floats a student seat on the Board of Regents. A Herald article headlined 'Ward Favors Student on Board of Regents' reported support for putting a student on the Board of Regents, months before Western sent lobbyists to Frankfort or a bill reached committee. In the recordHerald 47:10, 2 Nov 1967
2 November 1967ASG sponsors a Friday dance. The same issue that floated a student regent seat also reported the Associated Student Government sponsoring a campus dance that Friday. In the recordHerald 47:10, 2 Nov 1967
8 December 1967ASG survey of student activity preferences. The Associated Students published a survey of what activities students wanted, reported by Ellen Bennett in the same issue as a Herald piece commending the government's efforts and coverage of the Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association backing a proposal for student representation. In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967
8 December 1967Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association backs student representation. The statewide student press association came out for a proposal for student representation, reported in the same Herald issue as the Associated Students' activity survey. In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967
8 December 1967Associated Students survey students on activity preferences. The Herald reported the results of an Associated Students survey under the headline "Associated Students' Survey Reveals Activity Preferences." The same issue carried a letter headed "Commends Associated Student Government's Efforts." In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967
8 December 1967State press association backs student representation proposal. The 8 December 1967 Herald reported that the Kentucky Intercollegiate Press Association had come out in support of the proposal for student representation. The item ran alongside the paper's coverage of Associated Students activity that week. In the recordHerald 47:14, 8 Dec 1967
8 February 1968A bill to put a student on the Board of Regents reaches committee. Reported by Ron Lawrence. Western had sent lobbyists to Frankfort for it earlier that month. The same issue carries students berating dorm rules and a letter headed 'Wanted: Work for Judicial Council'. In the recordHerald 47:18, 8 Feb 1968
22 February 1968Herald questions ASG's Judicial Council as students organize a book swap. Bill Martin's column questioned the Judicial Council's work, while the same issue reported the Associated Student Government directing a student book swap. In the recordHerald 47:20, 22 Feb 1968
29 February 1968WKU sends lobbyists to Frankfort for a student on the Board of Regents. The same Herald issue carries a tuition increase, a discussion group on major issues before the Associated Student Government and a committee investigating women's dormitory rules. This is the origin of the student regent seat. In the recordHerald 47:20 [21], 29 Feb 1968
29 February 1968Associated Students discussion group takes up major campus issues. The Herald announced that major issues would be heard in an Associated Student Government discussion group. The same issue reported that Western had sent lobbyists in support of a bill to place a student on the Board of Regents, and carried coverage of a tuition increase. In the recordHerald 47:20 [21], 29 Feb 1968
4 April 1968William Menser becomes WKU's first student regent. Two months after the bill was in committee, the Herald reported that Menser 'assumes duties as Regent Board Member'. The seat carried no vote at first. The same issue opens candidate declarations for the next student government election. In the recordHerald 47:26, 4 Apr 1968
11 April 1968Filing reveals few candidates for the spring election. Alana White reported that filing for Associated Student Government offices turned up few candidates, in the same issue as a piece urging that criteria for the offices be voiced. In the recordHerald 47:27, 11 Apr 1968
29 April 1968Menser discusses the head fee. The same issue that opened coverage of the Straeffer-Whitley race to succeed him carried a piece on outgoing president Menser discussing the student head fee. The archive does not yet hold the article's text. In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968
29 April 1968Herald analyzes ASG's past performance under Menser. A retrospective headlined 'Past Performance of Associated Student Government Analyzed' ran as Menser's term ended, in the same issue as the Straeffer-Whitley presidential campaign coverage. The archive does not yet hold the article's text. In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968
29 April 1968Herald reviews the Associated Student Government's record. As Menser's term drew to a close the Herald ran an assessment headed "Past Performance of Associated Student Government Analyzed." It appeared in the same issue as the campaign coverage for the officers who would succeed him. In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968
9 May 1968Bill Straeffer wins the presidency; the Herald calls the election a failure. The issue reporting Straeffer's win also carries an editorial headed 'Elections Illustrate Faults, Indifference'. Turnout anxiety shows up in the second contested election the organisation ever held. In the recordHerald 47:30, 9 May 1968

1968-69Reed Morgan (role unresolved) · Bill Straeffer (president) · Paul Gerard, III (student regent)

29 April 1968Straeffer and Whitley vie for the presidency. The Herald's pre-election coverage set out the field: Bill Straeffer against Charles Whitley for president, Terry Gilpin against Bob Van Corbach for vice president, and contested races down to secretary, treasurer, and congressman at large. In the recordHerald 47:28, 29 Apr 1968
2 May 1968Straeffer elected president, 1,732 to 1,098; turnout 34 percent. The Associated Students' internal election-results memo lists the full slate: Bill Straeffer over Charles Whitley for president, Terry Gilpin over Bob Van Corbach for vice president, Becky Cooper over Mary Miller for secretary, Tonii Rizzo over John Combs for treasurer, and John Cobelli and Janie Heathcoat elected congressmen at large over Billy Goodman and Scott Phillips. Total turnout was 2,894 votes, about 34 percent of enrollment. In the recordUA3/3/1 Memo Re: Results of Election, Ron Beck, 3 May 1968Read it here
3 October 1968Committees go to work. The Herald reported Associated Students committees swinging into action as the year began. The same issue noted that booking problems still plagued the group's entertainment calendar. In the recordHerald 48:3, 3 Oct 1968
5 December 1968Judicial Council begins hearing cases. The Associated Students Judicial Council was hearing student cases, the Herald reported, an early exercise of the judicial power the young government claimed under its constitution. In the recordHerald 48:12, 5 Dec 1968
9 January 1969Bringing speakers and shows to the Hill. The Herald reported the Associated Students working to bring speakers and entertainment to campus, alongside notice of an upcoming Associated Students dance. In the recordHerald 48:15, 9 Jan 1969
13 February 1969A buffer against campus turmoil. As campus unrest spread nationally, the Herald suggested the Associated Student Government could deter turmoil at Western. The same issue reported president Bill Straeffer moving to discontinue the Greek-oriented Campus Favorites election. In the recordHerald 48:17, 13 Feb 1969
27 February 1969Paul Gerard profiled as student regent. Herald writer Bruce Tucker profiled student regent Paul Gerard, and the paper reported a committee appointed to study revision of the Associated Students constitution. In the recordHerald 48:19, 27 Feb 1969
13 March 1969Election Tuesday as declarations continue. Declarations of candidacy continued as the Associated Students election was set for the following Tuesday. In the recordHerald 48:21, 13 Mar 1969
8 May 1969Straeffer and Gilpin review their year. The Herald ran the outgoing administration's own account of its year under the headline 'Associated Students Produces Year of Advancement,' alongside a companion piece on Straeffer and Gilpin reviewing their term. In the recordHerald 48:28 [29], 8 May 1969
22 May 1969Zielke and Porter outline the coming year. Incoming leaders Larry Zielke and David Porter outlined the coming Associated Students administration for the Herald, closing the 1968-69 transition. In the recordHerald 48:30, 22 May 1969

1969-70Paul Gerard, III (student regent) · Larry Zielke (president)

25 March 1969Genzianelli and Zielke clash for the presidency. The Herald's Associated Students election special edition covered a two-way presidential race between Frank Genzianelli and Larry Zielke, and a separate race for the second officer spot between John Lyne and David Porter. In the recordHerald 48:23, 25 Mar 1969
22 May 1969Zielke and Porter outline the coming administration. With Larry Zielke elected president and David Porter as his second officer, the Herald ran their plans for the 1969-70 Associated Students administration. The same issue covered President Kelly Thompson's resignation announcement. In the recordHerald 48:30 [31], 22 May 1969
22 May 1969President Kelly Thompson announces his resignation. Thompson, who had approved the Associated Students constitution in 1966, announced he would step down as WKU's president. The Herald covered it in the same issue as the incoming Zielke-Porter student administration. In the recordHerald 48:30 [31], 22 May 1969
7 October 1969Associated Student Congress endorses the Vietnam Moratorium. The Herald called it a bold step. The clearest early example of the body taking a position outside the campus fence - the same argument that returns in 2017 and 2023. In the recordHerald 49:5, 7 Oct 1969
4 November 1969New constitution sent back for study. The Associated Student Government returned its proposed new constitution for further study while limiting how long the review could run. The same issue reported the group enlisting merchants for a student discount plan. In the recordHerald 49:13, 4 Nov 1969
7 November 1969Students start grading the faculty. An ASG committee compiled the results of Western's first student teacher-evaluation effort. The Herald had already editorialised demanding the tabulation move faster. In the recordHerald 49:11, 7 Nov 1969
9 December 1969ASG urges a probe of student housing. The Associated Student Government urged an investigation of student housing, one of the fall's most pointed challenges to university policy. In the recordHerald 49:20, 9 Dec 1969
13 January 1970Congress joins the fight against the superboard. The Associated Students Congress joined the fight against a proposed state superboard for higher education, and the Herald's editorial page argued the same week that the student regent deserved a vote. In the recordHerald 49:24, 13 Jan 1970
10 February 1970'Associate' regents want voting power. Two pieces in one issue: Associated Students seeking voting rights for the student regent, and student and faculty 'associate' regents pressing for a vote. An editorial calls for broad support of Senate Bill 75. Two years in, the seat was still symbolic. In the recordHerald 49:26, 10 Feb 1970
13 March 1970Lyne wins the presidency before the race begins. John Lyne won the Associated Students presidency before the race began, his bid unopposed. The same issue reported the legislature dropping the bill that would have given student regents a vote, under a headline that lawmakers had kept students impotent. In the recordHerald 49:35, 13 Mar 1970
24 April 1970Four constitution changes go to a vote. The Associated Students Congress moved to seek ratification of four constitution changes, and the Herald saluted vice president David Porter as the government's unsung hero. In the recordHerald 49:43, 24 Apr 1970
8 May 1970ASG figures in the Kent State week delegations. During the Strike Western! demonstrations after the Kent State shootings, John Lyne and Larry Zielke were among the students who presented resolutions to President Dero Downing and Dean Charles Keown on May 8, and both sat with the group that received the university's response on May 11. In the recordWKU Timeline: Strike Western!
16 May 1970Congress endorses Downing's reply to protesters. As the Strike Western! week wound down, the Associated Student Congress unanimously endorsed President Dero Downing's reply to the protesters, aligning the elected student government with the administration's answer to the demonstrations. In the recordHerald 49:49, 16 May 1970

1970-71John Lyne (president)

13 March 1970John Lyne wins the presidency before the race begins. No opponent filed against Lyne for the 1970-71 Associated Students presidency, and the Herald reported him elected without a contest. In the recordHerald 49:35, 13 Mar 1970
27 March 1970Doug Alexander captures the vice presidency. Alexander beat Steve Tichenor for the Associated Students vice presidency in the vote held the week after Lyne's uncontested presidential win. In the recordHerald 49:39, 27 Mar 1970
28 August 1970Regents seat eight students on the Academic Council. An editorial framed it as the Regents opening doors to student expression in academics. Representation was arriving faster in the curriculum committees than on the board itself. In the recordHerald 50:1, 28 Aug 1970
27 October 1970A resolution on the women's curfew, five months after Kent State. The Associated Student Congress passed a curfew resolution; the Herald reported abolition was unlikely that year and editorialised that the curfew was obsolete. The letters page in the same issue is almost entirely students arguing about Kent State. In the recordHerald 50:17, 27 Oct 1970
6 November 1970Congress funds Kunstler and Devlin lectures, plans new constitution. The Associated Student Congress passed a lecture bill funding campus appearances by William Kunstler and Bernadette Devlin, and the Herald reported the Congress was drafting a new constitution. In the recordHerald 50:20, 6 Nov 1970
20 November 1970Congress endorses a proposed constitution. The Associated Student Congress endorsed a proposed new constitution, continuing the reform effort launched two weeks earlier. The same issue previewed William Kunstler's scheduled Monday lecture, funded by the Congress's 6 November bill. In the recordHerald 50:24, 20 Nov 1970
26 January 1971A committee opens a constitution study. A committee was formed to study Associated Student constitutions, renewing the reform effort that had produced a second constitution the year before. In the recordHerald 50:31, 26 Jan 1971
29 January 1971Resolutions pass; a center for students sought. Resolutions gained approval in the Associated Students Congress, and the government pressed its call for a center for students in the Herald's pages. In the recordHerald 50:32, 29 Jan 1971
12 February 1971Constitution committee turns to judicial reform. The constitution study committee took up judicial reform provisions, the Herald reported. The same issue carried a student's published praise for William Kunstler's campus lecture. In the recordHerald 50:35, 12 Feb 1971
2 March 1971Twenty offices go begging. With filing open for the spring elections, the Herald reported twenty student government offices going begging for candidates. In the recordHerald 50:40, 2 Mar 1971
26 March 1971Eighty-four to seek campus offices. By election eve the field had filled out: the Herald counted 84 students seeking campus offices in Tuesday's voting. In the recordHerald 50:43, 26 Mar 1971
6 April 1971Linda Jones elected first woman president. Linda Jones was elected the first woman president of the Associated Student Government. The Western Alumnus pictured her being sworn in alongside faculty regent Lowell Harrison. In the recordWKU Timeline: Linda Jones (Western Alumnus, 6 Apr 1971)
16 April 1971New congress leaders air the issues. The newly elected Associated Student Congress leaders aired major issues for the Herald and gave clues on what to expect in the fall. In the recordHerald 50:49, 16 Apr 1971

1971-72Linda Jones (president)

6 April 1971Linda Jones elected first woman ASG president. Jones became the first woman elected president of the Associated Student Government. A photograph in the Western Alumnus shows her being sworn in alongside faculty regent Lowell Harrison by Georgia Bates. In the recordWKU Timeline, Western Alumnus, 6 Apr 1971
14 September 1971Associated Students affiliates with a wider student association. An early attempt to gain leverage beyond the Hill. Which body it joined is not clear from the article index alone. In the recordHerald 51:3, 14 Sep 1971
February 1972'Student Regent May Get Vote'. Four years after the seat was created it was still non-voting. The same issue has the Academic Council clarifying grievance procedure and an Associated Students open session scheduled for 12 February. In the recordHerald 51:32, 1 Feb 1972
22 February 1972Congress votes on a section of the new constitution; full text published. The Associated Students Congress voted on a section of the proposed constitution, and the Herald printed the full text of the document's proposed executive branch alongside the vote coverage. In the recordHerald 51:39, 22 Feb 1972
25 February 1972'Chaos Reigns at Associated Students Meeting'. The same issue carries students planning a petition to force dorm visitation and a separate piece arguing student interest had collapsed and the Associated Students had followed it down. In the recordHerald 51:39, 25 Feb 1972
29 February 1972Executive branch of a revised constitution accepted. The Herald reported acceptance of the executive branch of a revised Associated Students constitution. The archive does not yet hold the article's text or what changed. In the recordHerald 51:40, 29 Feb 1972
29 February 1972Kentucky Civil Liberties Union plans court action on behalf of Associated Students. The Herald reported the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union planning court action on behalf of Associated Students, under a headline that also named The Fly, a separate WKU underground newspaper active that year. The archive does not yet hold the article's text, so the underlying dispute is not yet confirmed. In the recordHerald 51:40, 29 Feb 1972
29 February 1972Linda Jones publicly corrects the Herald. President Linda Jones wrote a piece headlined 'Associated Students Corrects Herald', a public correction of the paper's own reporting on the organization. The archive does not yet hold the article's text or what it corrected. In the recordHerald 51:40, 29 Feb 1972
28 March 1972'Vote Yes' campaign for the new constitution; referendum set. The Herald carried a piece by Nancy Pape urging students to 'Vote Yes' on the Associated Students constitution ahead of a referendum set for the next two days, in the same issue that advertised an Associated Students mini-concert. In the recordHerald 51:44, 28 Mar 1972
28 March 1972Associated Students endorses the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union lawsuit. The Herald reported that Associated Students formally endorsed the Kentucky Civil Liberties Union's lawsuit, a month after the Herald first reported the union planning court action connected to the organization and The Fly. In the recordHerald 51:44, 28 Mar 1972
28 April 1972A strike threat over visitation, and six votes won on a university council. A Mass Action Committee called for a strike over dorm visitation while the Associated Students installed next year's officers. Buried in the same issue: students gained six votes on a university council. Linda Jones reflected on her term. In the recordHerald 51:50, 28 Apr 1972

25 April 1972Jordan wins the presidency. The Herald reported Ed Jordan's win under the headline 'Ed Jordan Wins Top Office,' alongside an editorial by Pence and Carter arguing the new ASG president needed cooperation and support to succeed. In the recordHerald 51:52, 25 Apr 1972

1974-75Gregory McKinney (student regent) · Jeffrey Consolo (president)

27 August 1974Regents extend visitation as the year opens. The Herald's opening issue reported the Board of Regents extending dormitory visitation and approving a $29.8 million budget at the board's first session of the year. In the recordHerald 50:1, 27 Aug 1974
27 September 1974Keffer wins freshman vote; Consolo names eight to congress. The Herald reported that Jay Keffer won the freshman election for the top freshman post. In the same issue, ASG president Jeff Consolo tabbed eight students for seats in the ASG congress, and the Academic Council heard a proposal for more student votes. In the recordHerald 50:9, 27 Sep 1974
15 October 1974Protesters urge ASG revamping. Protesters urged a revamping of the Associated Student Government. The same issue carried Janet Steen's report that ASG ecology projects were non-existent. In the recordHerald 50:14, 15 Oct 1974
19 November 1974ASG schedules Kiss and initiates concert hour. ASG scheduled the rock band Kiss and initiated a concert hour, part of its role booking campus entertainment that fall. The concert program later became a major source of financial trouble for the organization. In the recordHerald 50:24, 19 Nov 1974
21 January 1975ASG rescues the Student Volunteer Bureau. ASG agreed to administer the Student Volunteer Bureau. The Herald reported that the bureau was rescued by the student government's action. In the recordHerald 50:30, 21 Jan 1975
7 February 1975Budget troubles threaten ASG entertainment role. The Herald reported that financial difficulties might force ASG to drop its entertainment duties, and the ASG congress heard the treasurer's budget explanation. Columnists Dave Allen and Craig Griffith examined the organization's budget problems in the same issue. In the recordHerald 50:35, 7 Feb 1975
28 February 1975Quorum failures halt ASG twice in one week. ASG action was halted twice during the week by a lack of quorum. A Herald editorial said the confusion in ASG signaled a need for change. In the recordHerald 50:41, 28 Feb 1975
21 March 1975Primary canceled; constitutional change approved. The primary election for Associated Student Government was canceled, and the student government approved a constitutional change. A letter writer in the same issue criticized the Herald's coverage of ASG. In the recordHerald 50:43, 21 Mar 1975
28 March 1975Voting procedures simplified for the spring election. ASG passed a motion simplifying voting procedures for the spring election, and the ASG treasurer took to the Herald's letters column the same day. In the recordHerald 50:45, 28 Mar 1975
11 April 1975Steve Henry elected to lead ASG. Following the spring election, the Herald reported that incoming president Steve Henry would give activities priority in Associated Student Government. The organization also prepared to name its top member, and the paper noted that Greeks continued to dominate the campus political scene. In the recordHerald 50:49, 11 Apr 1975
15 April 1975New officers installed; concert plans dropped. New Associated Student Government officers were installed at the day's meeting, as the outgoing congress abandoned plans for a final concert of the semester and the editorial page pronounced incoming president Steve Henry's entertainment plan inadequate. In the recordHerald 50:50, 15 Apr 1975

1975-76Steve Henry (president)

19 September 1975Big concert, big loss. An ASG concert drew 4,300 people but lost $7,000, the Herald reported, opening a money argument that ran through the fall. In the recordHerald 51:7, 19 Sep 1975
3 October 1975ASG suggests a campus bank. ASG suggested creating a campus bank for students, one of the new administration's early service proposals. In the recordHerald 51:11, 3 Oct 1975
17 October 1975Budget approved amid concert debate. The ASG budget won approval as concerts were discussed, two weeks after the money-losing season opener had put the program under scrutiny. In the recordHerald 51:15, 17 Oct 1975
24 October 1975Fund misuse charges aired. Charges of ASG fund misuse were heard in the same week the congress voted to create an activities committee and a letter writer attacked the organization. In the recordHerald 51:17, 24 Oct 1975
25 November 1975A budget remedy and a book exchange. The Herald weighed whether a new ASG budget offered a remedy, and reported a spring semester book exchange to be co-sponsored by ASG and Veterans on Campus. President Steve Henry moved to change the concert proposal the same week. In the recordHerald 51:26, 25 Nov 1975
12 December 1975Petition drive seeks support. ASG sought student support with a petition and prepared to hear appeals over its concert policy as the fall semester closed. In the recordHerald 51:30, 12 Dec 1975
26 March 1976Faulk impeachment hearings open as campaign begins. The Associated Student Government began impeachment hearings against congress member Gerard Faulk the same week candidates for the spring election, including Christy Vogt, were set to speak to students. An editorial the same issue held up Associated Student Government's troubles as a cautionary example for the university's newly forming Faculty Senate. In the recordHerald 51:49, 26 Mar 1976
2 April 1976Bruce Smith and Christy Vogt survive the primary, 527 ballots cast. The Herald reported the Associated Student Government presidential primary under the headline "Bruce Smith, Christy Vogt Survive as 527 Cast Ballots," the two advancing to the 9 April runoff that Vogt went on to win. In the recordHerald 51:51, 2 Apr 1976
9 April 1976Election season and an acquittal. During the spring election season ASG acquitted congress member Gerard Faulk in an internal proceeding, and the Herald polled voters on the races. In the recordHerald 51:53, 9 Apr 1976
9 April 1976Christy Vogt wins the ASG presidency. The Herald reported Christy Vogt's win in the Associated Student Government presidential election under the headline "Christy Vogt Wins Election," with Vogt's own "Winner Says Thanks" running in the same issue. The paper reported the result the same week Gerard Faulk was acquitted in his impeachment case. In the recordHerald 51:53, 9 Apr 1976
27 April 1976Herald supplement recaps a year of ASG wins. A special supplement to the Herald, paid for and written by the Associated Student Government, summed up the outgoing Henry administration's year: women's hours abolished with ASG's backing, better intramural facilities credited to ASG resolutions, a new ASG discount card program, a second campus site for cashing checks, and a Veterans on Campus book exchange. The supplement also printed the year's roster of congress members and its bills and resolutions, and carried Christy Vogt's own piece on laundry facility improvement. In the recordStudent Insight (Herald supplement), 27 Apr 1976
30 April 1976Final meeting approves a budget. The congress approved a tentative budget at the final ASG meeting of the year, and the Herald assessed how Steve Henry's year had required balancing his twin jobs as student regent and ASG president. In the recordHerald 51:59, 30 Apr 1976

1976-77Christy Mollozzi (president)

7 September 1976ASG creates constitutional revision committee. The Associated Student Government congress passed Bill 2, creating a committee charged with revising the organization's constitution. Constitutional revision remained on the ASG agenda for the rest of the school year and appeared again among proposed amendments and a spring referendum bill. In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 2 - Constitutional Revision Committee, 7 Sep 1976
26 October 1976ASG asks WKU for a student minimum wage. The congress adopted Resolution 13, proposing that Western institute a minimum wage policy for all student employees. It was part of a heavy fall docket that also included resolutions on parking, laundry services, non-smoking areas and residence hall change machines. In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Resolution 13 - Minimum Wage, 26 Oct 1976
9 November 1976Seals and Crofts concert loses ASG $3,800. The Herald reported that the Seals and Crofts concert set the Associated Student Government back $3,800. Concert finances would remain a recurring sore point for ASG through the rest of the decade. In the recordHerald 52:21, 9 Nov 1976
23 November 1976ASG recommends preregistration for all students. The Herald reported that ASG would recommend preregistration for all students. Advance registration was one of the four items president Christy Vogt later carried into her end-of-year recommendations to the administration. In the recordHerald 52:25, 23 Nov 1976
15 February 1977Bill calls for ASG to evaluate itself. Bill 6 proposed that the Associated Student Government conduct a self-evaluation "for the purposes of transparency and improvement." In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 6 - ASG Evaluation, 15 Feb 1977
25 February 1977Discrimination resolution fails as 14 abstain. Fourteen members abstained as the Associated Student Government rejected a resolution on discrimination, the Herald reported. The same issue noted that filing for ASG posts would begin the following Monday. In the recordHerald 52:43, 25 Feb 1977
8 March 1977ASG passes bill opposing tuition increase. The congress approved Bill 9, formally opposing a proposed tuition increase. The same March meeting produced Bill 8, which created a Complaint Committee to handle student grievances. In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Bill 9 - Opposition to Tuition Increase, 8 Mar 1977
April 1977Four candidates open the race to succeed Vogt. The Herald previewed a crowded ASG election: Tom Blair, Kirt Grubbs, Mark McChesney and Bob Moore all sought the presidency, with voting set for a Tuesday primary. Three candidates ran for the administrative vice presidency and four for the activities post in the same election. In the recordHerald 52:49, 1 Apr 1977
12 April 1977Vogt urges involvement as her term closes. With her term nearly over, president Christy Vogt wrote "Urges Involvement" for the Herald, days before Bob Moore's election to succeed her. In the recordHerald 52:52, 12 Apr 1977
15 April 1977Bob Moore elected ASG president by 26 votes. One of the narrowest margins in the record. The same issue carries the outgoing president congratulating voters, the faculty asking for a say in hiring, and Western fighting a beer licence for a local pizzeria. In the recordHerald 52:53, 15 Apr 1977
26 April 1977Vogt closes the congress with four recommendations. President Christy Vogt sent a letter closing the congress and thanking ASG members for their work. She left four items to recommend to the administration: constitutional revision, extended hours for student buildings, open visitation and advanced registration. In the recordSGA Records (UA66), Christy Vogt Letter, 26 Apr 1977

1977-78Robert Moore (president)

8 September 1977ASG awaits approval of constitution changes. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government was awaiting approval of changes to its constitution as the fall term opened. The story ran alongside a look at how ASG's concert booking process actually worked. In the recordHerald 53:5, 8 Sep 1977
25 October 1977Moore questions freshman candidates' campaign spending. President Bob Moore publicly questioned how freshman class candidates were spending their campaign money. The Herald ran an editorial the same week, 'Bob Moore's Comment Isn't Good Politics,' pushing back on his remark. In the recordHerald 53:18, 25 Oct 1977
25 October 1977'A$G?' - Moore questions freshman campaign spending. President Bob Moore publicly questioned spending by freshman candidates, in a story the Herald headlined 'A$G?'. The paper answered with an editorial arguing that Moore's comment was not good politics, and Moore wrote back disputing it. In the recordHerald 53:18, 25 Oct 1977
27 October 1977David Bass named ASG vice president. The Associated Student Government named David Bass its new vice president. The same issue carried Moore's letter disputing the Herald's editorial on candidate spending. In the recordHerald 53:19, 27 Oct 1977
17 November 1977ASG and Interhall Council back coed dorm, end of door-ajar rule. ASG and the Interhall Council backed a coed dorm and abolition of the door-ajar visitation rule. The vote followed weeks in which the two bodies weighed a dorm petition and the Herald urged ASG to represent students in the dorm protest. In the recordHerald 53:25, 17 Nov 1977
24 January 1978ASG signs Atlanta Rhythm Section and Brick. ASG signed Atlanta Rhythm Section and Brick for spring concerts. Ticket sales proved weak, and by late February the Herald was reporting on the organization's concert losses. In the recordHerald 53:35, 24 Jan 1978
21 February 1978Concert losses will not stop a free concert. The Herald reported that losses would not halt an ASG free concert, and that ASG had thrown in towels as a bonus for performers. An editorial declared that the cry for better concerts had finally been heard. In the recordHerald 53:43, 21 Feb 1978
9 March 1978Spending limits set for the coming ASG election. The Associated Student Government set spending limits for candidates ahead of the spring election that would choose Moore's successor. In the recordHerald 53:49, 9 Mar 1978
6 April 1978Thornton and Johnson contest the presidency; four offices go uncontested. Steve Thornton and Ed Johnson faced off for the Associated Student Government presidency, Thornton campaigning on his experience, while four other offices had no opponent on the ballot. In the recordHerald 53:54, 6 Apr 1978
6 April 1978ASG elections held with four offices uncontested. Students voted in the Associated Student Government elections with four offices uncontested. Candidate Steve Thornton told the Herald his experience was an important factor in the race. In the recordHerald 53:54, 6 Apr 1978
11 April 1978Johnson contests his loss to Thornton. Ed Johnson, having lost the presidential race, contested the Associated Student Government election result. In the recordHerald 53:55, 11 Apr 1978
18 April 1978Judicial Council denies Johnson's appeal. After a long debate, the Associated Student Government Judicial Council denied Ed Johnson's appeal of the election result, letting Steve Thornton's win stand. In the recordHerald 53:57, 18 Apr 1978
18 April 1978Judicial council denies election appeal. After losing candidate Ed Johnson contested the election result, the ASG judicial council denied his appeal following a long debate. The Herald had criticized the appeal system's lack of objectivity while the case was pending. In the recordHerald 53:57, 18 Apr 1978

1978-79Steven Thornton (president)

7 September 1978Roll-call votes made public; Moore ruled ineligible. ASG decided its roll-call votes would be made public, the Herald reported. The same issue reported that former president Bob Moore was ineligible for an Associated Student Government job. In the recordHerald 54:5, 7 Sep 1978
9 September 1978President Dero Downing announces his resignation. Downing, who had led WKU since 1969, announced he would step down effective 31 December 1978. Vice President John Minton took over as interim president the following January while the Board of Regents searched for a successor. In the recordWKU Timeline: Dero Downing
28 September 1978ASG tables an open house bill. The Associated Student Government set aside a proposed open house bill rather than act on it, one of the fall semester's first pieces of business under new president Steven Thornton. In the recordHerald 54:11, 28 Sep 1978
28 September 1978David Rue wins freshman presidency by 11 votes. In the freshman election held under ASG, David Rue was elected president by 11 votes. Only 95 students had voted in the freshman primary the week before. In the recordHerald 54:11, 28 Sep 1978
19 October 1978ASG backs Thornton's plan for minority representation. The Associated Student Government backed president Steve Thornton's plan to add minorities to the regents' presidential screening panel. The Herald's editorial page argued the regents should appoint a minority representative. In the recordHerald 54:17, 19 Oct 1978
30 November 1978ASG approves revised constitution. The congress approved a revised Associated Student Government constitution. The revision capped a fall in which ASG also pushed teacher evaluations and parking rezoning. In the recordHerald 54:28, 30 Nov 1978
8 January 1979John Minton sworn in as interim president. Vice President John Minton was sworn in as WKU's interim president by Judge Charles Reynolds, succeeding Dero Downing and holding the post until Donald Zacharias took office that August. In the recordWKU Timeline: John Minton
18 January 1979ASG signs three lectures for the spring. The Associated Student Government signed three lectures for the spring semester, part of its ongoing role booking campus speakers. In the recordHerald 54:33, 18 Jan 1979
25 January 1979ASG could lose control of activities funding. The Associated Student Government faced losing control over student activities funding, the Herald reported, a direct threat to one of the government's core powers. In the recordHerald 54:35, 25 Jan 1979
25 January 1979ASG wants a student on a state council. In the same issue that reported the funding fight, the Associated Student Government pressed for a student seat on a state-level council, part of the broader campaign for student representation that ran through the decade. In the recordHerald 54:35, 25 Jan 1979
15 February 1979ASG establishes a Minorities Board. ASG established a Minorities Board, the Herald reported. The move followed the fall's push to add minority voices to the presidential screening process. In the recordHerald 54:41, 15 Feb 1979
27 March 1979Thornton and Craig win seats on Kentucky's student government council. The Herald reported two Western students, ASG president Steven Thornton and Terri Craig, elected to the executive council of the Student Government Association of Kentucky, a state-level student body - the kind of state seat ASG had pressed for in January. In the recordHerald 54:48, 27 Mar 1979
27 March 1979Thornton and Craig elected to SGAK executive council. Two Western students, Steve Thornton and Terri Craig, were elected to the Student Government Association of Kentucky executive council. The Herald also editorialized that ASG should make its teacher evaluation public. In the recordHerald 54:48, 27 Mar 1979
17 April 1979Voting held for Thornton's successor; United Black Students backs Hargrove. Students voted in the Associated Student Government presidential election, with the Herald running candidate endorsements the same day, including United Black Students' backing of Jamie Hargrove. In the recordHerald 54:55, 17 Apr 1979
17 April 1979Election day: candidates lean on experience. Students voted in the ASG general election, with the presidential candidates relying on their experience, the Herald reported. United Black Students backed Jamie Hargrove, and outgoing president Steve Thornton and former president Bob Moore published endorsements. In the recordHerald 54:55, 17 Apr 1979
19 April 1979Jamie Hargrove easily wins the presidency. The Herald reported that Jamie Hargrove easily won the Associated Student Government president race. The result closed an election season that had begun with 70 candidates signing up for offices. In the recordHerald 54:56, 19 Apr 1979
26 April 1979ASG approves resolutions on housing and parking policy. In one of the outgoing Thornton administration's final acts, the Associated Student Government approved resolutions addressing campus housing and parking policy. In the recordHerald 54:57, 26 Apr 1979

1979-80James Hargroave (president)

12 April 1979830 students vote in the ASG primary; the Herald runs a defence of not voting. The Associated Student Government's spring primary drew 830 voters and put the open-house policy on the ballot. The same issue carried a piece justifying student apathy in ASG voting - the paper had moved from scolding non-voters to explaining them. This primary elected the officers who took office for 1979-80; it was previously misfiled under 1978-79. In the recordHerald 54:54, 12 Apr 1979
August 1979Donald Zacharias sworn in as WKU's sixth president. Zacharias, previously executive assistant to the chancellor of the University of Texas system, took office as WKU's sixth president at the opening of the academic year; he was formally installed the following spring. In the recordWKU Timeline: Donald Zacharias
30 August 1979ASG head Jamie Hargrove profiled at year's start. The Herald profiled the Associated Student Government head under the headline that he believed students were interested, in the same issue that introduced the new president's wife, Tommie Zacharias, to campus. In the recordHerald 55:2, 30 Aug 1979
30 August 1979Hargrove opens the year saying students are interested. Associated Student Government head Jamie Hargrove told the Herald he believed students were interested in their government as the year opened. A week later ASG heard its 1979-80 budget and discussed changing its delegate policy. In the recordHerald 55:2, 30 Aug 1979
13 September 1979ASG weighs expanding hall representation. The Associated Student Government considered expanding residence hall representation in its congress, in the same issue reporting the Board of Regents set to consider a two-year budget request. In the recordHerald 55:5, 13 Sep 1979
20 September 1979Seats bill passes after revision under pressure. A bill on Associated Student Government seats passed after being revised under pressure, expanding on earlier talk of broader residence hall representation. The Herald called the representation bill a small step in the right direction. In the recordHerald 55:7, 20 Sep 1979
November 1979ASG rejects move to close Diddle Hall. The Associated Student Government rejected a move to close Diddle Hall dormitory. The vote came amid a fall of housing debates that later included a push to make Keen Hall a coed dorm. In the recordHerald 55:19, 1 Nov 1979
13 November 1979Resolution 79-10 seeks staff for scholarship administration. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 79-10, urging the university to assign staff to administer academic scholarships. In the recordSGA Resolution 79-10, Academic Scholarship Expansion
29 November 1979ASG proposes an activity fee for part-time students. ASG proposed a part-time student activity fee. The proposal came as the Board of Regents weighed budget requests for the coming biennium. In the recordHerald 55:25, 29 Nov 1979
21 February 1980ASG considers moving its spring elections. The Associated Student Government considered changing the date of its spring elections. The discussion took place against campus anger over a proposed tuition increase. In the recordHerald 55:40, 21 Feb 1980
17 April 1980Fuller and Irons win the presidential primary. Steve Fuller and Tim Irons emerged as victors in the ASG presidential primary, from a field of three that also included David Rue. Candidates had been certified earlier in the month. In the recordHerald 55:53, 17 Apr 1980
24 April 1980Steve Fuller elected ASG president. Steve Fuller, Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to the top Associated Student Government jobs. The Herald wrote that persistence had paid off in Fuller's campaign, while runner-up Tim Irons looked to the future after losing. In the recordHerald 55:55, 24 Apr 1980
May 1980New ASG officers and members sworn in. The new Associated Student Government officers and members were sworn in. ASG and the Interhall Council were also conducting student polls as the year closed. In the recordHerald 55:57, 1 May 1980

1980-81Steven Fuller (president)

3 April 1980ASG hopefuls debate the issues; ASG weighs opposing a UCB change. Associated Student Government presidential hopefuls discussed the issues and courted votes at a candidates' forum ahead of the spring election. The same issue reported ASG considering opposition to a proposed change to the University Center Board's structure. In the recordHerald 55:49, 3 Apr 1980
10 April 1980Three seek the ASG presidency. Steve Fuller, David Rue and Tim Irons entered the race for Associated Student Government president. In the recordHerald 55:51, 10 Apr 1980
24 April 1980Fuller elected ASG president. Steve Fuller won the Associated Student Government presidency over David Rue and Tim Irons. Mark Wilson and Greg Zoeller were elected to other top ASG offices the same day. In the recordHerald 55:55, 24 Apr 1980
4 September 1980ASG room inspection measure defeated amid criticism. A proposed ASG measure on dormitory room inspections was voted down, in a session a separate Herald article criticized for how the vote was conducted. The defeat opened a fall-long fight over dorm inspection policy. In the recordHerald 56:3, 4 Sep 1980
11 September 1980ASG bill targets pests in the dorms. ASG introduced a bill calling for a ban on bugs in residence halls; the Herald's editorial cartoon depicted a cockroach imperiled by the resolution. The paper's editorial page separately argued the university's protective inspection policy was unnecessary. In the recordHerald 56:5, 11 Sep 1980
30 October 1980ASG proposes a title change. The Associated Student Government proposed a title change for the organization. The proposal surfaced in the same week campus activities were limited for the national election day. In the recordHerald 56:19, 30 Oct 1980
13 November 1980ASG re-endorses dorm inspections after nearly missing the vote. ASG voted to re-endorse dormitory room inspections, in a session the Herald reported the government had nearly slept through. The same issue covered ASG's sponsorship of an international film and dance series and an attorney's interest in a dorm inspection case. In the recordHerald 56:22, 13 Nov 1980
20 November 1980ASG bill proposes a stricter room-entry rule. ASG introduced a bill proposing a stricter rule governing staff entry into student rooms, continuing the fall's running fight over dormitory inspections. In the recordHerald 56:24, 20 Nov 1980
5 February 1981ASG asks the state to evaluate higher education. ASG asked the state to evaluate higher education. The request came in a legislative season dominated by budget worries across Kentucky's universities. In the recordHerald 56:36, 5 Feb 1981
5 February 1981Associated Student Government asks the state to evaluate higher education. Robert Pillow reported that the Associated Student Government had called on the state to carry out an evaluation of higher education. The request appeared in an issue dominated by budget pressure, alongside coverage of controversy over cuts to the athletic budget. In the recordHerald 56:36, 5 Feb 1981
24 March 1981Resolution 80-32 asks for change machines in the dorms. ASG passed Resolution 80-32, requesting that change machines be installed in residence halls. In the recordSGA Resolution 80-32, Change Machines
2 April 1981Sturgeon and Bush win the ASG primary. David Sturgeon and Marcel Bush won the Associated Student Government primary, in a campaign the Herald said saw candidates playing big time politics. The same issue carried a resolution asking for a new ASG logo. In the recordHerald 56:50, 2 Apr 1981
9 April 1981Bush defeats Sturgeon for the presidency. David Sturgeon was defeated in the Associated Student Government race, leaving Marcel Bush the winner after endorsements had split between the two. The congress also voted to keep the present ASG logo. In the recordHerald 56:52, 9 Apr 1981
14 April 1981Close races prompt ASG recounts. Close races prompted recounts in the Associated Student Government election. The recounts came in the same week the Council on Higher Education approved a tuition increase. In the recordHerald 56:53, 14 Apr 1981
23 April 1981ASG changes its mind on changing minds. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government changed its mind on changing minds, capping a contentious election month. The same issue covered a withdrawn regent selection and the board's study of reorganizing the university. In the recordHerald 56:56, 23 Apr 1981

3 September 1981ASG announces its goals for the year. The Associated Student Government announced its goals for the coming year. 2 February 1982Five students seek the student regent seat. Five students sought the student regent spot in the first campus-wide election for the seat. The February 9 vote produced no majority, forcing a runoff the following week. In the recordHerald 57:36, 2 Feb 1982

22 April 1982Margaret Ragan wins the repeated election. Margaret Ragan won the ASG presidency in the repeated general election. The new officers were sworn in the following week. In the recordHerald 57:57, 22 Apr 1982

1982-83Sandra Norfleet (student regent) · Margaret Ragan (president)

28 January 1982ASG sets up a council to settle its own disputes. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had appointed a council to decide disputes inside the organization. The story ran two weeks after the same reporter, Kevin Francke, covered the resignation of ASG president Marcel Bush. In the recordHerald 57:35, 28 Jan 1982
11 February 1982ASG and the University Center Board both ask for more money. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government and the University Center Board both wanted larger budgets and planned to submit requests. Two weeks later the paper ran a piece arguing that the Center Board outshone ASG. In the recordHerald 57:39, 11 Feb 1982
16 February 1982Norfleet wins the student regent runoff. No candidate won a majority in the February 9 student regent primary, forcing a runoff. Sandra Norfleet won the runoff on February 16. In the recordHerald 57:41, 18 Feb 1982
April 1982ASG endorses William Natcher. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government had backed William Natcher. The same issue previewed the ASG presidential primary set for the following Tuesday, and five days later the paper editorialized that endorsing was not wise for ASG. In the recordHerald 57:51, 1 Apr 1982
8 April 1982Ragan and Sargent survive the ASG primary. Margaret Ragan and Glenn Sargent survived the Associated Student Government presidential primary, emerging from a five-way field. In the recordHerald 57:53, 8 Apr 1982
15 April 1982Norfleet's short regent term nears its end. The Herald noted that the student regent's two-month term was already nearing its end, a reminder of how short a stopgap the office had been. In the recordHerald 57:55, 15 Apr 1982
20 April 1982Ragan wins the presidency in a repeated election. The first general election was voided, and Margaret Ragan won the Associated Student Government presidency in the repeated election held April 20. She and the other new officers were sworn in before the month was out. In the recordHerald 57:57, 22 Apr 1982
26 August 1982Ragan opens the year promising major ASG changes. Monica Dias reported that major ASG changes were envisioned by Margaret Ragan. The story ran in the Herald's second issue of the fall semester and was the paper's first substantial account of her plans. In the recordHerald 58:2, 26 Aug 1982
2 September 1982ASG considers a Wall of Fame. Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government was considering a Wall of Fame. A week later the Herald followed with a report that the wall looked promising. In the recordHerald 58:4, 2 Sep 1982
18 November 1982ASG approves a coed housing bill. Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had approved a coed housing bill. The measure built through the fall: ASG and the Interhall Council polled students on coed housing in September, and ASG formally proposed it on 10 November. In the recordHerald 58:25, 18 Nov 1982
9 December 1982ASG breaks from the student legislature. Monica Dias reported that the Associated Student Government had broken from the student legislature. The break did not last, and by February 1984 the Herald was reporting that the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature might join ASG again. In the recordHerald 58:29, 9 Dec 1982
13 January 1983No quorum, so ASG does not meet. The Herald reported that the Associated Student Government failed to reach a quorum and did not meet. It was the first ASG item the paper carried after the winter break. In the recordHerald 58:32, 13 Jan 1983
3 February 1983ASG floats a shuttle service, and Ragan explains the split with the regent seat. The same issue that carried President Margaret Ragan's Herald piece explaining that the ASG presidency and student regent seat were now separate positions also reported ASG was considering a shuttle service, the proposal put to a student vote the following week. In the recordHerald 58:38, 3 Feb 1983
10 February 1983Grade plan passes; students vote for a shuttle. ASG passed a grade plan, and 206 students voted for a campus shuttle service. In the recordHerald 58:40, 10 Feb 1983
March 198324 elected to Senate. Twenty-four students were elected to the Associated Student Government Senate, the same issue reporting increased dormitory hours had been proposed. In the recordHerald 58:45, 1 Mar 1983
17 March 1983Constitution changes approved; filing opens. The Associated Student Government approved changes to its constitution, and ten students filed for offices ahead of the deadline. Dean Charles Keown publicly questioned the revisions the following week, as filings swelled to 68. In the recordHerald 58:47, 17 Mar 1983
7 April 1983500 vote in the ASG primary. About 500 students voted in the Associated Student Government primary. The Herald's letters pages carried a steady stream of endorsements for presidential candidate Jack Smith. In the recordHerald 58:53, 7 Apr 1983
14 April 1983Jack Smith wins the ASG presidency. Jack Smith won the presidency of the Associated Student Government, and students voted for the ASG constitutional revisions on the same ballot. The Herald had dared students to vote at all in a sardonic election day editorial. In the recordHerald 58:55, 14 Apr 1983
28 April 1983ASG endorses a $15 athletic fee. The outgoing congress endorsed a $15 athletic fee. The vote came as the Board of Regents turned its focus to the budget. In the recordHerald 58:59, 28 Apr 1983

1983-84Jack Smith (president)

12 April 1983ASG election day: candidates court votes for the top offices. The Herald urged students to the polls for the Associated Student Government election. Beyond the presidential contest, candidates for ASG's other top offices - including Bob Shults, Laura McClellan, Traci Turner, Kim Binkley and Allan Kujala - each drew endorsement letters in the paper; the Herald index does not specify which office each sought. In the recordHerald 58:54, 12 Apr 1983
23 August 1983Escort service returns; discount card floated. The Herald's opening issue reported that the student escort service would resume and that ASG might sponsor a discount card. Filing for freshman elections was set to begin September 19. In the recordHerald 59:1, 23 Aug 1983
30 August 1983Smith opens with a "year of action". Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government was planning for a year of action. The story ran in the third issue of the fall semester, a week after the Herald first reported that ASG might sponsor a discount card. In the recordHerald 59:3, 30 Aug 1983
September 1983Discount card plan draws fire. ASG voted to study the discount card after the Herald editorialized that the organization should govern, not market cards. A week later the paper reported ASG would offer members a commission on card sales, prompting letters calling the plan cheap shots and old tricks. In the recordHerald 59:4, 1 Sep 1983
8 September 1983ASG members to take a commission on discount cards. Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government would offer its members a commission on the discount cards. The same issue carried two critical columns aimed at ASG, Timi Flener's "Cheap Shots" and Connie Hoffman's "And Old Tricks." In the recordHerald 59:5, 8 Sep 1983
13 October 1983ASG asks for cable television in dorm rooms. Steve Paul reported that the Associated Student Government wanted cable in dormitory rooms. The same issue ran a Lou Bloss editorial cartoon on an ASG penalty and a letter from Carl Davis disagreeing with an ASG proposal. In the recordHerald 59:15, 13 Oct 1983
27 October 1983ASG passes incomplete-grade deadline proposal. The Associated Student Government passed its proposal on the deadline for incomplete grades, after tabling it the week before. The grade issue had occupied ASG since September. In the recordHerald 59:19, 27 Oct 1983
3 November 1983Budget falls short as the grade plan passes. Craig Dezern and Steve Paul reported that the ASG budget would not cover its planned projects. The same issue reported that ASG had approved its grade plan, the change to the grading scale that ran through most of the year. In the recordHerald 59:21, 3 Nov 1983
10 November 1983ASG takes up a university day-care center. Barry Rose reported that a university day-care center would be studied by the Associated Student Government. It joined study hall research and cable television among the service questions ASG picked up that fall. In the recordHerald 59:23, 10 Nov 1983
6 December 1983ASG voids its own procedures amid growth. The Herald reported that ASG voided its own procedures, while also noting growth in membership and a congress weighing 14 proposals. The editorial page mocked the body with a cartoon, and Jack Smith wrote in to say the cartoon aggravated him. In the recordHerald 59:27, 6 Dec 1983
12 January 1984Vice president William Chandler quits. Victoria Malmer reported that Associated Student Government vice president William Chandler had quit. Within a week the Herald reported that three people had been nominated for ASG positions. In the recordHerald 59:29, 12 Jan 1984
14 February 1984Student legislature may rejoin ASG. The Kentucky Student Legislature delegation was reported possibly rejoining the Associated Student Government. Letter writers sparred the same day over whether the ASG stereotype was deserved. In the recordHerald 59:38, 14 Feb 1984
23 February 1984The top ASG officers file for re-election. Mark Edelen reported that the top Associated Student Government officers were seeking re-election. The same issue reported that legislators were upset with ASG and that students were being asked to gripe, and it carried further responses to the alcohol poll plan. In the recordHerald 59:41, 23 Feb 1984
20 March 1984Top four ASG offices decided without runoffs. The top four Associated Student Government spots were decided, the Herald reported, as ASG emphasized representation. About 450 students had voted in the primary the week before. In the recordHerald 59:45, 20 Mar 1984
3 April 1984ASG polls students on beer and a campus pub. ASG began a student poll on the beer and campus pub issue on general election day. The Herald's editorial page argued the economics of the campus pub plan were faulty. In the recordHerald 59:49, 3 Apr 1984
10 April 1984Low turnout may force a beer poll revote. Low turnout threatened to spur a revote in the ASG beer poll. The same issue reported president Jack Smith impersonating a bunny for the season. In the recordHerald 59:51, 10 Apr 1984

1984-85Jack Smith (president)

20 September 1984Four proposals made reality in the third week of class. The Herald reported that four Associated Student Government proposals had already been carried out, and that the congress was beginning a study of a student book exchange. The exchange went on to become the running project of the year. In the recordHerald 60:7, 20 Sep 1984
27 September 1984The grade scale proposal is denied. ASG's proposal for a new grade scale was denied, one week after the congress's early run of successes. It was the first setback of the fall reported in the Herald's coverage. In the recordHerald 60:9, 27 Sep 1984
18 October 1984ASG wants less general education. The congress went on record wanting a reduction in general education requirements. It was an early instance of the body intervening in curriculum policy, three years before the fights over the General Education Task Force. In the recordHerald 60:15, 18 Oct 1984
8 November 1984LaMont Jones drops out of a revote. LaMont Jones withdrew from an ASG revote, and the same issue carried an editorial cartoon on the organization. A disputed election requiring a revote marked the low point of the fall semester. In the recordHerald 60:19, 8 Nov 1984
31 January 1985Education cuts loom and the book exchange stalls. ASG weighed a fight against state education cuts, while its book exchange venture looked likely to pause for the summer. Both stories ran in the same late-January issue. In the recordHerald 60:34, 31 Jan 1985
14 February 1985Apathy as an editorial cartoon. 'Voter Apathy Can be Solved' ran alongside a cartoon on election apathy and a report that a 24-hour open house was under discussion. In the recordHerald 60:38, 14 Feb 1985
28 February 1985Four file for congress president. A fourth candidate filed for ASG congress president and a debate was set, as the spring filing period opened. The same issue carried letters both applauding an ASG bill and requesting its support. In the recordHerald 60:42, 28 Feb 1985
28 March 1985McKinney and Watkins take the primary. Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins rode their experience to victory in the ASG primary. The congress also passed a resolution on grade point averages the same week. In the recordHerald 60:47, 28 Mar 1985
11 April 1985Jack Smith ends his term. The Herald marked the end of Jack Smith's presidency with a news story, an editorial crediting his enthusiasm with reviving interest in ASG, and an editorial cartoon. Mitchell McKinney had been elected the new president the week before. In the recordHerald 60:51, 11 Apr 1985

1985-86Mitchell McKinney (president)

14 February 1985An apathy editorial greets a 24-hour open house debate. The Herald ran an apathy editorial and cartoon aimed at student government alongside a report on debate over 24-hour open house policy in the dorms. In the recordHerald 60:38, 14 Feb 1985
21 March 1985Dueling op-eds spar over forcing a bill. The Herald ran a pair of opposing opinion pieces, both headlined "Associated Student Government Shouldn't Force Bill," one by future ASG president Mitchell McKinney and the other by Jamie Morton. In the recordHerald 60:45, 21 Mar 1985
28 March 1985McKinney and Watkins win the ASG primary. Mitchell McKinney and Chris Watkins won the Associated Student Government presidential primary over a field that included candidate Stan Reagan. In the recordHerald 60:47, 28 Mar 1985
4 April 1985McKinney elected president; a legislative group rejoins ASG. Mitchell McKinney was elected Associated Student Government president. The same issue reported that an unnamed legislative group had rejoined ASG. In the recordHerald 60:49, 4 Apr 1985
24 September 1985ASG abolishes its Finance Committee. The congress voted to abolish its own Finance Committee, a structural change later reversed in part when a Financial Advisory Council was written into the bylaws the following spring. In the recordSGA Bill 85-1-F, Abolishment of Finance Committee
12 October 1985ASG orders its own student discount card. The congress passed legislation calling for ASG to produce its own student discount card, one of several consumer-service ideas the group pursued that fall. In the recordSGA Bill 85-15-F, Production of Own Student Discount Card
31 October 1985A 20-vote margin and a GPA debate. About 20 votes separated the top two finishers in a fall ASG election, and the congress debated setting a grade-point average requirement for its own members. Both stories ran in the same late-October issue. In the recordHerald 61:19, 31 Oct 1985
5 November 1985Alcohol on campus studied again. ASG returned to the question of alcohol on campus, an issue that had already produced a student poll and a campus pub debate in 1984. The congress opened a new study of the policy. In the recordHerald 61:20, 5 Nov 1985
21 November 1985A shuttle to the mall. The congress discussed running a shuttle service from campus to the mall. It was one of several consumer-service ideas, alongside student discount cards, floated that fall. In the recordHerald 61:25, 21 Nov 1985
12 December 1985Lighting proposal defeated. Student government defeated a campus lighting proposal in the last week of the fall semester. It was one of the few outright defeats of legislation reported that year. In the recordHerald 61:30, 12 Dec 1985
23 January 1986Fall-break bill narrowly passes. A bill calling for a fall break narrowly passed ASG. The proposal drew an opposing editorial in the next issue calling the extra break impractical and not needed. In the recordHerald 61:35, 23 Jan 1986
30 January 1986No day off for Martin Luther King Day. ASG rejected a proposal to dismiss classes for the Martin Luther King holiday, one week after passing the fall-break bill. The King holiday question returned to the congress the following year. In the recordHerald 61:37, 30 Jan 1986
4 March 1986McKinney withdraws from re-election. Mitchell McKinney pulled out of the race for a second term as ASG president. The same issue carried a piece arguing that student government needed a strong leader. In the recordHerald 61:46, 4 Mar 1986
20 March 1986Library hours proposals, and elections delayed a week. ASG proposals asked for more library hours, and the spring elections were pushed back a week. The same issue carried dueling letters on whether the organization was in trouble. In the recordHerald 61:48, 20 Mar 1986
25 March 1986College representative seats created. The congress created major/minor college representative seats within its own membership. In the recordSGA Bill 86-19-S, Voting of Representatives for Colleges
April 1986ASG revises its membership application. The congress adopted a revised application process for SGA membership. In the recordSGA Bill 86-21-S, Adoption of New Application
April 1986ASG asks regents to attend a meeting. The congress asked that Board of Regents members attend and speak at one SGA meeting during their term. In the recordSGA Bill 86-22-S, Attendance of Regents at Meetings
April 1986ASG seeks chains for Pearce-Ford Tower windows. The congress asked for chains to be placed on Pearce-Ford Tower windows so they could be opened. In the recordSGA Bill 86-26-S, Placing of Chain on Windows
2 April 1986Financial Advisory Council written into the bylaws. The congress incorporated the Financial Advisory Council into the ASG bylaws, months after abolishing its own Finance Committee. In the recordSGA Bill 86-3-S, Incorporation of Councils into By-Laws
3 April 1986Outgoing congress commends President McKinney. The outgoing congress passed a bill commending the work of SGA president Mitchell McKinney as his term ended. In the recordSGA Bill 86-13-S, Commendation of President
10 April 1986Pranks and accusations mar the races. The Herald reported that pranks and accusations had marred the ASG races, and printed the election results in the same issue. Tim Todd emerged from the field as the new president. In the recordHerald 61:54, 10 Apr 1986
15 April 1986ASG pushes for a campus welcome sign. The congress pushed for a welcome sign to be placed at the intersection of Normal Drive and University Boulevard. In the recordSGA Bill 86-36-S, Placing of Welcome Sign on Campus
15 April 1986ASG commends outgoing President Minton. The congress passed a bill commending outgoing WKU president John D. Minton for his service to the university. In the recordSGA Bill 86-39-S, Commendation of Dr. John D. Minton
8 August 1986Regents honor McKinney at term's end. The WKU Board of Regents included a resolution honoring outgoing ASG president Mitchell McKinney, alongside honors for Georgia Bates and outgoing WKU president John Minton, at its August meeting - held the same day Kern Alexander was named the university's new president. In the recordBoard of Regents minutes, 8 Aug 1986

1986-87Timothy Todd (president)

4 August 1986Twenty years of amendments consolidated into one document. The constitution of the WKU Associated Students with amendments - the only surviving snapshot of how the 1966 framework had been patched over two decades. A Judicial Council roster for 1986-87 survives alongside it. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Constitution
11 September 1986A $12,100 budget and a retreat with the university president. ASG approved a $12,100 budget, planned a phone outreach effort to hear students' ideas and needs, and announced a retreat featuring university president Kern Alexander. All three stories ran in the second week of the fall semester. In the recordHerald 62:5, 11 Sep 1986
18 September 1986A minor change in voting. ASG sought a minor change in its voting procedures early in the fall term. It was the first structural tinkering of the Todd presidency. In the recordHerald 62:7, 18 Sep 1986
5 March 1987Rules suspended, bills passed. The congress suspended its rules to pass a batch of bills in a single meeting. The rush came as the spring filing period for elections was opening. In the recordHerald 62:45, 5 Mar 1987
19 March 1987Martin Luther King bill splits the congress. A Martin Luther King bill passed the congress with members split by the argument, a year after ASG had rejected dismissing classes for the holiday. The same issue reported that Tim Todd and Greg Elder would battle again for the presidency. In the recordHerald 62:46, 19 Mar 1987
2 April 1987Attendance drops after the speeches. The Herald reported that ASG attendance fell off once campaign speeches had been heard. An accompanying piece warned voters that talk was cheap in the presidential race. In the recordHerald 62:50, 2 Apr 1987
9 April 1987An amendment dies of low member turnout. A constitutional amendment was defeated because too few members turned up to vote on it. The failure came in the same week as the presidential election. In the recordHerald 62:52, 9 Apr 1987
14 April 1987The Herald calls the race for Elder; the index calls it no contest. On election day the Herald endorsed challenger Greg Elder as the better choice to lead ASG, ran a letter calling the organization impotent, and headlined the race itself as no contest. The indexed issues that survive do not record the published result; the SGA plaque carries Todd through 1988 on a two-year plate. In the recordHerald 62:53, 14 Apr 1987

1987-88Timothy Todd (president)

1987Not enough candidates to fill the ballot. ASG races faced a candidate shortage; one report notes a candidate entered a race to help a rival rather than to win. The same issue has ASG tabling a phone bill after amendment. In the recordHerald 62:48, 1987
10 September 1987Dropping the intercollegiate legislature considered. ASG considered dropping its membership in the intercollegiate legislature, while the Herald warned that sharing an officer with Interhall Council could mean trouble for both groups. An editorial the following week argued the Kentucky Intercollegiate State Legislature was worth keeping as a way to promote ideas. In the recordHerald 63:5, 10 Sep 1987
October 1987Crosswalk resolution passes. The congress passed a resolution calling for a crosswalk. Campus safety items, including new screens for dormitory windows, filled much of the fall agenda. In the recordHerald 63:11, 1 Oct 1987
27 October 1987Getting tough on absenteeism. ASG moved to get tough on absenteeism after a member lost his seat the week before. The Herald was simultaneously reporting that apathy was killing both ASG and the Residence Hall Association. In the recordHerald 63:18, 27 Oct 1987
10 November 1987Constitutional amendments up for a vote. Constitutional amendments went before the body in November, in the same season the congress was pushing for required teacher evaluations. It was the third straight year of structural revision attempts. In the recordHerald 63:22, 10 Nov 1987
23 February 1988ASG explains its empty seats. The organization publicly cited its reasons for the vacancies in its ranks, and four congress positions had been filled at a single meeting earlier that month. Days later an editorial told the body it needed better ideas, not gimmicks. In the recordHerald 63:42, 23 Feb 1988
31 March 1988Ragland and Whitehouse win the primaries. Shannon Ragland and Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential primaries, narrowing a field of seven. The same issue reported passage of a proposal requesting a memorial area on campus. In the recordHerald 63:50, 31 Mar 1988
7 April 1988Whitehouse elected; condom machines approved. Scott Whitehouse won the ASG presidential election, in an issue that also reported the congress approving condom machines for campus. The election coverage ran alongside editorials saying oversight and closed minds had marred the process. In the recordHerald 63:52, 7 Apr 1988
14 April 1988Bruce Cambron calls for a new election. Bruce Cambron called for a new election a week after the results, following coverage of votes cast for a write-in candidate that ASG was told it could not ignore. The dispute carried into the following fall. In the recordHerald 63:54, 14 Apr 1988
