ASG filed a written response to a proposed overhaul of general education requirements - one of the earliest surviving examples of student government intervening in curriculum rather than campus life. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports/11
15 September 1988Write-in campaigns banned. ASG approved a ban on future write-in campaigns, five months after write-in votes had thrown its own presidential election into dispute. An editorial the next issue said the block showed ASG was not listening. In the recordHerald 64:7, 15 Sep 1988
29 September 1988Freshman election turnout called pretty good. Turnout in the ASG freshman election was reported as "pretty good." The same issue said the organization was working to make the importance of voting register with students. In the recordHerald 64:11, 29 Sep 1988
6 October 1988Cambron takes his election complaint to the president. Bruce Cambron, who had called for a new election in April, talked to university president Thomas Meredith about the ASG election. The spring's disputed result was still alive six months on. In the recordHerald 64:13, 6 Oct 1988
3 November 1988Half the open slots filled; shelters for shuttle stops. ASG filled half of its open congress seats and sought shelters and seats for campus shuttle stops. The following week the Herald editorialized that ASG's efforts directly helped and served students. In the recordHerald 64:21, 3 Nov 1988
12 December 1988The weeklong Thanksgiving break is dropped. ASG dropped its push for a weeklong Thanksgiving break, three weeks after voting to seek one. In the same issue, members rated their own organization as average. In the recordHerald 64:28, 12 Dec 1988
16 February 1989An extra study day recommended. ASG recommended adding an extra study day before exams. The proposal followed January efforts to find a way to print teacher evaluations. In the recordHerald 64:39, 16 Feb 1989
2 March 1989More movie hours wanted. The congress asked for more movie hours on campus. It was one of the quality-of-life items that filled the spring agenda before election season. In the recordHerald 64:43, 2 Mar 1989
13 April 1989Amos Gott edges Lynn Groemling. Amos Gott narrowly defeated Lynn Groemling in the ASG presidential race. The campaign season had drawn complaints from candidates about the brief primary and an editorial warning that name recognition should not decide the race. In the recordHerald 64:49, 13 Apr 1989

1990-91Michael Colvin (president)

19 April 1990Michael Colvin elected Associated Student Government president. Colvin won the Associated Student Government's presidential election, the Herald reported under the headline "Michael Colvin Aces Associated Student Government Election." In the recordHerald 65:55, 19 Apr 1990
19 April 1990ASG pushed for a higher student activity fee. The same Herald issue that reported Colvin's election win reported the Associated Student Government was seeking an increase to the student activity fee. In the recordHerald 65:55, 19 Apr 1990, "Associated Student Government Wants Activity Fee Raised"
30 May 1990Regents set the 1990-91 tuition and operating budget. WKU's Board of Regents met in special session and approved the university's 1990-91 operating budget, tuition rates, and personnel changes ahead of Colvin's term. In the recordWKU Board of Regents, special meeting, 30 May 1990
23 August 1990Colvin wants to make ideas reality. The Herald introduced Michael Colvin as the new ASG leader who wanted to make ideas reality. The profile opened the organization's year in the second issue of the fall. In the recordHerald 66:2, 23 Aug 1990
September 1990ASG bill proposes an organizational presidents roundtable. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #90-2-F, proposing a roundtable of student organization presidents. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #90-2-F, "Organizational Presidents Roundtable"
September 1990ASG bill would put microwaves in cafeterias. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #90-4-F, requesting that microwaves be placed in campus cafeterias. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #90-4-F, "Microwaves"
13 September 1990Glasgow's student body budget cut. ASG cut the budget of the WKU Glasgow associated student body. The move came a year after the main campus organization had helped Glasgow change its constitution. In the recordHerald 66:7, 13 Sep 1990
29 November 1990ASG passes resolution for left-handed desks. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 90-10-F, requesting that a left-handed desk be provided in each classroom. The Herald reported the vote in its 29 November 1990 issue, alongside news that a companion resolution on excused absences had been killed the same week. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 90-10-F, "Left Handed Desks"
29 November 1990ASG kills resolution on earthquake-prediction absences. The Associated Student Government killed Resolution 90-12-F, which had asked that student absences tied to Iben Browning's widely publicized forecast of a major New Madrid Fault earthquake be excused. Browning had predicted the quake for on or near 3 December 1990; it prompted regional anxiety and some school closures, but no earthquake occurred. The Herald reported the resolution's defeat in its 29 November 1990 issue. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 90-12-F, "Excused Absences for Earthquake Prediction"
29 November 1990Left-handed desks pushed; excused absences killed. ASG pushed for left-handed desks in classrooms and killed a resolution on excused absences in the same stretch of meetings. The two items closed out the fall legislative calendar. In the recordHerald 66:27, 29 Nov 1990
1991ASG votes to join the Hilltopper Athletic Foundation. The Associated Student Government passed Bill #91-3-S, providing for ASG membership in the Hilltopper Athletic Foundation. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-3-S, "ASG to Join Hilltopper Athletic Foundation"
1991ASG overhauls its by-laws, including veto-override procedure. In the spring term the Associated Student Government passed a cluster of by-law bills: Bill #91-4-S suspended the by-laws to allow a vote on a pending matter, Bill #91-5-S amended the by-laws on how resolutions could be submitted, and Bill #91-6-S changed the by-laws on overriding a presidential veto. The new override procedure was tested weeks later when the Senate's emergency-kit resolution survived a veto on 14 March 1991. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-6-S, "By-Laws"
1991ASG resolves to improve Detrex Field. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-7-S, requesting improvements to Detrex Field, the campus intramural field. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 91-7-S, "Intramural Field"
1991ASG bill would recognize presidential scholars in the Herald. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-7-S, a bill separate from the same-numbered resolution on Detrex Field, proposing that WKU's presidential scholars be recognized in the College Heights Herald. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-7-S, "Presidential Scholar Recognition"
1991ASG bill proposes a book exchange board in Grise Hall. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-9-S, proposing a book exchange bulletin board be placed in Grise Hall. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-9-S, "Book Exchanger Bill"
10 January 1991Survey backs a dead week. An ASG survey supported creating a dead week before finals. The same issue carried an opinion piece headlined that Colvin failed on final examinations. In the recordHerald 66:31, 10 Jan 1991
15 January 1991ASG raised concern over an insurance change. The Herald reported that a change in insurance practice was "upsetting" the Associated Student Government; the archive does not preserve further detail of what the change was or how ASG responded. In the recordHerald 66:32, 15 Jan 1991, "Insurance Trend Upsets Associated Student Government"
15 January 1991Students held a campus vigil as the Gulf War approached. The same Herald issue covered a campus prayer vigil for peace as the U.N. deadline for Iraq's withdrawal from Kuwait neared, two days before the United States led a coalition into the Gulf War. In the recordHerald 66:32, 15 Jan 1991, "Students Pray for Peace"
17 January 1991Two officers step down. Amos Gott and Van Hodge stepped down as ASG officers, and the remaining officers clashed over comprehensive exams in the same issue's coverage. Two weeks later Karl Miller was picked as public relations vice president. In the recordHerald 66:33, 17 Jan 1991
7 February 1991ASG looked at a four-day class week. The Associated Student Government considered the idea of moving to a four-day class week, the Herald reported. In the recordHerald 66:39, 7 Feb 1991, "Associated Student Government Looks at Having Four-Day Class Week"
12 February 1991Tuition caps, Detrex, and financial aid. In a single February issue, ASG wanted to cap tuition increases, proposed an overhaul of Detrex registration, and planned lobbying to protect financial aid. It was the broadest policy week of the Colvin year. In the recordHerald 66:40, 12 Feb 1991
14 March 1991Emergency kit resolution survives a veto. A resolution on emergency kits survived a veto and stood as passed. It was the only veto fight reported in the Herald index that year. In the recordHerald 66:49, 14 Mar 1991
11 April 1991Heather Falmlen wins amid protests. Heather Falmlen won the ASG presidency amid election protests, with a group urging students to boycott the vote and an editorial condemning immature antics in the campaign. The results issue reported three races as clear-cut. In the recordHerald 66:54, 11 Apr 1991

1991-92Heather E. Falmlen (president)

2 April 1991Herald previews four ASG candidates. The Herald's "Meet the Candidates" feature previewed four contenders in the spring Associated Student Government elections: Heather Falmlen, Rob Evans, Van Hodge, and Dan Knowles. Falmlen went on to win the race. In the recordHerald 66:51, 2 Apr 1991, "Meet the Candidates"
11 April 1991Heather Falmlen wins the ASG presidency amid election protests. Falmlen won the Associated Student Government presidential election in results the Herald reported under the headline "Heather Falmlen Wins Amid Associated Student Government Election Protests." The same issue covered a rival group's call to boycott the election, an editorial calling the contest "immature antics," and a complaint that the Herald's own coverage had been biased. In the recordHerald 66:54, 11 Apr 1991
22 May 1991University newsletter confirms Falmlen holds both offices. WKU's own "On Campus" newsletter reported Heather Falmlen as both Student Regent and Associated Student Government President, a contemporaneous confirmation that the two offices - separately elected two decades earlier - were held by the same person entering her term. In the recordOn Campus 1:7, 22 May 1991, "Heather Falmlen is Student Regent, Associated Student Government President"
September 1991ASG asks for a change in Big Red Shuttle fares. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-2-F, sponsored by the Student Affairs committee, requesting a one-way fare option on the Big Red Shuttle for infrequent riders. The resolution's text called the existing $10 fee "outrageous and unfair" to students and faculty who did not ride the shuttle daily. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 91-2-F, "Modified Shuttle Fare"
September 1991ASG resolves to support Meredith's contract renewal. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-7-F, backing the renewal of President Thomas Meredith's contract by the Board of Regents. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 91-7-F, "Student Picket to Support President Meredith"
September 1991ASG bill funds a "President for a Day" fundraiser. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-09-F, providing for a "President for a Day" fundraiser. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-09-F, "President for a Day"
September 1991ASG bill funds renovation of its own chambers. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-03-F, providing for the renovation of the ASG chambers. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-03-F, "ASG Chambers Improvement"
September 1991ASG bill proposes changing its own slogan. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #91-11-F, proposing to change the organization's slogan, in the same fall that it voted to rename itself from the Associated Students to the Student Government Association. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #91-11-F, "Change ASG Slogan"
5 September 1991Health tops the agenda; more money for the environment. Heather Falmlen opened the year with a student health issue at the top of her agenda, and ASG budgeted more money for environmental efforts. Both stories ran in the first week of the fall semester. In the recordHerald 67:3, 5 Sep 1991
12 September 1991Fighting the city's noise ordinance. ASG resolved to fight Bowling Green's noise ordinance. It was the organization's most direct engagement with city government in years. In the recordHerald 67:5, 12 Sep 1991
24 September 1991Officers go to the city's meeting. ASG officers attended a city meeting to press the noise ordinance fight, and the organization restarted its voter registration drive. A recycling resolution had its first reading the week before. In the recordHerald 67:8, 24 Sep 1991
15 October 1991Fall ASG senate and freshman elections held. The Herald covered the Associated Student Government's fall elections on 10 October, and a separate freshman senator election on 15 October; the paper's abstracts do not preserve the results. In the recordHerald 67:13, 10 Oct 1991, "Associated Student Government Elections Tuesday"
29 October 1991ASG asks that Iracane not be re-elected regents chair. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 91-6-F, authored by Mark Miller and Eric McWilliams and sponsored by Mistianna Holcomb, asking that Joe Iracane not be re-elected chair of the Board of Regents. The resolution's text stated that Iracane, chairman for eight consecutive years, was under investigation by the FBI, the IRS and U.S. attorneys in Indiana and Kentucky over an alleged $6 million payment to Pyramid Mining Co. in return for contracts and a separate alleged $14,500 payment to the company for a consulting contract; it also accused him of overstepping into day-to-day university operations reserved for the president under the Board's bylaws. The resolution asked student regent Heather Falmlen to vote against him. No source found reports the investigation's outcome. The same day's Herald covered the vote under "Associated Student Government Opposes Joseph Iracane." In the recordSGA Resolution 91-6-F, "Board of Regents Chair Term Limit"
31 October 1991ASG asks the regents to elect a new leader. ASG urged the Board of Regents to elect a new leader in place of chairman Joseph Iracane, two days after the Herald reported the organization's opposition to him. It was a rare direct challenge to the university's governing board. In the recordHerald 67:19, 31 Oct 1991
6 November 1991Regents re-elect Iracane despite ASG's resolution. A week after the Associated Student Government asked the Board of Regents not to re-elect Joe Iracane as chair, the board did so anyway. The university's own newsletter reported the result under "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents." In the recordOn Campus 1:16, 6 Nov 1991, "Joe Iracane Re-elected to Chair Regents"
12 December 1991A mailing asks parents to back the health service. The Residence Hall Association and ASG sent a joint mailing asking parents to support the campus health service. It closed out the health-focused fall Falmlen had promised in August. In the recordHerald 67:29, 12 Dec 1991
28 January 1992ASG introduces a bill for a student regent advisory committee. The Associated Student Government introduced Bill #92-01-S, authored by Greg Butler, Mistianna Holcomb, Melony Jones and Melissa Maggard and sponsored by the Public Relations committee, proposing a Student Advisory Committee - made up of the class presidents, a representative from each college and the executive council as ex-officio members - to brief the student regent on Board of Regents agenda items and canvass student opinion before each meeting, two days before the Herald reported the plan. In the recordSGA Legislation, Bill #92-01-S, "Development of Advisory Committee for Student Regent"
30 January 1992ASG plans a committee on student access to the regent. The Herald reported the Associated Student Government was planning a committee aimed at securing student access to WKU's regent, amid a statewide debate over how regents were selected. In the recordHerald 67:34, 30 Jan 1992, "Associated Student Government Plans Regent Committee"
30 January 1992Editorial cartoon targets Falmlen. The same Herald issue ran an editorial cartoon, "Ventriloquist's Dummy" by Patrick Richardson, with Falmlen as its subject. In the recordHerald 67:34, 30 Jan 1992, "Editorial Cartoon Heather Falmlen Ventriloquist's Dummy"
2 April 1992ASG resolves to support football despite budget cuts. The Associated Student Government passed Resolution 92-7-S, declaring its support for the WKU football program in spite of budget cuts. The resolution's own text argued the university had already awarded 67 football scholarships it would be contractually bound to honor even if the program were suspended, calling a suspension that still paid non-playing scholarship athletes an unnecessary expense. This entry corrects the resolution's date: an earlier record in this archive gave 4 February 1992, but the resolution itself is dated introduced 2 April 1992, shortly before the Board of Regents' 1 May vote to keep the program. In the recordSGA Legislation, Resolution 92-7-S, "Support of Football Program"
7 April 1992Associated Students votes to become the Student Government Association. The body voted to rename itself on 7 April and students ratified the change in a referendum on 14 April. It took effect that autumn. In the recordWKU SGA history
7 April 1992The primary is canceled. The ASG primary election was canceled, with too few candidates to require one, and a parking bill sat in committee the same week. The general election went ahead the following Tuesday. In the recordHerald 67:50, 7 Apr 1992
16 April 1992Joe Rains wins big as 1,200 turn out. Joe Rains won the presidential election by a wide margin, with about 1,200 students casting votes. The same ballot carried the constitutional amendments students had voted on two days earlier, including the name change. In the recordHerald 67:53, 16 Apr 1992
21 April 1992Rains to oversee the change to SGA. The Herald reported that incoming president Joe Rains would oversee the transition from the Associated Student Government to the Student Government Association. Student reaction to the spring's parking bill was reported as varied in the same issue. In the recordHerald 67:54, 21 Apr 1992
May 1992Board of Regents votes to keep football. The Board of Regents voted to keep the football program, following months of budget pressure that had prompted the ASG's February resolution of support. In the recordHerald, 1 May 1992, "Board of Regents Votes to Keep Football"

1992-93Joe Rains (president)

9 April 1992Herald previews the race and the rename referendum. The Herald previewed the Associated Student Government presidential race under "Mistianna Holcomb, Joe Rains Vying for Presidency," profiled candidate Susan Mitchell under "Susan Mitchell Has a Fresh Perspective," and reported that students would soon vote on a referendum to rename the Associated Student Government the Student Government Association. No source found confirms what office Mitchell sought or whether she won it. In the recordHerald 67:51, 9 Apr 1992
14 April 1992Joe Rains elected SGA president as the ASG-to-SGA renaming took effect. Rains won a contested Associated Student Government presidential election covered by the Herald under the headline "Associated Student Government Needs Joe Rains," alongside a rival editorial cartoon depicting him as Darth Vader and profile pieces on candidates Mark Miller, Mistianna Holcomb and Melony Jones. The same ballot carried the referendum renaming Associated Students as the Student Government Association. In the recordHerald 67:52, 14 Apr 1992
14 April 1992Turnout worries and candidate profiles filled the ballot issue. The same issue that reported Rains' win ran the Herald's concern piece "Many Students Won't Vote" alongside profile pieces on the other candidates: "Mark Miller's Involvement Makes Him a Leader," "Mistianna Holcomb Takes a Stand for Students," and "Melony Jones Loved & Respected by Peers." In the recordHerald 67:52, 14 Apr 1992
21 April 1992Rains takes office with a rename to carry out. The Herald reported that incoming president Joe Rains would oversee the change from Associated Student Government to Student Government Association, which students had ratified by referendum the week before. The new name took effect that fall, making Rains the first president to serve under it. In the recordHerald 67:54, 21 Apr 1992
25 August 1992Fall opened with a new logo and discount cards. At its first meeting of the fall on August 25, 1992, the student government discussed a new logo, student discount cards, a voter registration drive and committee assignments. The group was still transitioning from the Associated Student Government name to SGA, and its minutes from this year appear under both titles. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 25 Aug 1992
3 September 1992The renamed SGA elects its representatives. In its first weeks under the new name, the Student Government Association held elections for its representatives. The Herald covered the vote at the start of the fall semester. In the recordHerald 68:4, 3 Sep 1992
6 October 1992Support gathers for a rally. The Herald's index for this issue records the new SGA winning support for a campus rally that October, under the headline "Student Government Association Gets Support for Rally." In the recordHerald 68:12, 6 Oct 1992
13 October 1992Resolution asked WKU to spare academics from budget cuts. Resolution 92-7-F asked the university to exempt academic units from a round of proposed budget cuts. State funding pressure ran through the whole fall; the same weeks produced repeated plans for a student rally in Frankfort. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 92-7-F, 13 Oct 1992
13 October 1992President Meredith addressed the student congress. WKU President Thomas Meredith came to the October 13 meeting to talk about computers, laundry facilities, cable television, lighting and Potter Hall. The same minutes record discussion of budget cuts, homecoming elections, a newsletter and joint forums with the Residence Hall Association. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 13 Oct 1992
20 October 1992Congress honored the Lady Toppers. Resolution 92-8-F honored the WKU women's basketball team for its runner-up finish in the NCAA tournament. It was one of a string of numbered resolutions the congress produced that fall on subjects from drop-add fees to parking. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 92-8-F, 20 Oct 1992
19 November 1992An invitation to get involved. An opinion piece by Paul Weathers urged students to get involved in the Student Government Association, part of the Herald's running commentary on the body during its first semester under the new name. In the recordHerald 68:23, 19 Nov 1992
December 1992Just Ask Joe radio program and Project Western. The December 1 minutes record plans for a Just Ask Joe call-in radio program, the Project Western campus cleanup, a President for a Day event, recycling bins and student health insurance. The meeting closed out a semester dominated by tuition and budget worries. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 1 Dec 1992
10 December 1992Rains pushed SGA to back a student escort service. SGA president Joe Rains argued the organization should support a campus student escort service, the Herald reported. In the recordHerald 68:27, 10 Dec 1992
11 December 1992University Senate honored Rains for a Frankfort budget-cut rally. The WKU University Senate adopted Resolution R92.11, commending SGA president Joe Rains for taking part in a rally at the state capitol in Frankfort asking the legislature to stop cuts to higher-education funding. TopSCHOLAR records the resolution's history running from 11 December 1992 to its adoption on 29 January 1993. In the recordWKU University Senate, Resolution R92.11
2 February 1993Meredith returned to pitch Potter Hall as a student service center. President Thomas Meredith addressed the February 2 meeting about campus laundry, cable television and turning Potter Hall into a student service center. Members also discussed tuition increases, resignations and general education requirements. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 2 Feb 1993
13 April 1993Spring closed with elections and Earth Day plans. The April 13 meeting took up the budget, spring elections, the annual banquet, a one-card ID system, smoking policy, Adopt-a-Spot and Earth Day. It was the last full meeting recorded in the digitised minutes for the year. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 13 Apr 1993
22 April 1993Donald Smith rolls to victory. The Herald called the spring election with the headline "Student Government Association Election: Donald Smith Rolls to Victory." Smith would succeed Rains for the 1993-94 term. In the recordHerald 68:54, 22 Apr 1993

7 September 1993A new constitution came up first. Bill 93-1-F, introduced at the second meeting of the fall, proposed amendments to the SGA constitution. Constitutional revision stayed on the agenda through October, alongside the tuition rally the congress was planning. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-1-F, 7 Sep 1993Read it here
16 September 1993Congress changes approved. The SGA approved changes to its congress in September while freshmen debated for open positions. The Herald covered both in a single mid-September issue. In the recordHerald 69:7, 16 Sep 1993
12 October 1993Congress planned a tuition rally. The October 12 meeting discussed a tuition rally, the budget, the Plus System and parking. November 1993At least seventeen numbered resolutions in one semester. Resolutions 93-4-F through 93-20-F survive in the correspondence files - the fullest single-semester record in the collection, and the best available answer to how much a WKU student senate actually passes in a working term. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports
9 November 1993Bill funded emergency phones on campus. Bill 93-6-F proposed purchasing and installing emergency telephones on campus. The Herald was still reporting on SGA's security phones the following February, and campus lighting and safety stayed on the agenda into the spring. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-6-F, 9 Nov 1993Read it here
30 November 1993Memorial trees for students who die while enrolled. Bill 93-12-F proposed planting memorial trees in tribute to students who die while enrolled at WKU. It capped a heavy late-November run of legislation that also included child care grants for non-traditional students, a book exchange and opening the Downing University Center computer lab during finals. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 93-12-F, 30 Nov 1993Read it here
14 December 1993Executive Council pressed the administration on holiday housing. The SGA Executive Council, acting on Resolution 93-18-F, wrote to administrators Katherine Tolbert, Dave Parrott, John Osborne and Ann Stathos asking the university to address housing for students during holiday breaks. In the recordSGA Records: Correspondence - Resolution 93-18-F, 14 Dec 1993Read it here
1994SGA wrote guidelines for its public forums. The association adopted written guidelines governing how it would run student public forums, formalizing a process that had previously run ad hoc. In the recordSGA Records: Guidelines for SGA Public Forums, Jan 1994Read it here
8 February 1994Let's work together for change. The Herald ran an opinion piece under the heading "Let's Work Together for Change" and put the question of how SGA could reach more students to its People Poll. The paper also ran a Stacy Curtis editorial cartoon offering a "recipe for better representation." In the recordHerald 69:35, 8 Feb 1994
17 February 1994President for a Day swapped a student into Meredith's office. The Herald reported that student Angelo Rodriguez would switch places with President Thomas Meredith through SGA's President for a Day program. The same issue covered SGA's security phones on campus and a proposal to let students retake C grades that was killed in committee. In the recordHerald 69:37, 17 Feb 1994
3 March 1994A resolution on class attendance. An SGA resolution covered by the Herald would have let students skip class, reported under the headline "Attendance: Student Government Association Resolution Would Let Students Skip Class." In the recordHerald 69:41, 3 Mar 1994
8 March 1994A $3 fee to support the Big Red Card. Resolution 94-4-S proposed a three dollar student fee to support the Big Red Card program. The card system and its fees ran through the minutes for the rest of the spring. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 94-4-S, 8 Mar 1994Read it here
29 March 1994Willard's resignation reached the floor. The March 29 meeting took up the resignation of basketball coach Ralph Willard along with the Big Red Card fee, teacher evaluations, emergency telephones, campus lighting and the coming elections. Dialogue Day and Adopt-a-Spot rounded out a crowded agenda. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 29 Mar 1994Read it here
14 April 1994A disputed primary. The Herald reported that presidential candidate Scott Sivley had not followed SGA and university procedures during the election, in the same issue that carried the tallied results of the primary. The episode ran alongside the paper's get-out-the-vote editorial coverage. In the recordHerald 69:50, 14 Apr 1994
21 April 1994Evans and Higdon ready to lead. The Herald closed the election season with "Rob Evans & Tara Higdon Ready to Lead Students." The same issue carried letters both defending the organization and, from future president Kristen Miller, a piece headlined "Student Government Association Defends Itself." In the recordHerald 69:52, 21 Apr 1994
28 April 1994A year-end banquet, and corners cut on the budget. The Herald closed the year with two SGA stories: the year-end banquet recognizing award winners and officers, and a report that the association was cutting corners with its budget. In the recordHerald 69:54, 28 Apr 1994

1994-95Robert Evans (president)

19 April 1994Evans defeats Sivley for the SGA presidency. Rob Evans faced Scott Sivley at the polls on election day; the Herald reported the same day that Sivley had been warned by SGA for violating the organization's campaign policies. Evans and running mate Tara Higdon won. In the recordHerald 69:52 [51], 19 Apr 1994, "Student Government Association Elections: Scott Sivley vs. Rob Evans at Polls Today"
19 April 1994Campus assesses storm damage. The Herald reported that WKU's campus suffered less damage than the surrounding city after a tornado, the same week as the SGA election. In the recordHerald 69:52 [51], 19 Apr 1994, "Storm; Campus Suffered Less Damage than City"
August 1994Fall 1994 membership roster filed. SGA filed its list of representatives for the fall 1994 semester, part of the organization's routine paperwork under the Evans administration. In the recordSGA Records: Membership List Fall 1994Read it here
15 August 1994Evans sworn in as student regent. The Board of Regents' quarterly meeting swore in Robert Evans, Joy Gramling and Cornelius Martin, and carried resolutions of appreciation for outgoing officers Donald Smith - the previous SGA president and student regent - and Monnie Hankins. In the recordWKU Board of Regents, quarterly meeting, 15 Aug 1994
8 September 1994The 1994-95 budget passes. The SGA approved its budget for the year in early September, reported by the Herald under "Student Government Association Approves Budget for 1994-95." In the recordHerald 70:5, 8 Sep 1994
November 1994Expanded shuttle service draws attention. The Herald reported that expanded Big Red Shuttle bus service, a route the Student Government Association had pushed to extend, was drawing enthusiasm from local stores along its new stops. In the recordHerald 70:19, 1 Nov 1994
November 1994An editorial defends the memorial trees. The same issue carried the opinion piece "Don't Destroy Trees," addressing the fate of the memorial trees the SGA had established the previous year to honor students who died while enrolled. In the recordHerald 70:19, 1 Nov 1994
November 1994Resolution asks for grades before the "W" deadline. SGA passed Resolution 94-11-F, asking that students be given a grade before the end of the withdrawal ("W") period so they could make an informed decision about dropping a class. In the recordSGA Resolution 94-11-F, Examination Prior to end of "W" PeriodRead it here
8 November 1994Bill seeks an SGA listing in the phone book. SGA introduced Bill 94-8-F, asking that a Student Government Association directory section be added to the university's telephone book. In the recordSGA Bill 94-8-F, Student Telephone DirectoryRead it here
24 January 1995Security phone tops SGA's spring to-do list. The Herald reported a new security phone, a shuttle stop, and the memorial trees on the Student Government Association's agenda, under "New Security Phone, Shuttle Stop, Trees Lead to Student Government's To Do List." The same issue reported a mystery caller had been scaring students with stalking and harassment, the incident that would shape the spring campaign two months later. In the recordHerald 70:32, 24 Jan 1995, "New Security Phone, Shuttle Stop, Trees Lead to Student Government's To Do List"
28 February 1995SGA discusses escort service, campus cleanup. SGA's regular meeting took up the student escort service, a "President for a Day" promotion, a campus cleanup, and open positions on the body. In the recordSGA Meeting Minutes, 28 Feb 1995Read it here
11 April 1995Campus security shapes the spring campaign. The Herald reported that being stalked had influenced candidate Tara Higdon, putting campus security at the center of the spring election coverage. In the recordHerald 70:51, 11 Apr 1995
20 April 1995Tara Higdon moved up as turnout moved down. The Herald reported the spring election under the headline 'Tara Higdon Moves Up; Voting Down,' recording both the choice of the next president and a drop in voter participation. The election closed out the 1994-95 administration. In the recordHerald 70:54, 20 Apr 1995
25 April 1995The Herald called visibility the key to SGA's success. As the year ended, the Herald ran an editorial package on the association, pairing a Stacy Curtis cartoon of student government in a glass box with the editorial 'Visibility Key to Student Government Association Success.' It was a summing-up of a year in which the paper pressed SGA to be seen doing its work. In the recordHerald 70:55, 25 Apr 1995
27 April 1995A new beginning. The Herald's transition piece, "Tara Higdon Sees New Beginning," marked the handover from Robert Evans to his elected successor at the end of the academic year. In the recordHerald 70:56, 27 Apr 1995

1995-96Tara (Higdon) Howard (president)

22 August 1995Two more emergency phones. The year opened with a security win. The Herald reported that SGA had put two more emergency phones on campus, continuing the safety agenda that had shaped the previous spring's election. In the recordHerald 71:1, 22 Aug 1995
7 September 1995A dress code, and a call for interest. September coverage included an SGA dress code and a piece headlined "Tara Higdon Seeks Student Interest in Group," as the new president worked to draw students into the organization. In the recordHerald 71:5, 7 Sep 1995
2 November 1995Presidential pay compared. The Herald reported that pay for student government presidents was higher at other schools, an early airing of a compensation question that would recur in later decades. In the recordHerald 71:20, 2 Nov 1995
23 January 1996A student credited SGA for its trees. A Herald opinion piece ran under the headline 'Student Government Association Doing Good Job with Trees,' crediting the association's campus planting work. Trees and campus grounds were among the group's most visible projects that year. In the recordHerald 71:32, 23 Jan 1996
8 February 1996A skywalk at the bottom of the Hill. SGA proposed a skywalk at the bottom of the Hill, and the Herald also reported the organization bringing emergency phones to campus in the same issue. The skywalk would quickly draw editorial fire. In the recordHerald 71:37, 8 Feb 1996
8 February 1996SGA proposed a skywalk at the bottom of the Hill. The Herald reported SGA's proposal for a pedestrian skywalk at the bottom of the Hill, and the same issue covered its push to bring emergency phones to campus. The skywalk became the most argued-about SGA idea of the spring. In the recordHerald 71:37, 8 Feb 1996
13 February 1996The Herald pushes back. Five days after the skywalk proposal, the Herald told SGA to "ditch the pie-in-the-sky idea," and its letters page carried Richard Malek's charge that the organization acted as a "puppet" group. Another letter defended officers Horace Johnson and Kristen Miller against the label "hair-brained." In the recordHerald 71:38, 13 Feb 1996
13 February 1996The skywalk drew fire within a week. Five days after the proposal, the Herald ran a column telling SGA to 'ditch' the 'pie-in-the-sky' skywalk idea, and a letter in the same issue called the association a 'puppet' group. The episode set the combative tone of the spring semester. In the recordHerald 71:38, 13 Feb 1996
5 March 1996A new store on campus. SGA proposed a new store on campus, reported by the Herald in early March as the organization kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring. In the recordHerald 71:44, 5 Mar 1996
5 March 1996A campus store proposal followed. SGA proposed a new store on campus, the Herald reported, as the association kept generating campus improvement ideas through the spring. A week earlier the paper had covered its wish to see the next university president promoted from within. In the recordHerald 71:44, 5 Mar 1996
14 March 1996Longer visitation hours. SGA asked the university for longer residence hall visitation hours, one of the quality-of-life requests that defined the organization's agenda that spring. In the recordHerald 71:47, 14 Mar 1996
28 March 1996Four candidates ran for the top office. The Herald reported that four students were running for SGA president. The campaign filled the opinion pages for the next three weeks, with endorsements, a debate and a proposed slate of constitutional amendments on the ballot. In the recordHerald 71:48, 28 Mar 1996
9 April 1996A test-free week before finals. SGA proposed a test-free week before finals, one of the last legislative pushes of the year. The idea ran in the Herald alongside Board of Regents coverage of fee increases. In the recordHerald 71:51, 9 Apr 1996
16 April 1996Debate, amendments and endorsements filled election week. The Herald covered the presidential debate under the headline 'Debate Reflects Attitudes,' while letters urged a yes vote on SGA's constitutional amendments. Outgoing officer Tara Higdon's letter backing Kristen Miller ran on the same pages. In the recordHerald 71:53, 16 Apr 1996
25 April 1996New officers sworn in as a columnist shrugged. The Herald reported the swearing-in of SGA's new officers for 1996-97. A column in the same issue, 'Students Just Don't Care About Student Government Association,' summed up the year's running argument about relevance. In the recordHerald 71:56, 25 Apr 1996

1996-97Kristen Miller (president)

18 April 1996Few turn out for the election that chose Miller. The same Herald issue that declared "It's Kristen Miller's Time" also ran the headline "Few Turn Out for Election," continuing the decade's pattern of falling voter participation in SGA races. In the recordHerald 71:54, 18 Apr 1996
20 August 1996A retreat opens the year. The Herald reported that an SGA retreat provided the opportunity for new discussion and legislation, setting the agenda for Kristen Miller's term before classes had fully begun. In the recordHerald 72:1, 20 Aug 1996
27 August 1996Officers sworn in at the first fall meeting. The August 27 meeting swore in officers and took up the retreat, an open house, the budget and homecoming. It opened the first full year of minutes in the digitised record since 1994. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 27 Aug 1996
29 August 1996A plan to drive party-goers home. The Herald reported "Kristen Miller Makes Plan to Drive Party-Goers Home," the earliest indexed coverage of the safe-ride idea that became Provide-A-Ride. The same issue reported SGA giving more money to campus clubs. In the recordHerald 72:4, 29 Aug 1996
17 September 1996SGA created a Technology Committee. The September 17 meeting created the SGA Technology Committee and discussed intramural facilities, photocopiers in dorms and Campus Clean Up. Student email accounts and other technology questions recur in the fall's minutes. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 17 Sep 1996
24 September 1996Roller blades, skateboards, and a technology push. A September 24 meeting took up campus rules on roller blading and skateboards alongside Provide-A-Ride, a voter registration drive, a bonfire, Big Red Roar, the budget, and student email accounts. In the recordSGA Meeting Minutes, 24 Sep 1996
10 October 1996More lights proposed, and a veto recorded. The Herald reported SGA proposing more campus lighting while a resolution was vetoed. Campus lighting had been a steady SGA cause since the earlier emergency phones push. In the recordHerald 72:15, 10 Oct 1996
24 October 1996Thirty years of student government. The Herald's Homecoming edition carried Kim Leonard's feature "Student Government Association Has Grown in 30 Years," marking three decades since the Associated Students' founding in 1966. In the recordHerald Homecoming edition, 24 Oct 1996
14 November 1996Extending the shuttle route. SGA pushed to have the campus shuttle route extended, reported by the Herald in mid-November. In the recordHerald 72:24, 14 Nov 1996
21 January 1997Website, vacancies, and bylaws open the spring. The January 21 meeting discussed the organization's website, Provide-A-Ride, open vacancies on the body, the budget, and the by-laws, as the congress organized itself for the spring semester. In the recordSGA Meeting Minutes, 21 Jan 1997
28 January 1997Provide-A-Ride needs support. The Herald reported that Provide-A-Ride needed SGA and student support to survive its first year. The service would outlast the doubts and still be running as a free weekend van service years later. In the recordHerald 72:32, 28 Jan 1997
4 March 1997A seat at the presidential search. Resolution 97-4-S addressed the Presidential Search Committee as WKU sought a successor to Thomas Meredith, and Bill 97-3-S contributed to the WKU Senior Class Campaign the same day. The search ended with the hiring of Gary Ransdell later that year. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
25 March 1997SGA followed the presidential search. With Thomas Meredith's departure looming, the March 25 meeting discussed the university's presidential search along with an Orientation, Admissions and Registration Pal program, the Bridging the Gap forum and Campus Clean Up. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 25 Mar 1997
8 April 1997Candidates prepare, and fire alarms get a deadline. The Herald covered candidates preparing for the spring elections alongside an SGA effort seeking faster shut-off times for fire alarms, a snapshot of the organization's mix of politics and practical fixes. In the recordHerald 72:49, 8 Apr 1997
15 April 1997Reaching beyond campus. In one April session the body passed Resolution 97-13-S to reactivate the Kentucky Students Association and Resolution 97-14-S to establish a student representative position on the Council for Postsecondary Education, pushing WKU student interests into state-level policy. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
17 April 1997An anti-discrimination stand passed by a slim margin. The Herald reported that SGA passed a measure calling for gays to be included in Western's anti-discrimination policy by a slim margin, a week after covering the proposal's introduction. A letter in the same issue congratulated both SGA and the paper. In the recordHerald 72:52, 17 Apr 1997
22 April 1997The year closed with a memorial tree dedication. The last recorded meeting of the year discussed the memorial tree dedication, elections, Earth Day, Thomas Meredith, Campus Clean Up, off-campus housing scholarships and a residence hall privatization study. In the recordSGA Records: Meeting Minutes, 22 Apr 1997

1997-98Keith Coffman (president)

24 April 1997Keith Coffman took charge. The Herald announced the new administration with 'Keith Coffman Takes Charge,' and a companion piece reported the new president mapping his upcoming term. His term began as the spring semester closed. In the recordHerald 72:54, 24 Apr 1997
10 September 1997More student seats at the games. SGA secretary Jamie Fite wrote to interim president Barbara Burch requesting additional student seating in Diddle Arena and Smith Stadium. The letter survives in the SGA records collection. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/14
23 September 1997The ten-point scale fight begins. Resolution 97-6-F called for reinstatement of the ten-point grade scale, and Resolution 97-5-F addressed charitable organizations and solicitation of funds the same evening. The grading fight would run on for years at WKU. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
7 October 1997A career fair for summer jobs. Bill 97-1-F funded a Summer Job and Internship Career Fair, the first bill of the fall session under Keith Coffman. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
22 October 1997A crosswalk on Dogwood Drive. One of a run of outgoing letters in these years covering student seating at athletic events, ice machines in residence halls, campus safety, professors posting office hours, food court hours, housing scholarships for off-campus students and student health services. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Documents/Reports
4 November 1997Designated driver cards. Bill 97-3-F funded designated driver cards, extending the safe-ride agenda begun under Kristen Miller into a second year. The same week brought a bill to buy typewriters for the library. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
4 November 1997Paper towels for the Downing University Center. Resolution 97-9-F asked that paper towels be placed in the restrooms of the Downing University Center. It is one of only two pieces of legislation from the year in the digitised SGA collection. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 97-9-F, 4 Nov 1997
11 November 1997A November flood of resolutions. Between November 2 and 18 the congress passed at least fifteen numbered resolutions, covering a speed hump for the Regents Avenue lot, fifteen-minute parking spaces, working ID scanners, new sidewalks at Thompson and Grise, ice machines, soap and sanitary restrooms in residence halls, picnic tables, bicycle racks and recognition for honors graduates. It is one of the densest legislative months in the surviving 1990s record. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1997 (archived 2003)
18 November 1997Picnic tables for the bottom of campus. Resolution 97-23-F requested picnic tables for the campus area near Zacharias Hall, Meredith Hall and Pearce-Ford Tower. Its numbering shows the congress had produced at least 23 fall resolutions by mid-November. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 97-23-F, 18 Nov 1997
4 March 1998Housing stipends for off-campus students. Jamie Fite wrote to Academic Affairs Vice President Barbara Burch about applying housing stipends to off-campus housing, following up resolutions on the subject passed in both 1997 sessions. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/17
7 April 1998Coffman gets high marks as candidates line up. The Herald ran "Keith Coffman Served Students Well" alongside a People Poll asking students what they thought of his job performance, in the same issue that reported candidates preparing for the spring election. In the recordHerald 73:47, 7 Apr 1998
21 April 1998Spring bills: watch signs and a teaching award. The spring session's surviving record includes Bill 98-4-S for Neighborhood Watch signs on April 19 and Bill 98-5-S creating an Excellence in Teaching Award on April 21. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1998 (archived 2004)
22 April 1998A push for action on stalled legislation. As the term closed, secretary Jamie Fite wrote to Provost Barbara Burch requesting action on several pieces of legislation, pressing the administration to answer what the congress had passed. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/21
28 April 1998A $15,000 electronic sign and a campaign for scholarships. In election week the Herald polled students on how they would spend $15,000 of SGA's money, ran a column arguing the money for a big electronic message sign could be better used, and printed dueling letters on whether the association served students. Its campaign coverage reported that candidate Stephanie Cosby wanted more scholarships. In the recordHerald 73:52, 28 Apr 1998
30 April 1998Stephanie Cosby rolled to a huge victory. The Herald reported 'Stephanie Cosby Rolls to Huge Victory' in the SGA election that closed the year, alongside a story on how taxing election day was for officer candidates. Cosby would lead the association in 1998-99. In the recordHerald 73:53, 30 Apr 1998

1998-99Stephanie Cosby (president)

19 September 1998Dues to the state association. The treasurer of the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents wrote to president Stephanie Cosby requesting payment of the 1998-99 dues, evidence of WKU's continuing seat at the state student leadership table. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/19
29 September 1998Dorm sprinklers and an advisor checklist. The Herald reported SGA wanted sprinklers added in the dorms, while Bill 98-1-F created a checklist of questions for students to ask their advisors. Days earlier the paper had counted the association's legislative efforts trailing the previous year, and a letter in this issue accused it of wasting time and money. In the recordHerald 74:10, 29 Sep 1998
30 September 1998Relief funds for Murray State. Bill 98-2-F allocated funds to the Murray State University Fire Relief Fund after the fatal Hester Hall dormitory fire that September, one of the rare occasions the body directed money off campus. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1998 (archived 2004)
6 October 1998SGA asked for a wider University Boulevard. Resolution 98-7-F requested that University Boulevard be widened and that a traffic island be added for pedestrians. The Herald reported the following week that the University Boulevard proposal had failed, but the advising checklist was approved and grew into a run of advising-reform legislation through the fall. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 98-7-F, 6 Oct 1998Read it here
20 October 1998A coffee house for Pride Week and a Homecoming float. In a single October session the congress passed Bill 98-5-F funding a coffee house for Pride Week and Bill 98-6-F funding a joint SGA and Hillraiser Homecoming float. The fall slate also included a W.O.W. conference, ashtrays outside residence halls and an SGA survey. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1998 (archived 2004)
27 October 1998The SGA president was crowned homecoming queen. The Herald reported 'Stephanie Cosby Named Queen of Hill' at homecoming. SGA had its own stake in the festivities that fall, funding a joint homecoming float with the Hillraisers. In the recordHerald 74:17, 27 Oct 1998
10 November 1998An anonymous complaint about the room. An anonymous congress member wrote to the Executive Council about the tone and mood of SGA meetings. Mitchell Bailey issued a written response a week later, and both documents survive in the SGA records collection. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/28
17 November 1998A bill to help the burned-out Kappa Alphas. Bill 98-10-F proposed allocating funds to the Kappa Alpha fraternity after its house burned. The proposal set off the sharpest fight of the fall. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 98-10-F, 17 Nov 1998Read it here
December 1998Betting on Bookswap.com. Bill 98-12-F had SGA sponsor Bookswap.com, an early attempt to use the web against textbook prices, and Bill 98-13-F funded the 1999 Camp Fair the next day to close the fall session. In the recordWKU SGA legislation archive, 1998 (archived 2004)
8 December 1998The Kappa Alpha aid vote failed, loudly. The Herald reported some SGA members were upset after the group voted down aid to the fraternity, and a companion letter said SGA had 'abandoned' the Kappa Alphas. Letters defending and attacking the decision ran for the rest of the semester. In the recordHerald 74:27, 8 Dec 1998
10 December 1998Answering the charge of doing nothing. Vice president Matthew Bastin circulated a memo of the fall's passed legislation to the SGA advisor, officers, committee heads and the Herald's editor, answering accusations that SGA had been unproductive. The list itself was the rebuttal. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/24
15 April 1999Turbulent elections declared complete. The Herald reported the spring elections finished under the headline 'Turbulent Elections Complete,' while an opinion piece charged that SGA offered no leadership and a letter questioned the probe of candidate Will Jones. The turbulence was not over. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999
20 April 1999The Judicial Council overturned the election. The Herald reported that SGA's Judicial Council overturned the spring election, with coverage centering on candidate Joe Matheis, an editorial cartoon on nasty campaigns, and an opinion piece describing a 'swath of scandal' around the elections. In the recordHerald 74:52, 20 Apr 1999
22 April 1999A final rush of legislation amid the election mess. Two days later the Herald reported SGA passing a final rush of legislation, while the election fallout continued in the letters column and a story urged students to vote again on Monday. The same issue introduced the incoming president as a self-described workaholic. In the recordHerald 74:53, 22 Apr 1999
23 April 1999Concerns about student health services. Vice president Matthew Bastin wrote to president Gary Ransdell expressing SGA's concerns about student health services, closing the year by taking a student welfare issue to the top of the administration. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - SGA Documents/Reports/29

1999-00Amanda Lich (president)

8 April 1999Jones and Coates square off amid a pizza-party dispute. The Herald's pre-election issue covered the presidential race between Will Jones and Amanda Coates, alongside a report that SGA was questioning an election-eve pizza party Jones had held, a debate over eliminating the rule requiring a year of SGA experience to run for office, and a heated treasurer's race between Ryan Morrison and Joe Matheis. In the recordHerald 74:49, 8 Apr 1999
15 April 1999A turbulent election puts Amanda Coates in office. The Herald's coverage of the spring SGA election was headlined "Turbulent Elections Complete"; the same issue carried an opinion piece, "Student Government Association Offers No Leadership," challenging the incoming administration to prove itself. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here
15 April 1999Recount narrows Coates and Martin's win to three votes. Amanda Coates and running mate Cassie Martin initially led Will Jones and Kara Yeckering 616-611 for president and vice president; after the Coates-Martin ticket asked for a recount to be sure of the win, the recount that night found an even closer margin, 614-611. A write-in ticket of Dwight Campbell and Kerri Richardson finished third with 145 votes. Total turnout was 1,436 students. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here
15 April 1999Matheis survives a flier scandal to win vice president of finance. Joe Matheis defeated Ryan Morrison 700-688 for vice president of finance in the campaign's most contentious race. Two hours after the initial result, SGA's judicial council placed the race under review after fliers Matheis had distributed turned up left on classroom desks and in computer labs overnight, violating election code; the council warned Matheis could lose the seat if he had not made a good-faith effort to collect them. The council let the result stand the next day, and Morrison filed a complaint with the judicial council disputing that decision, saying fliers were still on desks in Garrett and the fine arts center. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here
15 April 1999Griffey and Bastin win the remaining executive seats. Brandon Griffey defeated Amanda Kirby 729-652 for vice president of administration, and Matt Bastin defeated Duan Wright 806-570 for vice president of public relations, completing the 1999-2000 executive slate. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here
15 April 1999A letter to the editor questions an SGA probe of racially charged campaign fliers. A Herald letter to the editor reported that fliers reading "Vote for Will Jones in Racism," written in black ink, had circulated in dorms during the campaign, and that SGA opened an investigation into whether they were racially motivated. The letter's author named Jones - described as the first Black candidate for SGA president in years - as a suspect despite his denial of any involvement, and questioned whether the investigation was following proper procedure rather than targeting him by assumption. No source found reports how, or whether, the investigation was resolved. In the recordHerald 74:51, 15 Apr 1999Read it here
15 September 1999Bill proposes an SGA Information Technology Director. SGA considered Bill 99-10-F, creating a new SGA position of Information Technology Director. In the recordSGA Bill 99-10-F, Information Technology Director
15 September 1999SGA created an Information Technology Director. Bill 99-10-F created the SGA position of Information Technology Director, and the same month produced a bill amending the constitution to include website guidelines. The association was formalising its web presence as the decade closed. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-10-F, 15 Sep 1999
28 September 1999A senior awards banquet and hall of distinguished seniors. Bill 99-5-F established a senior awards banquet and a hall of distinguished seniors, with a companion bill creating an ad hoc committee to run the event. A Meet Your Dean reception bill passed through the same September meetings. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-5-F, 28 Sep 1999
12 October 1999Students vote for R&B acts. SGA ran a student vote on Rhythm & Blues concert programming for campus, reported by the Herald under "Students Vote for R&B." In the recordHerald 75:13, 12 Oct 1999
26 October 1999Congress asked WKU to keep Jerry Wilder. Resolution 99-1-F requested that Jerry Wilder remain vice president of Student Affairs. The Herald reported the following week that SGA members opposed the move in Student Affairs. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-1-F, 26 Oct 1999
2 November 1999Topline, a toll-free campus activity line. Resolution 99-4-F proposed creating a toll-free activity phone line called Topline. The same weeks produced resolutions on WKU banners and suggestion boxes in residence halls. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-4-F, 2 Nov 1999
4 November 1999Members took the Student Affairs fight public. The Herald reported that Student Government Association members opposed the administrative move in Student Affairs. The story followed the congress's resolution asking that Vice President Jerry Wilder be retained. In the recordHerald 75:20, 4 Nov 1999
11 November 1999SGA endorsed ending Flip Friday. A fall resolution endorsed the schedule proposed by the Class Schedule Review Committee to do away with Flip Friday. It was the association's formal word on one of the era's odder scheduling experiments. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 99-F, 11 Nov 1999
18 November 1999Keep our voice: a rally at Wetherby. About fifty students gathered outside the Wetherby Administration Building to urge the university to retain both the Vice President of Student Affairs and the Dean of Student Life positions, chanting "It's not your choice. Keep our voice." The SGA's own account said president Ransdell appreciated how the students conducted themselves and would keep an open mind. In the recordWKU SGA site, V.P. of Student Affairs Update (archived 2000)
30 November 1999VarsityBooks.com came to the SGA website. Bill 99-17-F had SGA join VarsityBooks.com and post a link from its website, and a same-day bill extended library hours during finals week. The dot-com partnership marked the first e-commerce deal in the digitised SGA record. In the recordSGA Records: Bill 99-17-F, 30 Nov 1999
2000Provide-A-Ride in full operation. During this year SGA ran Provide-A-Ride as a free service giving safe and sober rides anywhere in the Bowling Green and campus area on Thursday and Friday nights from 11 p.m. to 2 a.m. A fifteen-passenger blue van answered calls within about fifteen minutes, and all a rider needed was a valid Western ID. In the recordWKU SGA site, Provide-A-Ride (archived 2000)
22 February 2000The faculty evaluations campaign opens. President Amanda Coates opened a campaign to publish faculty evaluations as a tool for students choosing professors, starting with a February 22 meeting with the university president and the Faculty Senate chair. The SGA published a step-by-step timeline running through a March 23 presentation to the full Faculty Senate, saying it did not want to win the tool at the expense of unnecessarily upsetting faculty. In the recordWKU SGA site, Faculty Evaluations (archived 2000)
28 March 2000Martin and Wright battle to succeed Coates. The Herald reported that Cassie Martin and Duan Wright were competing to succeed Amanda Coates as SGA president in the spring election. In the recordHerald 75:47, 28 Mar 2000
4 April 2000Resolution 00-2-S: publish the evaluations. Resolution 00-2-S, authored by Amanda J. Coates and Adam Howard and sponsored by the Legislative Research Committee, asked the Faculty Senate to approve a mandatory SGA-sponsored faculty evaluation to be published beginning in fall 2000. Its attached questionnaire asked practical questions such as whether an instructor takes attendance, offers extra credit or gives comprehensive finals. In the recordWKU SGA site, Resolution 00-2-S (archived 2000)
4 April 2000SGA proposed its own faculty evaluations. Resolution 00-2-S proposed creating an SGA faculty evaluation to help students select courses, reviving an idea the congress had pushed since the mid-1990s. It is the last piece of spring 2000 legislation in the digitised collection. In the recordSGA Records: Resolution 00-2-S, 4 Apr 2000
11 April 2000Two tickets make their case to succeed Coates. In the campaign's final week the Herald covered both tickets on the ballot to succeed Coates: Duan Wright with running mate Dwight Campbell, and Cassie Martin with running mate Leslie Bedo, each laying out a platform on the SGA's current issues. In the recordHerald 75:51, 11 Apr 2000
18 April 2000Martin elected; faculty evaluations move forward. As Coates's term ended, the Herald's post-election coverage reported Cassie Martin had won the SGA presidency, running an opinion piece titled "Cassie Martin Must Stand Up on Tough Issues," and separately confirmed the SGA-sponsored faculty evaluations Coates's administration had pushed would be conducted and published starting that fall. In the recordHerald 75:53, 18 Apr 2000

2000-01Cassie Martin (president)

17 February 2000SGA proposed election code rewrite to close loopholes. The Herald reported on new Student Government Association election codes intended to close loopholes in how campaigns were run, ahead of the spring 2000 officer elections that Cassie Martin and Leslie Bedo would go on to win. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:39, 17 Feb 2000
2 March 2000Insurance dispute put SGA "on edge". The Herald ran a story headlined "Insurance Puts Student Government Association on Edge," in the same issue that covered the ongoing debate over the association's new election codes. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:43, 2 Mar 2000
2 March 2000Election-code debate turned to fairness and spending limits. The Herald reported that SGA's proposed election codes were meant to ensure fairness between candidates and set campaign spending limits, continuing coverage begun two weeks earlier of loopholes in the existing rules. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:43, 2 Mar 2000
28 March 2000Martin and Wright set to battle for SGA presidency. The Herald reported that Cassie Martin and Duan Wright would face off for the SGA presidency in the coming spring election, the first coverage of what became the Martin-Bedo versus Wright-Campbell race. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:47, 28 Mar 2000
13 April 2000Martin and Wright discussed the issues on the eve of the vote. The day before the election, the Herald ran a piece by Rex Hall in which presidential candidates Cassie Martin and Duan Wright discussed the issues facing the campaign. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:52, 13 Apr 2000
14 April 2000Martin-Bedo ticket won SGA presidency. Students elected Cassie Martin, a junior from Glasgow, as SGA president for 2000-2001, a post that also made her the student representative on Western's Board of Regents. Her ticket with vice presidential candidate Leslie Bedo defeated Duan Wright and Dwight Campbell by 654 votes to 541 in the Thursday election. In the only other contested race, Amy Caswell defeated Billy Lyons 706 to 461 for finance vice president, while Adam Howard and Leslie McClard ran unopposed for the administration and public relations vice presidencies. In the recordWKU news release, 14 Apr 2000 (archived)
18 April 2000SGA planned to conduct and publish faculty evaluations. The Herald reported that SGA planned to conduct student evaluations of faculty and publish the results starting in fall 2000, in the same issue that covered the close of the Martin-Bedo campaign. The same issue carried an editorial titled "Cassie Martin Must Stand Up on Tough Issues," urging the incoming president to take firmer positions once in office. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:53, 18 Apr 2000
20 April 2000Herald reported SGA membership still declining. The Herald ran a story headlined "Student Government Association Membership Still Declining," tracking a drop in participation as the Martin administration prepared to take office. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 75:54, 20 Apr 2000
29 August 2000SGA Congress opened its fall 2000 session. SGA's congress held its first meeting of the fall semester on Tuesday, August 29 at 5 p.m. in Downing University Center room 305. The body met every Tuesday during the semester, and the organization invited students to pick up membership applications in the SGA office on the first floor of DUC. In the recordWKU SGA site, archived 2 Sep 2000
27 October 2000Regents raised athletics fee over Martin's dissent. The Board of Regents voted 8-2 to raise the $16 student athletic fee by $40 in January 2001 and another $40 in fall 2001, to fund a Diddle Arena renovation, a larger football budget for WKU's move to the Gateway Conference, and the athletic department's budget shortfall. Student Regent Cassie Martin and Faculty Regent Mary Ellen Miller cast the two votes against. Martin said she understood the need for the funding but questioned the timing and the amount, and disagreed with raising student fees in the middle of an academic year. In the recordWKU news release, 27 Oct 2000 (archived)
9 March 2001WKU took student health service back in-house. WKU announced it would return to self-operation of its campus student health service after its contractor, Collegiate Health Care, notified employees it would be out of business at the end of the day. The university hired the clinic's 17 employees on a temporary basis through the end of the spring semester, and the vice president for Student Affairs promised students would see no reduction in health services. In the recordWKU news release, 9 Mar 2001 (archived)
13 May 2001Bedo ticket stood unopposed to succeed Martin. SGA's candidate page for the 2001 officer elections listed a single ticket for the top job: executive vice president Leslie Bedo for president with Jamie Sears as her running mate. The only race with two names was for vice president of public relations, between Mark Rawlings and Holly Skidmore, while Aaron Spencer and Jamil Sewell stood alone for the finance and administration vice presidencies. The date shown is the Internet Archive capture date; the page itself carried no date and no results or turnout figures were found in allowed sources. In the recordWKU SGA site, archived 13 May 2001

2001-02Leslie Bedo (president)

18 August 2001Bedo questions timing of 9 percent tuition increase, then votes for it. WKU's Board of Regents voted on Friday, August 17 to raise tuition 9 percent starting in fall 2002, the first tuition hike in university history devoted entirely to faculty and staff pay. Student Regent Leslie Bedo said she was troubled that the vote came before students officially began fall classes, telling the board it sent a message that the university would slide the increase through before students could respond. Despite her concerns, Bedo joined the unanimous vote approving the increase, which raised in-state undergraduate tuition $138 a semester, from $1,422 to $1,560. In the recordDaily News, 18 Aug 2001
7 September 2001Regents approve $32.5 million Diddle Arena bond deal funded by student athletics fee. The Board of Regents approved an agreement with the City of Bowling Green to sell up to $32.5 million in bonds to renovate E.A. Diddle Arena, with the university repaying the debt service through its student athletics fee. Planned improvements included air conditioning, new seating, luxury boxes, expanded parking and a pedway from new parking areas to the arena. The renovation was scheduled to run from April to September 2002. In the recordWKU News, 7 Sep 2001
13 September 2001Students organize candlelight vigil after September 11 attacks. Two days after the September 11 attacks, WKU held a student-organized candlelight vigil at the Ivan Wilson Fine Arts Center Amphitheater as part of a slate of campus responses. The university also planned a faculty forum at Van Meter Auditorium, opened the Faculty House for reflection and counseling, created a condolences message board to send to New York and Washington, and scheduled a blood drive for September 27. In the recordWKU News, 13 Sep 2001
6 November 2001SGA raises over $800 for Red Cross disaster relief. The SGA homepage, as archived on November 6, 2001, reported that the association had helped raise more than $800 for the Red Cross Disaster Relief Fund following the September 11 attacks. The same page announced that Congress applications were available in DUC 130 and promoted the Campus Spirit Award, which SGA administered that year. In the recordSGA site, archived 6 Nov 2001
9 November 2001Provide-A-Ride carries 929 passengers over twelve fall nights. SGA's Provide-A-Ride service posted its fall 2001 ridership on its website, listing twelve Thursday and Friday nights of operation between September 20 and November 9, 2001. Nightly passenger counts ranged from 49 to 112, for a total of 929 riders over the period. In the recordSGA site, archived 27 Nov 2001
27 November 2001Fall project slate: online syllabi, extended library hours, alcohol policy. SGA's current-projects page, as archived on November 27, 2001, listed the association's work for the semester. Projects included online course syllabi, extended library hours during finals week, a review of the alcohol policy, a 9/11 Remembrance Wall, the SGA Disaster Relief Fund, Provide-A-Ride keychains, the Senior Class Challenge, the Campus Spirit Award, Homecoming Queen 2001 and the Homecoming parade. In the recordSGA site, archived 27 Nov 2001
29 November 2001SGA organized Christmas presents for Potter Children's Home. The Herald reported that SGA was collecting Christmas presents that fall for children at Potter Children's Home, a Bowling Green residential care facility, in a news piece by staff writer Hollan Holm. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 77:27, 29 Nov 2001
29 November 2001President Bedo and senator Ransdell publicly debated SGA's effectiveness. The same Herald issue ran dueling opinion pieces on SGA: an op-ed by President Leslie Bedo headlined "Meeting Goals of Student Government Association, But Not Students'", followed by a response from fellow member Troy Ransdell titled "Action, Not Complaints." The full text of the exchange is not available online; only the headlines and bylines are indexed. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 77:27, 29 Nov 2001
2002SGA constitution amended, Spring 2002. TopSCHOLAR's SGA collection holds a copy of the WKU Student Government Association constitution described as "amended Spring 2002," indicating the association revised its governing document during Bedo's term. The specific amendments are not detailed in the record. In the recordWKU SGA Constitution, amended Spring 2002, TopSCHOLAR
27 March 2002Bedo presses parking issue after WKU land purchase collapses. Negotiations for WKU to buy the Forest Park Trailer Park for 400 to 500 new parking spaces broke down over price, even as the Diddle Arena renovation was set to eliminate about 200 spaces permanently. SGA President Leslie Bedo said several regents had voted to increase the student athletics fee on the basis that student parking would grow, and that the promised parking expansion had been put on hold. She argued more students parked on campus than attended basketball games and called more parking imperative. In the recordDaily News, 27 Mar 2002
11 April 2002Jamie Sears elected SGA president for 2002-03. In online voting, junior public relations major Jamie Sears of Melber defeated senior Sam Stinson 1,284 to 594 for SGA president, winning the seat as student representative on the Board of Regents. John Bradley beat Dana Lockhart 1,065 to 730 for executive vice president, Ross Pruitt ran unopposed for vice president of finance with 1,524 votes, Anna Coats edged Holly Skidmore 933 to 809 for vice president of public relations, and Brandon Copeland defeated Patti Johnson 1,106 to 761 for vice president of administration. In the recordWKU News, 11 Apr 2002
26 April 2002Voters approve Supremacy Clause constitutional amendment. SGA's official general election results page, archived on April 26, 2002, recorded that a constitutional amendment titled Supremacy Clause passed in the spring 2002 general election. The page listed the amendment result alongside the vote totals for the five executive races. In the recordSGA site, archived 26 Apr 2002

The full article text is not available online; only the headline and byline are indexed. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 77:56, 30 Apr 2002
