2002-03Jamie Sears (president)

22 August 2002Record enrollment of 17,500 strains campus. Western opened the fall with enrollment ballooning to 17,500, nearly 1,000 more students than the year before and a 20 percent increase since 1997. President Gary Ransdell warned that growth would be "painful" amid decreased state funding, and the Board of Regents approved a 10.4 percent tuition increase for 2003-04. In the recordHerald, 22 Aug 2002
19 September 2002Members demand answers on missing gazebo money. SGA members Brooke Smith, Dana Lockhart and Sam Stinson petitioned congress over $28,000 they said was unaccounted for, including about $5,000 that a April 2001 bill had set aside to build an on-campus gazebo that never appeared. President Jamie Sears said of the gazebo fund, "I have absolutely no idea where that money went." The petition was withdrawn after the executive council formed an ad hoc financial review committee. In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2002
24 September 2002Herald editorial blasts SGA over 'Gazebo-Gate'. The Herald's 11-member editorial board attacked SGA leaders over what it called "Gazebo-Gate," saying the money had gone to computers for the SGA office instead of the promised gazebo. It called leaders' ignorance about the missing money "shameful" and challenged Sears by name to "do her job" and provide real answers, writing that "I don't know" did not cut it. In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2002
October 2002Gazebo funds traced to SGA general fund. Vice president of finance Ross Pruitt reported that the $13,000 SGA had put toward the gazebo mistakenly went back into the organization's general fund and was spent on other things, including computers for SGA. Sears said she and former student activities director Scott Taylor decided over the summer where the leftover budget money would go, with other executive council members consulted by email. Pruitt said leaders from the past two administrations shared the blame, saying "I didn't do my homework." In the recordHerald, 1 Oct 2002
24 October 2002Congress votes down enrollment cap resolution. SGA congress rejected by a large margin a resolution asking Western to implement an enrollment cap, with Sears among those calling the measure too drastic. The failed proposal argued the university and state budgets had not kept pace with enrollment growth from 14,543 students in 1997 to about 17,770. Provost Barbara Burch and President Ransdell both said a cap was not the best answer to the growth problem. In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2002
5 December 2002Three resolutions pass on faculty pay, enrollment, parking. SGA passed two resolutions responding to a shortage of 75 faculty members and the lowest-paid faculty in the state, asking that unbudgeted tuition surplus money, about $800,000 that year, be used to hire faculty, and encouraging President Ransdell to create a task force on enrollment. A third resolution requested a change to the policy that gave Hilltopper Athletic Foundation donors student parking spaces, including the Grise Hall lot, at basketball games. In the recordHerald, 5 Dec 2002
6 February 2003Freshman committee appointments tabled. SGA tabled Sears's proposal to appoint three freshmen, Tim Howard, Katie Dawson and Robert Watkins, as the student members of a joint University Senate and SGA enrollment growth committee. Sears said she picked freshmen so they could serve the committee's expected two to three year life, but critics including associate justice Dana Lockhart said the appointments would make it hard for SGA to be taken seriously. In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2003
4 March 2003SGA joins Frankfort rally against budget cuts. About 200 students from six public universities rallied at the state Capitol against cuts to higher education, after the Kentucky House passed a budget cutting Western's funding by more than $1 million. Western sent a delegation of roughly 20 people including SGA members, organized through the board of Kentucky's student body presidents. Sears said 17 people "took the initiative to get on the bus." In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2003
4 March 2003Congress puts $3 radio fee referendum on ballot. SGA unanimously approved a bill placing a referendum on the April 2-3 general election ballot letting students vote on a $3 student fee for campus radio station Revolution 91.7-WWHR, which was operating on a $7,000 budget unchanged since 1998. Executive vice president John Bradley, who championed the measure, said it would empower students and boost voter turnout. A yes vote would send the fee recommendation to the Board of Regents for a final decision. In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2003
8 April 2003Bradley elected president; 2,014 vote. A total of 2,014 students voted in the spring SGA election, with results announced shortly after 1 a.m. Friday by chief justice Holly Skidmore. Paducah junior John Bradley won the presidency unopposed with 1,662 votes, Patti Johnson beat Dana Lockhart 1,185 to 685 for executive vice president, and Jessica Martin beat Shawn Peavie 1,056 to 686 for vice president of administration. The $3 WWHR radio fee referendum passed 1,066 to 765 and moved to the Board of Regents. In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2003
29 April 2003SGA closes year after 55 pieces of legislation. SGA held its last meeting of the year on April 22, having heard and debated more than 55 pieces of legislation, including a resolution that earmarked funds for new benches across campus. Sears counted the Frankfort rally among the year's greatest accomplishments, and the Revolution 91.7 fee measure stood as the first student referendum in SGA history, awaiting a final Board of Regents vote on May 9. President-elect Bradley said the high election turnout was the semester's best moment and pledged to fight student apathy the next year. In the recordHerald, 29 Apr 2003

2003-04John Bradley (president)

19 August 2003Bradley opens the year with cost, safety and involvement goals. New SGA president John Bradley opened the fall by naming low education costs his first goal and warning that fees for the proposed Greek Village should not be passed to the whole student body. SGA created an Ambassador Council to visit student organizations weekly, and planned its first forum of the semester on campus safety, an issue Bradley had worked on as a member of the Campus Safety Task Force formed after the death of freshman Katie Autry. The first congress meeting of the semester was set for August 26 in Downing University Center. In the recordHerald, 19 Aug 2003
25 September 2003SGA lines up against plus/minus grading. SGA members voiced concern at their Tuesday meeting over a plus/minus grading system proposed in the University Senate by economics professor Brian Strow. Bradley said he planned to oppose it, reporting that the state's other student body presidents had urged him to fight it, and the Academic Affairs committee prepared a student questionnaire on the change. Chief Justice Troy Ransdell argued the system would penalize students who scored best. In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2003
30 October 2003Congress urges students to vote as grading petition circulates. SGA unanimously passed a resolution recommending that Western students vote in the November 4 state election and research the candidates' stands on higher education, suspending the bylaws so it could pass before the vote. Members also reported that the petition against plus/minus grading had gathered 350 signatures with more petitions in circulation, and SGA planned a Homecoming tent on the Downing University Center south lawn. In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2003
2004The Constitutional Convention rebuilds the body. Three branches - Executive Cabinet, Senate and Judicial Council - drawn from the student body at large. The most consequential clause is the quietest: every enrolled student became a member of SGA with the right to vote in its elections. In the recordWKU SGA history
29 January 2004SGA organizes for a higher education rally in Frankfort. SGA prepared to join student governments from across Kentucky at a February 5 rally at the state Capitol against cuts to higher education funding, with slogans such as "Don't Balance the Budget on Our Backs" and students asked to wear backpacks. Congress approved $650 for transportation and reserved 47 spots for the trip. Bradley conceded change that year might be "unreasonable" to expect but said rallying could affect the future. In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2004
5 February 2004SGA budget frozen as Western absorbs $5.6 million in cuts. SGA announced at its Tuesday meeting that its budget, along with the Campus Activities Board's, had been informally frozen while Western worked out how to cut $5.6 million ordered by Gov. Ernie Fletcher's administration. SGA held $65,309.52 in its 2003-04 budget at the time, plus about $7,400 in an Aramark contract and foundation accounts that were not affected. Bradley said congress could still pass legislation requiring money, with the director of student activities deciding whether funds were available. In the recordHerald, 5 Feb 2004
18 March 2004Nick Todd elected SGA president as 1,232 students vote. Vice president of finance Nick Todd won the SGA presidency with 772 votes to Jessica Martin's 424, in a two-day online election in which 1,232 students voted. Katie Dawson won executive vice president with 778 votes and Evelina Petkova won administrative vice president with 692, with the first elected senate under the new constitution chosen at the same time. Bradley said he was disappointed by the turnout, and the winners were set to be sworn in at the SGA banquet on April 27. In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2004
18 March 2004Congress buys stepping stones for muddy campus paths. SGA unanimously approved legislation allocating $200 from its campus improvements account for stepping stones near Mass Media and Technology Hall, Tate Page Hall and Southwest Hall, where student foot traffic had worn dirt and mud paths. The bill's authors, Shawn Peavie and Sarah Cecil, said sidewalks had been considered but were too expensive. In the same meeting a straw poll on a proposed dorm Internet service fee drew 3 votes in support, 11 against and 11 abstentions. In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2004
8 April 2004SGA races to spend its remaining $45,000. With about $45,000 left of its original $105,000 budget for 2003-04, SGA moved to spend the remainder before the semester ended, since leftover funds would go to offset budget cuts across the university rather than carry over. Officers attributed the surplus partly to frugality during the spring budget freeze, and Todd suggested putting the money toward campus improvements such as benches or shuttle shelters. SGA also sponsored a dining services forum that week with Auxiliary Services and Dining Services officials. In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2004
15 April 2004Disputed 9-8 vote clouds the first speaker of the senate election. Congress elected constitution author Robert Watkins as the first speaker of the senate by 9 votes to 8 over Brittany Fausey, with 17 of 20 members present voting. The result was immediately questioned because the new constitution was unclear on whether two-thirds of eligible voters or of total membership was required, and three members present were barred from voting under a judicial council ruling. Martin warned of a "semester of frustration" if the dispute was not resolved at the year's final meeting, while Fausey declined to challenge the result. In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2004
20 April 2004The president-elect is investigated before he takes office. The Herald reported an investigation into missing funds from an SGA dining account. Articles of impeachment were drafted against the president-elect's existing finance post but the judicial council found the two-week process could not finish before the term ended. Because state law governs the student regent seat, the new constitution required a separate special election to fill it. In the recordHerald, April 2004

2004-05Patti Johnson (president)

20 April 2004SGA judicial council fielded impeachment bid against president-elect Todd. Days before new officers were due to be sworn in on April 27, SGA's judicial council found that $611 was missing from the SGA Aramark Dining Dollars account, which had started the academic year with $5,000 and had about $1,200 left. Senator Josh Collins drafted articles of impeachment against Todd's outgoing vice presidency of finance, but the council ruled a two-week impeachment process could not be completed before he left that office regardless. Only Todd, outgoing president John Bradley and adviser Charley Pride held cards to the account. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2004 - "SGA President-Elect Under Investigation" (Wayback)
24 August 2004SGA president Nick Todd resigned amid funds investigation. Nick Todd, elected SGA president in March with 772 of 1,232 votes cast, submitted his resignation in July, citing personal conflicts within the association. The former vice president of finance had come under investigation in April for the misuse of more than $600 in an SGA Dining Dollars account. Executive Vice President Katie Dawson acted as president until a new election set for Sept. 14-15. In the recordHerald, 24 Aug 2004
26 August 2004Internal audit recommended Todd repay SGA money. WKU's Office of the Internal Auditor reported that $872 in questionable purchases were made from the SGA Dining Dollars account between August 2003 and May 2004, mostly small buys at campus restaurants with no receipts. The report recommended that Todd reimburse the money, plus $71 for a charge made with the SGA purchasing card after a spring break car rental. Campus police determined no police action was necessary. In the recordHerald, 26 Aug 2004
2 September 2004Patti Johnson emerged as the only candidate in the special election. At a meeting for students interested in running in SGA's September special elections, Marion senior Patti Johnson, the previous year's executive vice president, was the only student to show interest in the presidency. She said she decided to run because of "the turmoil within the organization." Applications were also taken for the 23 open senate seats ahead of online voting on Sept. 14-15. In the recordHerald, 2 Sep 2004
21 September 2004Dean of Student Life contradicted Todd on sanctions. Howard Bailey, dean of Student Life, said Todd had been sanctioned by judicial affairs in July over the alleged misuse of university funds, disputing Todd's public claim that losing access to the Dining Dollars card was the only action taken against him. Bailey said federal privacy law barred him from revealing the sanctions. Todd acknowledged he was also no longer allowed to handle any SGA funds. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 21 Sep 2004
23 September 2004SGA approved a $110,000 budget. SGA approved a $110,000 budget for the 2004-05 academic year, up from $105,000 the year before, despite earlier expectations of a $15,000 to $17,000 cut under the university's budget reduction plan. Most of the money went toward operating fees, campus improvements and organizational aid. Adviser Charley Pride credited steady enrollment growth for the increase. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 23 Sep 2004
28 September 2004Johnson sworn in as president after winning 1,291 votes. Patti Johnson was sworn in as SGA president at the organization's fall reception on Sept. 23, after receiving 1,291 votes in the uncontested online election held Sept. 14 and 15. The 23 new senators were seated in the first fall senate election held under SGA's new constitution. Johnson was due to be sworn in as student regent at the Oct. 29 Board of Regents meeting. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 28 Sep 2004
16 November 2004SGA proposed a faculty evaluation pilot to the University Senate. SGA prepared to propose a two-year pilot program to the University Senate that would add five questions on matters such as office hours, punctuality and textbook use to faculty evaluations and post the answers on TopNet for students. Senator Josh Collins wrote the proposal with Troy Ransdell and Morgan Phelps after SGA scaled back an earlier push to release entire evaluations. The questions could appear on evaluations at the end of spring 2005 if the study was approved. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 16 Nov 2004
17 March 2005Katie Dawson elected SGA president for 2005-06. Executive Vice President Katie Dawson defeated Senate Speaker Josh Collins 1,268 to 472 in the spring election's only contested race to become the next SGA president. Students also passed a package of 40 constitutional amendments 1,193 to 262 and voted 1,019 to 669 to ask the Board of Regents to institute a $9 per semester Talisman yearbook fee. Mason Stevenson and Melissa Paris won the two vice presidencies unopposed, and all 25 senate candidates on the ballot were elected. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 17 Mar 2005
31 March 2005Goodrum found not guilty in Katie Autry murder trial. A jury in Owensboro found Lucas Goodrum, 23, of Scottsville not guilty of the May 2003 murder of Pellville freshman Melissa "Katie" Autry, who was set on fire in her Poland Hall dorm room and died three days later. The verdict came March 21 after three hours of deliberation, ending a three-week trial that had been moved from Warren County. Stephen Soules had earlier pleaded guilty to murder, rape, sodomy, arson and robbery and expected life in prison. In the recordHerald via Wayback, 31 Mar 2005
14 April 2005SGA funded the Buy-A-Book program. SGA passed legislation 22-2 on April 5 allocating $2,000 to the Buy-A-Book program, and the University Bookstore pledged to match the amount. The bill by senator Katharine Pettit was amended unanimously to help 20 students who needed financial assistance buying textbooks instead of 10. 2005The plus/minus grading fight. An Institutional Research report on plus and minus grading, a protest broadside, a post-winter-term student survey and an SGA handbook all survive - one of the few academic-policy campaigns documented from research through to public agitation. 20 November 2005WKU launched its centennial celebration. Western kicked off a 14-month celebration of its 1906 founding on Saturday, Nov. 19, dedicating three new campus landmarks including Centennial Plaza. SGA President Katie Dawson spoke at the plaza dedication, offering her own meaning of the school slogan "The Spirit Makes the Master." In the recordDaily News, 20 Nov 2005
8 December 2005SGA closed the fall with 10 pieces of legislation. The Herald reported that SGA passed 10 pieces of legislation in the fall semester, fewer than in previous fall semesters. Its legislation brought bikes, a cancer documentary and iPods to Western. The same issue reported that a senator named Johnson had been elected the new speaker of the senate. In the recordHerald, 8 Dec 2005 (via Wayback)
February 2006SGA took up a proposed $45 construction fee. At its first regular meeting of the spring semester, SGA discussed a proposed $45-per-semester fee to pay for a campus-wide wireless network, a new health center and renovations to the Ivan Wilson Center for Fine Arts. President Katie Dawson supported the fee, and Western's chief financial officer estimated it would raise about $1.4 million a year. In the recordDaily News, 1 Feb 2006
8 February 2006Ransdell asked SGA for a resolution backing the fee. WKU President Gary Ransdell came to the SGA meeting and urged senators to pass a resolution supporting the proposed $45 fee, which the Board of Regents would vote on April 7. Dawson sat on that board as student regent, and SGA officers said a supporting resolution was likely within a few weeks. In the recordDaily News, 8 Feb 2006
3 March 2006Executive vice president aired an internal rift. Executive Vice President Mason Stevenson read a letter at the SGA meeting saying some members trying to protect their political interests had "thwarted" SGA's mission to improve Western. The letter outlined his concerns about relations between the executive and legislative branches. In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2006 (via Wayback)
16 March 2006Senate put $2,000 toward SGA's 40th anniversary party. Two bills devoting $2,000 to a party for SGA's 40th anniversary passed unanimously at the group's Tuesday meeting. The Herald reported the organization planned a campus-wide party to mark four decades of student government at Western. In the recordHerald, 16 Mar 2006 (via Wayback)
8 April 2006Regents approved the fee; Dawson's senior exemption failed. The Board of Regents voted 9-1 to approve the $46-per-semester construction fee, with Dawson abstaining, and rejected 10-1 her proposal to exempt next year's seniors, an idea she had raised at a student forum the week before. Dawson said that although she supported the fee, she could not vote for it with so many seniors counting on the exemption. In the recordDaily News, 8 Apr 2006
13 April 2006Rob Watkins elected SGA president. Bowling Green senior Robert Watkins won the online election for SGA president after spending more than a week seeking supporters who would vote on TopNet. He defeated Berea junior Kara Ratliff, and the results were announced Tuesday at a crowded Revolution 91. In the recordHerald, 13 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)
20 April 2006Executive board issued its first veto of the year. After the Tuesday senate meeting, the SGA executive board vetoed a bill that would have financed community- and campus-oriented projects through civic engagement grants, the first time it exercised its veto power that year. The Herald reported the grants were "a reality for only about 30 minutes" and that time restraints halted an appeal of the veto. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)
20 April 2006Herald editorial attacked SGA misspending. A Herald editorial titled "SGA misspending" said members should not have to be "motivated by a giveaway to show up for meetings." It noted that the opinion page had devoted considerable space in recent weeks to both positive and negative aspects of SGA, which it said could and should be an important organization on campus. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2006 (via Wayback)

2006-07Robert Watkins (president)

5 September 2006Fifth SGA opened its year, swore in eight senators. At the first meeting of that year's Senate, called to order with 8 of 18 senators present, eight new senators were sworn in: Chris Anderson, Diane DeRosa-Reynolds, Leah Keys, Amanda Kidd, Suzie Moghaddam, Seth Norman, Tori Theiss and Christa Wilcox. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen reported $30,000 in organizational aid for the year, and the senate nominated committee heads and Judicial Council members, including Matt Holland as chief justice. The minutes record Jeanne L. Johnson delivering the executive vice president's report. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Sep 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here
24 October 2006SGA tightened its budget after leaving $24,000 unspent. The Herald reported that SGA had left about $24,000 of its $115,000 budget unspent at the end of 2005-06, money that returned to Western's general fund. Administrative Vice President Amanda Allen said SGA was cutting money from areas where it went unspent, adding almost $10,000 to organizational aid and $3,000 to the miscellaneous fund. Allen called the previous year a bad budgetary year but also a learning year. In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2006 (Wayback)
25 October 2006SGA-run referendum showed students favored the I-A football move. In an online referendum SGA arranged alongside the homecoming queen election, 64.6 percent of voting students, 1,095, supported WKU's proposed move to Division I-A football, with 600 against. A total of 2,136 students voted in the poll, and the 1,695 who answered the football question represented about 9 percent of enrollment. SGA President Rob Watkins, who held the student seat on the Board of Regents, said the poll would help him define a position but noted the homecoming tie-in likely drew football-friendly voters. In the recordDaily News, 25 Oct 2006
2 November 2006SGA senate unanimously passed a resolution backing the I-A move. SGA members unanimously passed a resolution saying they supported the move to Division I-A football, following the student referendum result. Watkins, as student regent and SGA president, still would not say what his own position was before the regents' vote. In the recordHerald front page, 5 Nov 2006 (Wayback)
28 November 2006Watkins resigned as SGA president and student regent. SGA's own senate minutes record that president and student regent Rob Watkins's resignation was formally read into the meeting at the senate's regularly scheduled Tuesday session, with senators told Jeanne Johnson would be sworn in as president at the Dec. 5 Winter Banquet. Senators had voiced concerns about Watkins at an unannounced 10 p.m. meeting the evening before. A Herald front-page account (Wayback, 2 Dec 2006) covered the same resignation but gave the date as 30 November; this entry follows the primary senate minutes, which date the reading of the resignation to 28 November, leaving students without representation on Western's governing board for at least a month. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here
28 November 2006Senate passed Books for Africa bill and a printing-quota resolution. At the same Nov. 28 meeting where Watkins's resignation was read into the record, the senate unanimously passed Bill 11-06-F, sponsored by Lucas Humble, to collect textbooks the university bookstore would not buy back and send them to Africa. Senators also unanimously passed Resolution 08-06-F, sponsored by Seth Norman, backing a university study of a computer-lab printing quota after administrators told SGA's Student Affairs committee how many pages some students were printing. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here
28 November 2006Senate heard Douglas Keen Hall was next for renovation. In a University Committees report to the senate, a member reported that the Student Life Foundation had discussed campus housing renovations and that Douglas Keen Hall would be the next residence hall to be renovated, within about three years. The same report covered a Budget Council discussion of rolling several student organizations' budgets, including SGA's, into the university's base budget. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 28 Nov 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here
5 December 2006Senate tabled two resolutions for lack of quorum at Winter Banquet meeting. With 16 of 31 senators present, the senate lacked quorum to act on Resolution 09-06-F on vending machine prices and Resolution 10-06-F on special events parking, so both were tabled. Executive Vice President was listed vacant, since Jeanne Johnson had moved into the presidency after Robert Watkins's resignation. The Judicial Council reported meeting on the time requirements for the student regent seat. Winners of the Outstanding Senator and Outstanding Committee Member awards, chosen by secret ballot, were announced later that evening at the Winter Banquet. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 5 Dec 2006 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here
27 January 2007Fill-in SGA leader Jeanne Johnson challenged tuition plan at regents meeting. The Board of Regents approved a 7.8 percent tuition increase for 2007-08, bringing tuition and fees to $6,417 a year including the higher athletics fee. Jeanne Johnson, a junior economics and finance major from Marion described as a fill-in for the former SGA president, opposed the size of the increase for online and distance-learning courses, though she had no vote. She said 'We know tuition increases are inevitable' but argued distance learners should not carry that burden. In the recordDaily News, 27 Jan 2007
February 2007Johnson won the student regent election; SGA seated a full senate. Jeanne Johnson, SGA president and Marion junior, won the special election for Western's vacant student regent seat with 688 votes, 41 percent of ballots cast. The same Herald issue reported that SGA began the spring semester with its first full senate attendance since fall 2004. In the recordHerald front page, 3 Feb 2007 (Wayback)
24 April 2007Provost rejected plus/minus grading; Johnson credited SGA's campaign. Provost Barbara Burch told the University Senate she would not implement the plus/minus grading system the senate had passed 36-23 in March. SGA President Jeanne Johnson said she was grateful for the decision, noting SGA had raised awareness and led student protests, and pledged that students would keep fighting if the issue returned. She said 'I'm confident that the students' opinions have been expressed.' In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2007 (Wayback)
2 May 2007SGA banquet closed the year and swore in 2007-08 officers. At its annual banquet on May 1, SGA presented awards and swore in officers for 2007-08, with Jeanne Lynn Johnson of Marion becoming the new SGA president and student regent and receiving the Dero Downing Award. Johnathon Boles of Elizabethtown became executive vice president, Kayla Shelton speaker of the Student Senate, and Cherieth Lea Lineweaver administrative vice president. Amanda Beth Allen received the Charles A. Keown Award, SGA's highest honor. In the recordWKU News, 2 May 2007 (Wayback)

2007-08Jeanne Johnson (president)

13 September 2007Fall senate election drew 25 candidates for 20 seats. SGA reported record interest in its fall senate election, with 25 students running for 20 available seats, the most applications President Jeanne Johnson said she had ever seen. Elections were set for Sept. 19 and 20 through TopNet, with an informational table in Downing University Center on Sept. 18. Public relations director Liz Goddard said more competition would produce harder workers. In the recordHerald, 13 Sep 2007
2 October 2007SGA co-sponsored mock gubernatorial election. SGA and the Office of the Secretary of State co-sponsored a mock gubernatorial election at Centennial Mall as part of Secretary of State Trey Grayson's Civic Literacy Initiative of Kentucky. The 127 students who voted chose challenger Steve Beshear over incumbent Gov. Ernie Fletcher, 74 to 50. President Jeanne Johnson and Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles called the event a success. In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2007
18 October 2007Resolution demanded more state funding for Western. At its Oct. 9 meeting SGA passed a resolution asking the state government to appropriate more money to Western, which had received 54 percent of the funding the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended for fiscal year 2008. President Jeanne Johnson argued that tuition increases to cover the shortfall hurt students. The resolution stated Western needed the full recommended amount to meet its 2020 educational goals. In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007
18 October 2007SGA organized Walk Out Western budget protest. SGA sponsored Walk Out Western, asking students to leave class at 12:20 p.m. on Oct. 25 for a rally at the Colonnade to protest state budget cuts, with empty seats meant as a message to Frankfort legislators. President Gary Ransdell said he could not condone students walking out of class and doubted a single-campus protest would affect state funding. Johnson said other state universities declined to join but were watching how it worked at Western. In the recordHerald, 18 Oct 2007
25 October 2007Committee proposed $1,995 educational video subscription. SGA's Academic Affairs Committee, chaired by Drew Eclov, prepared legislation to buy a roughly $1,995 subscription to United Streaming, a Discovery Channel-owned site with about 45,000 educational video clips that Eclov called a version of YouTube for higher education. The committee planned to survey students and professors before bringing it to a vote. SGA also scheduled a vote on a resolution placing $1,000 in a field trip fund to support learning outside the classroom. In the recordHerald, 25 Oct 2007
November 2007Athletics director asked SGA for help on football attendance. Athletics Director Wood Selig came to the SGA meeting to ask senators for ideas on getting more students to football games as Western moved to the Football Bowl Subdivision, which required an average attendance of 15,000 to keep bowl eligibility. Senators suggested advertising on Western's website and Facebook rather than email, and later game times. Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles, who sat on a faculty advisory committee for athletics, arranged the consultation. In the recordHerald, 1 Nov 2007
15 November 2007SGA planned Listen Up Legislators lobbying campaign. SGA began laying groundwork for Listen Up Legislators, a spring lobbying campaign in which senators would meet legislators one-on-one in Frankfort to push for university funding, after the Council on Postsecondary Education recommended a $174 million increase for public universities. Chief of staff Skylar Jordan said the traditional February rally had not worked, pointing to Western receiving only 54 percent of the recommended increase. Other state student governments expressed interest in coordinating lobbying dates. In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2007
31 January 2008Spring session opened with ONE Campus bill. At its first spring meeting on Jan. 29, SGA introduced legislation by Senators Matt Vaughan and Doug Tate asking the senate to recognize Western as a ONE Campus, part of the national campaign against global AIDS and extreme poverty. SGA also released its spring schedule, including Listen Up Legislators on Feb. 14, the Frankfort rally for higher education on Feb. 20 and the annual banquet on April 29. In the semester's opening handout, Executive Vice President Johnathon Boles pointed members to the constitution's purpose of serving the student body equally. In the recordHerald, 31 Jan 2008
20 February 2008Fifty senators write down what a lobbying trip felt like. After a student rally at the Capitol in Frankfort, dozens of SGA members each filed an individual written reflection, archived one per person. The richest first-person source in the entire collection. In the recordTopSCHOLAR - Frankfort rally reflections
April 2008Spring election closed amid low-turnout criticism. Voting for three executive seats and 28 senate seats ended after a one-week campaign that candidates criticized as part of SGA's low-involvement problem; turnout had been 1,424 the year before and 1,376 the year before that. Red Towel Party presidential candidate Tedde Harden promised to rework what he called outdated election codes, while opponent Johnathon Boles agreed campaign time should be extended. President Jeanne Johnson said her administration inherited the codes and had tried new turnout methods, including extra credit for attending the debate. In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2008
17 April 2008Ransdell announced 9 percent tuition increase. President Gary Ransdell announced at campus forums that he would recommend a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09, abandoning a plan to hold increases at 6 percent. The change followed a state budget crisis in which Gov. Steve Beshear ordered a 3 percent cut to postsecondary education in December 2007 and proposed an additional 12 percent, later reduced by the General Assembly to 3 percent. Ransdell said the swing from expected state revenue was about $11 million to $12 million. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2008
24 April 2008Student regent Johnson opposed scale of 9 percent tuition increase. The Board of Regents approved a 9 percent tuition increase for 2008-09 and finalized $2.5 million in cuts to the 2007-08 budget. Louisville regent Larry Zielke moved to cap the increase at 6 percent and push the General Assembly for more funding instead; SGA President and student regent Jeanne Johnson seconded the motion, but it died with only two votes. Johnson also argued the $370,000 budgeted for the Honors College should be reduced, saying the college benefited only 900 students and other students should not have to pay for it. In the recordHerald 83:51, 29 Apr 2008 - "Regents approve 9 percent tuition increase, finalize 07-08 budget cuts"
18 July 2008Johnson's regent term ended as Boles took the board oath. The Board of Regents read a resolution thanking Jeanne Johnson for her service as the board's student member from April 27, 2007 to July 18, 2008, calling her term one of "able leadership, faithful service, and dedication." Johnathon Boles, who had already been installed as SGA president that spring, took the oath of office as student regent the same day, formally completing the transition between administrations. In the recordWKU Board of Regents minutes, 18 Jul 2008 (TopSCHOLAR)Read it here

2008-09Johnathon Boles (president) · Kayla Shelton (president)

4 September 2008Shots fired outside Pearce-Ford Tower put dorms on lockdown. Campus police responded to a report of shots fired at about 3 a.m. Saturday in the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot, where a witness said a man got out of a vehicle, fired a gun and drove away. Police found shell casings but no damage, no one was hurt, and all dorms went into lockdown after the incident. In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2008
18 September 2008Fall senate election drew above-average turnout. SGA seated nine new student senators after a two-day fall election in which 18 candidates competed. Seven seats had been open, four reserved for freshmen, and two more opened when two senators resigned the Monday before the vote. A total of 687 students voted, which President Johnathon Boles said was higher than the average for a fall election. In the recordHerald, 18 Sep 2008
13 November 2008Boles and Smiley appointed to governor's college affordability group. Gov. Steve Beshear appointed SGA President Johnathon Boles and SGA member Kevin Smiley to the student committee of his College Access Work Group, which was charged with recommending ways to make Kentucky higher education more affordable. The two traveled to Frankfort for the committee's first meeting, where they raised the impact of textbook costs, which Boles put at an average of $800 a year. In the recordDaily News, 13 Nov 2008
19 November 2008Senate voted to launch a Textbook Subsidy Program. The SGA senate voted to contribute $500 to start a Textbook Subsidy Program, an effort developed with the University Bookstore, which pledged another $500, to build an endowment that would lower textbook costs for students. The senate also created a program board of nearly 20 members, including Boles, bookstore representatives and members from each college, to work out funding and distribution. In the recordDaily News, 19 Nov 2008
4 December 2008SGA made its first mid-year budget cut. Facing a state shortfall that required the university to cut about 4 percent of its budget, SGA cut $4,100 from its $110,000 budget, the first time it had cut its budget in the middle of an academic year. Boles and Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley chose to cut a $2,600 surplus from the fall retreat and $1,500 from organizational aid, protecting scholarships and Provide-A-Ride. Boles said he was working to get charter buses to send students to a Feb. 3 rally in Frankfort against higher education budget cuts. In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2008
29 January 2009Ice storm hit campus, injuring a student and closing regional campuses. A winter storm coated campus in ice during the week of Jan. 27, part of the second-largest power outage recorded in Kentucky. A falling tree limb struck a sophomore near Grise Hall, who was treated and released, and WKU canceled classes at its Elizabethtown, Owensboro, Glasgow, Fort Knox and Radcliff campuses as well as evening classes on the main campus. AT&T cell outages kept officials from reaching students by text message. In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2009
12 February 2009Judicial Council ordered a special student regent election over executive dissent. After Boles' resignation left the student regent seat empty, the SGA Judicial Council voted 2-1 on Feb. 10 to hold a special election on Feb. 24 and 25. Chief Justice Lisa Kappler cast the dissenting vote, calling the constitution's requirement a gray area, and Executive Vice President Skylar Jordan presented a letter arguing the election was unnecessary. President Kayla Shelton said she supported the council's decision. In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009
12 February 2009Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned. SGA Chief Justice Lisa Kappler resigned Thursday night in a letter sent to President Kayla Shelton and student activities director Charley Pride, saying she wanted to spend more time on school and family. Shelton said she hoped the senate would vote on a new chief justice at the next meeting because the special election for student regent was two weeks away. In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2009
26 February 2009Reagan Gilley won the special student regent election. Administrative Vice President Reagan Gilley, a Pineville senior, defeated Speaker of the Senate Nate Eaton 477 votes to 224 in the special election for student regent, with 701 students voting. The seat had been vacant for 26 days after former President Johnathon Boles resigned on Jan. 30 for health reasons; Executive Vice President Kayla Shelton had taken his place as president but not as regent. In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2009
16 April 2009Kevin Smiley won the SGA presidential election. The Herald reported Kevin Smiley's win in the spring SGA presidential election under the headline "All Smiles, Kevin Smiley Wins Student Government Association Election," ending Kayla Shelton's term as the president who had finished out Johnathon Boles's 2008-09 year. Smiley took office as president and student regent for 2009-10. In the recordCollege Heights Herald 84:46, 16 Apr 2009
23 April 2009SGA negotiated removal of proposed $30 per-credit-hour fee. SGA and university officials agreed to strike a proposed $30 fee for every credit hour over 15 from the Board of Regents agenda, replacing it with a proposal to raise the add/drop fee from $20 to $50. SGA canceled a planned protest after the compromise, and Student Regent Reagan Gilley called the outcome "really a win-win for everyone." In the recordHerald, 23 Apr 2009

2009-10Kevin Smiley (president)

4 September 2009Smiley nominates his brother as chief of staff. SGA President Kevin Smiley announced Danville sophomore Eric Smiley, his brother, as his nominee for chief of staff, a paid voting position on the executive cabinet. Former executive vice president Skylar Baker-Jordan called the nomination "completely unethical," while Smiley said he chose his brother because he had no previous political agenda. The senate was set to vote on all nominations Sept. 8, with a two-thirds majority needed for approval. In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2009
15 September 2009Fall election opens; SGA gives $2,000 to Residence Hall Association. At the Sept. 15 senate meeting, Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that SGA gave $2,000 from its budget to the Residence Hall Association. President Kevin Smiley announced that voting in the fall SGA election had started on TopNet, with polls open until Wednesday night and results announced about midnight. Smiley also urged senators to join the Campus Safety Walk, in which participants looked for dimly lit or overgrown areas on campus. In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2009
14 October 2009SGA sponsors forum on new tailgating policy. About 30 people attended an SGA-sponsored forum where students and administrators discussed Western's amended tailgating policy, which banned vehicles from campus lawns on game days. Howard Bailey, vice president for student affairs, told students the policy would stay the same, and Speaker of the Senate Wade Pierce suggested tent giveaways to ease the transition. President Kevin Smiley said he was pleased with the attendance and that SGA would keep questioning the policy. In the recordHerald, 14 Oct 2009
20 October 2009Three senators resign over publications committee appointment. Senators Michel Stephens, Emmett Stephens and Daniel Shaw resigned at the Oct. 20 meeting. Michel Stephens cited President Kevin Smiley's nomination of Greg Capillo to the Student Publications Committee, which helps choose the Herald's editor-in-chief, saying the pick was not based on merit or experience. Smiley called the accusations of favoritism and corruption unfounded and said the seats would stay vacant until he appointed replacements for senate approval. In the recordHerald, 20 Oct 2009
10 November 2009Judicial Council removes senator for unexcused absences. Chief Justice Stuart Kenderes reported that the Judicial Council removed Senator Theodore Harden, a graduate student from Otisville, N.Y., from SGA for excessive unexcused absences; Harden did not attend the council meeting to defend himself. The council also reviewed Senator Vashae Swope for absences but voted to let her remain. Attendance guidelines were posted in the SGA office window, and Rachel Wilcox was approved as a new senator at the same meeting. In the recordHerald, 10 Nov 2009
11 December 2009WKU begins weighing a smoke-free campus. After the University of Kentucky and the University of Louisville went smoke-free, the Faculty Welfare Committee of Western's University Senate prepared a smoking survey for students, faculty and staff to take in February. SGA President Kevin Smiley said he would encourage the whole campus to take the survey, and President Gary Ransdell said he would look to SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council for direction on any policy. In the recordHerald, 11 Dec 2009
27 January 2010Two more senators resign; Frankfort rally buses announced. At the Jan. 27 meeting, Aaron Pawley and Eileen Forsythe resigned as senators, Pawley because of a difficult course load and Forsythe because she was studying abroad in England. President Kevin Smiley announced free buses to carry 75 students to a Feb. 9 rally in Frankfort where advocates from Kentucky's public universities would lobby legislators on higher education funding. Western student Colton Jessie was slated to speak at the rally. In the recordHerald, 27 Jan 2010
2 February 2010SGA organizes trip to Rally for Higher Education. SGA and the Provost's office offered free bus transportation for 75 students to the Rally for Higher Education on Feb. 9 at the Kentucky State Capitol, a year after winter weather derailed the previous attempt. Students who registered through the SGA website received an excused absence, and the rally included a chance to meet lawmakers and hear an address from Gov. Steve Beshear. In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2010
22 February 2010Senate passes funding bills for baseball, a sorority event and study abroad. At its Feb. 22 meeting the senate unanimously passed a funding bill and, with single dissents apiece, a bill funding the baseball program and a $1,300 allocation for an Alpha Kappa Alpha event. It also unanimously approved several study-abroad reimbursement bills and confirmed Daniel Shaw as parliamentarian, along with a new Academic Affairs committee chair nominee and a new Student Affairs chair. In the recordSGA senate minutes, 22 Feb 2010
23 March 2010SGA passes election codes and two funding bills. The senate passed the spring 2010 election codes, a bill giving $500 to the Agriculture Students Striving for Effective Tomorrows conference for high school students, and a bill designating $1,200 for lodging for FIJIs Across America, in which eight Phi Gamma Delta members planned to cycle across the country for Alzheimer's research. Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman reported that all but three approved organizations had received their organizational aid checks. In the recordHerald, 23 Mar 2010
April 2010Colton Jessie elected SGA president for 2010-11. Bowling Green junior Colton Jessie won the SGA presidency with 63 percent of the vote, taking 726 votes to 424 for Administrative Vice President Justin Thurman, on a platform of sustainability, handicap accessibility and changing the tailgating policy. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president with 731 votes to Currie Martin's 415, and Wade Pierce ran unopposed for administrative vice president with 1,016 votes. Results were announced at midnight Wednesday. In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2010

2010-11Colton Jessie (president)

14 September 2010SGA raised scholarship budget to $20,000. After running out of scholarship money the previous year, SGA increased its scholarship budget from $12,000 to $20,000 and lowered general senate funding from $20,000 to $12,000 to cover the change. Study abroad awards were capped at $500 for a semester trip and $250 for a winter or summer term so more students could receive money. SGA also finalized a new study away scholarship for travel inside the country and set aside $400 for it in the winter term. In the recordHerald, 14 Sep 2010
23 September 2010Twelve senators elected in fall election with 847 voters. Twelve students won seats in the fall senate election, in which 847 total voters cast ballots on TopNet. Keyana Boka, Natalie Broderick and Eppiphanie Benton were elected freshman senators, running unopposed, while 25 students competed for the at-large seats. Winners included Diego Leal Ambriz, who would run for president that spring. In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2010
19 November 2010Ransdell brought $49 million DUC renovation plan to SGA. President Gary Ransdell and head architect Jeff Stivers told SGA at its Nov. 16 meeting that officials were moving ahead on a plan to completely renovate Downing University Center at a cost of up to $49 million. Students would pay about $140 extra per year in fees for up to 20 years, and Ransdell promised students would be involved in every decision. SGA had to pass resolutions on the design and fees before the Board of Regents could approve the project. In the recordHerald, 19 Nov 2010
7 December 2010SGA funds extended library hours for finals week. The senate approved $600 to keep the library open until 2 a.m. during finals week, covering extra staff time and lighting. President Colton Jessie said continuing the service was never in question, calling finals "an important time for students." In the recordHerald, 7 Dec 2010
10 December 2010Senate tabled DUC resolution over lack of student input. Senators tabled the bill supporting the DUC renovation at the Dec. 7 meeting, saying they had not received enough student input just three weeks after learning of the project. Jessie backed the delay, saying he wanted to hear students' voices before moving forward, even though it pushed SGA's presentation to the Board of Regents from January 21 to April 22. Campus Improvements Chair Kaylee Egerer said many students did not yet know they would pay $140 a year for the project. In the recordHerald, 10 Dec 2010
11 February 2011Herald reported Greeks held 40 percent of SGA seats. The Herald reported that 21 of SGA's 50 members belonged to Greek organizations, more than 40 percent, while less than 8 percent of the student body was in a fraternity or sorority. Sixteen of the 21 were fraternity men, and two fraternities, Sigma Chi and Lambda Chi Alpha, accounted for nine of them. Officers defended the imbalance, and the story noted SGA's operating budget for 2010-11 was $121,335, drawn from tuition. In the recordHerald, 11 Feb 2011
22 February 2011SGA unanimously passed DUC renovation resolution. SGA unanimously passed the resolution supporting DUC renovations at its Feb. 22 meeting, the bill's second reading. Project costs were capped at $49,128,545, with a student fee of up to $70 per semester for 20 years and $1.5 million per year from WKU. The resolution, authored by Kaylee Egerer, asked for assurance of a 24-hour study space and called for construction to begin as soon as possible while interest rates were low. In the recordHerald, 22 Feb 2011
March 2011SGA members joined Rally for Higher Education in Frankfort. SGA members traveled to Frankfort on March 1 for the annual Rally for Higher Education, where SGA secretary Katie Stillwell was the keynote speaker representing students statewide. Her speech urged legislators to protect money already set aside for higher education. Jessie, the previous year's keynote speaker, joined chief of staff Charlie Harris and other state SGA officers for a lunch with Gov. Steve Beshear. In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2011
April 2011Administrative Vice President Wade Pierce to hand post to fraternity brother. Pierce, who chaired the organizational aid committee, said he would be succeeded as administrative vice president by Devon Hilderbrandt, his committee co-chair and his "little brother" in Lambda Chi Alpha. Hilderbrandt ran unopposed in that spring's election. In the recordHerald, 1 Apr 2011
7 April 2011Stephens won presidency with 56 percent of 1,066 votes. Billy Stephens, a junior from Hawesville, defeated senior Diego Leal Ambriz for SGA president, taking 56 percent of the 1,066 total votes in results announced just after midnight on April 7. Kendrick Bryan was re-elected executive vice president and Devon Hilderbrandt won administrative vice president, both unopposed. All 35 senate candidates were elected to the 36 open seats, each needing just one vote to win. In the recordHerald, 7 Apr 2011
6 May 2011Senate tabled tobacco-free campus resolution. After nearly 45 minutes of debate, the senate tabled a resolution supporting a tobacco-free campus until the next semester. The resolution rested on a survey of more than 400 students in which 47.82 percent supported a ban, but senators argued the survey was biased because tombstones displaying the dangers of smoking had been laid outside DUC the day it was given. The campus improvements committee then said it would not support a ban until the two-year on-campus living requirement was removed. In the recordHerald, 6 May 2011

2011-12Billy Stephens (president)

6 September 2011Senate reconvenes, appointments confirmed, tobacco vote postponed. At the semester's first senate meeting, held after the previous week's session was canceled, senators postponed a vote on the tobacco-free campus resolution so new members could review it first. President Billy Stephens made all of his executive-branch, judicial-committee and committee-chair appointments in a single blanket vote that passed unanimously, and Speaker of the Senate Kaylee Egerer told senators to keep generating new ideas for their committees. In the recordHerald, 7 Sep 2011
16 September 2011SGA passes tobacco-free campus resolution with housing condition. The SGA senate voted unanimously for a resolution supporting a campus-wide tobacco ban, but only if WKU dropped its requirement that students live on campus for two years. President Gary Ransdell had said the Board of Regents would not consider a ban until SGA, the University Senate and Staff Council all passed resolutions. SGA was the only body to attach the housing stipulation. In the recordHerald, 16 Sep 2011
23 September 2011Fall senate election fills 11 seats with 977 votes cast. SGA announced its fall senator election results just after midnight on Thursday, with 11 new senators elected including Christopher Costa, Corey Johnson and Mallory Treece. Twenty students ran for the seats and 977 students voted. President Billy Stephens said he was happy with the turnout for a fall election and that he got the contested race he wanted. In the recordHerald, 23 Sep 2011
30 September 2011SGA to lend iPads through WKU's Educational Resource Center. SGA partnered with the Educational Resource Center in Gary Ransdell Hall to provide two first-generation iPads for the ERC to load textbooks onto and lend out to students at no cost, part of President Billy Stephens' push to make the organization more visibly useful to students. In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2011
9 November 2011Senate defeats DUC name change resolution 19-8. A resolution to rename Downing University Center as Downing Student Union, written by campus improvements chair Keyana Boka, was voted down 19-8 with one abstention after a lengthy open debate. Executive Vice President Kendrick Bryan suggested putting the question on the spring ballot, but senators noted architects working on the DUC renovation would need an answer sooner. In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2011
15 November 2011Herald editorial tells SGA to drop renaming and keep its promises. The Herald editorial board wrote that SGA should focus on student issues rather than renaming a building honoring former president Dero Downing, who had recently died. It said Stephens had barely addressed his platform promises, including a dead day before finals and an improved Provide-a-Ride service, which had seen no visible progress since SGA cut ties with Franklin Taxi. In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011
15 November 2011Two senators removed for absences; ten faced judicial review. Ten of SGA's 36 senators were called before the judicial board during the fall semester for excessive absences from senate and committee meetings. Two of them, Kevin Adams and Kevin Preston, were dismissed from the senate after failing to attend their judicial hearings, which the council interpreted as intent to resign. The rest received warnings, and Stephens said he would appoint replacements to the two empty seats. In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2011
18 November 2011SGA pays surprise $15,000 bill for previous year's Provide-A-Ride. SGA paid Parking Services a $15,000 retroactive payment for the prior year's Provide-A-Ride service after Parking Services found no record of the previous administration's payment. The money was split evenly between the organizational aid and student scholarship funds, $7,500 from each. Stephens said he was "shocked" by the bill, while 2010-11 president Colton Jessie insisted his administration had budgeted the money. In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2011
24 February 2012SGA approves $50,026 spring budget after $54,000 fall spending. The senate approved a spring 2012 budget of $50,026, divided among operations, public relations, executive programming and senate programming, with $10,500 set aside for organizational aid and $12,000 for scholarships. Chief of Staff Katie Stillwell told senators SGA had spent about $54,000 in the fall, $15,000 of it the retroactive Provide-A-Ride payment. In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2012
28 March 2012Chief of Staff Eric Smiley approved after Stillwell's resignation. The senate approved President Billy Stephens' choice of Eric Smiley as chief of staff after Katie Stillwell resigned the post; Smiley had served as chief of staff two years earlier under his brother Kevin Smiley's administration. The same meeting passed five bills, including two Organizational Aid grants of $500 each to six campus groups (the Chinese Students and Scholars Association, Geology Club, Chinese Music Club, Relay for Life, International Club and Baptist Campus Ministry), $500 toward the April 19 International Night, $398 reimbursing two Kindle Fires raffled at the WKU Student Research Conference, and $500 toward Big Red's trip to the 2012 Mascot Nationals. Senators also passed a resolution for a second campus cleanup on April 17 and moved $3,000 from general senate funds to Organizational Aid so SGA could spend down its budget before the semester's end; announcements noted that spring executive elections would open at 12:01 a.m. the next day. In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2012
30 March 2012Dodds elected SGA president for 2012-13; Boka and Alvey win uncontested VP races. Cory Dodds was elected SGA president for 2012-13 with 44 percent of the vote, over senator Corey Johnson with 35 percent and former senator Austin Wingate with 21 percent. Sophomore Keyana Boka was elected executive vice president and Cain Alvey administrative vice president; both vice-presidential races were uncontested. In the recordHerald, 30 Mar 2012

2012-13Cory Dodds (president)

6 September 2012Senate unanimously opposed the bi-term and per-credit-hour tuition proposal. SGA unanimously passed a resolution opposing an administration proposal to emphasize bi-term courses and shift tuition to a per-credit-hour model. Dodds argued the change would charge students more, since full-time students then paid for 12 hours but could enroll in up to 18. He called it a financial burden students should not have to bear. In the recordHerald, 6 Sep 2012
25 September 2012Fall senate seats filled after two resignations. Two senators resigned over time commitments and student Shea Wyatt was named to fill in. New freshman senators Barrett Greenwell, Taylor Ruby, Cole McDowell and Paige Settles were sworn in along with Gatton Academy senator Linda Cruz and graduate senators Mark Reeves and Katie Martin. In the recordHerald, 27 Sep 2012
13 November 2012SGA worked to restart a student government for the Glasgow campus. SGA officials traveled to WKU's Glasgow campus to help restart its dormant student representative body and connect it to main campus. Dodds said Glasgow students had no mechanism for their voices to be heard except contacting main-campus SGA. Roy Ratliff, nominated interim president of the Glasgow student body, said its top priority was establishing a writing center, for which the group had set aside $2,700. In the recordHerald, 13 Nov 2012
14 November 2012Senate reviewed its budget and heard a retention pitch. Speaker of the Senate Christopher Costa opened the floor to Joelle Carter, assistant vice president for Retention and Student Services, who asked senators for ideas on keeping students enrolled to graduation, and SGA's current budget balance was distributed to members. In the recordHerald, 14 Nov 2012
15 February 2013SGA passed its teaching assistant evaluation resolution. On Feb. 5 the senate passed a resolution creating teaching assistant evaluations, a program Dodds had campaigned on and drafted with his executive officers to pitch to Provost Gordon Emslie. Nicki Seay, chair of the Legislative Research Committee, wrote the bill, which aimed to make TA evaluation uniform across departments. The resolution next needed review by the Academic Quality Committee and approval by the University Senate. In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2013
20 February 2013Senate tabled a plus-minus grading resolution. Senator Hannah Garland's resolution to adopt plus and minus grades for high and low letter grades was tabled after public relations chair Mac Mullins argued for a more formal proposal and more student input first; a similar plan had drawn SGA resistance when the provost proposed it in 2007. In the recordHerald, 21 Feb 2013
26 February 2013Senate amended the constitution, adding regional-campus seats. After two to three years of executive discussion, the senate passed most of a package of constitutional amendments, replacing class-year senate seats with college-based representation and guaranteeing seats for regional campuses such as Glasgow and Owensboro. A bylaw that would have made SGA members permanently ineligible for SGA-sponsored scholarships was stripped out and did not pass. In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013
March 2013Provost Emslie cancelled the bi-term proposal SGA had opposed. Provost Gordon Emslie announced at the Feb. 21 University Senate meeting that he was dropping his bi-term emphasis proposal and had no plans to revive it, citing input from students and faculty. Both SGA and the University Senate had passed resolutions against it. Dodds said the revocation was in the student body's best interest, saying "I strongly opposed it." In the recordHerald, 1 Mar 2013
19 March 2013SGA passed a resolution opposing the $150 Study Abroad application fee. The senate passed a resolution opposing a new $150 application fee for Study Abroad and Global Learning, set to begin with summer 2013 programs, arguing it could put program costs out of reach; the University Senate passed a similar resolution. A separate amendment proposed by Dodds to make SGA members ineligible for SGA-awarded Study Abroad scholarships failed. Dodds said 11 of the 125 such scholarships and grants that year had gone to SGA members, which he called a conflict of interest. In the recordHerald, 19 Mar 2013
27 March 2013Executive candidates debate ahead of spring election. Outgoing President Cory Dodds opened a candidates' debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium by describing to the audience how much influence the students elected to SGA's executive positions would actually have on WKU's campus, ahead of the election that would choose his successor. In the recordHerald, 29 Mar 2013
4 April 2013Boka, Reeves and Seay won the spring executive elections. Executive vice president Keyana Boka was elected 2013-14 SGA president with 626 votes, 47 percent, over administrative vice president Cain Alvey with 419 votes and Austin Wingate with 300. Mark Reeves won executive vice president with 632 votes, 57 percent, over Brad Cockrel, and Nicki Seay ran unopposed for administrative vice president. Twenty-six student senators were also elected. In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2013
9 April 2013Judicial Council disqualified president-elect Boka, 3-2. In an emergency meeting, SGA's Judicial Council voted 3-2 to disqualify president-elect Keyana Boka after runner-up and outgoing administrative vice president Cain Alvey complained that a self-promotional email had gone to Honors College students at Boka's request, sent by Honors College graduate assistant Destiny Savage, violating the election code. The disqualification would have made Alvey, who had placed second in the April 4 vote, the incoming president; Boka said she would appeal. In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2013
16 April 2013Judicial Council declined to contest Bailey's reinstatement of Boka. In an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council unanimously decided not to challenge Bailey's memorandum reinstating Boka, saying it did not believe it had the power to do so, while expressing official disapproval. Chief Justice Seth Church called the intervention "a serious infringement on our autonomy" and said it set a bad precedent. Boka said the council had conflicts of interest and needed to be held accountable by a neutral party in the administration. In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2013
16 April 2013Costa stepped down as speaker; Settles elected to succeed him. Christopher Costa did not seek another term as speaker of the senate, and senators elected Paige Settles to replace him. The same meeting confirmed presidential appointments Roy Ratliff as senator-at-large and Jackie Stewart as associate justice, with Chief of Staff Travis Taylor and public relations chair Mac Mullins giving reports. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2013
25 April 2013Senate opposed automatic athletic-fee increases ahead of C-USA move. The senate passed a resolution against the annual automatic increase in the student athletic fee, arguing the revenue-sharing WKU would gain on joining Conference USA that July would outweigh the roughly $40,000 the university lost annually in the Sun Belt. Executive vice president-elect Mark Reeves, who introduced it, said the resolution set a precedent against automatic fee increases generally. In the recordHerald, 26 Apr 2013

2013-14Keyanna Boka (president)

28 March 2013Presidential debate drew full field of candidates. Ahead of the spring 2013 election, outgoing president Cory Dodds opened a debate in Ransdell Hall Auditorium among presidential candidates Cain Alvey, Keyana Boka and Austin Wingate, plus executive vice presidential candidates Brad Cockrel and Mark Reeves and administrative vice presidential candidate Nicki Seay. Boka said SGA members needed better training in their roles, Alvey said the presidency's responsibilities went beyond the constitution, and Wingate, a former Speaker of the Senate, called for better representation across student groups. In the recordHerald, 28 Mar 2013
10 September 2013Executive Council floated plus/minus grading, set fall calendar. At the Executive Council's weekly meeting, Executive Vice President Mark Reeves reported that the University Senate Council had discussed reviving a plus/minus grading system and that Provost Gordon Emslie was interested in SGA's support. The council set a Nov. 9 Picnic with the President for the presidents' council and deans, and swore in Samantha Johnson to an executive cabinet seat vacated by the resignation of Keith Watson. In the recordSGA Executive Council minutes, 10 Sep 2013
11 September 2013SGA reviewed 24-hour dining, grading and registration proposals. SGA gave first read to a proposal for a 24-hour on-campus dining option, with the Organizational Aid Committee sponsoring the resolution and assistant vice president for auxiliary services Gary Meszaros set to attend the next meeting. Reeves told senators Provost Gordon Emslie was reviving a plus/minus grading proposal and had brought priority registration and major-declaration changes to University Senate. In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2013
12 September 2013Senate passed international student seat amendment. President Keyana Boka and executive vice president Mark Reeves authored a constitutional amendment adding a senate seat for Navitas or English as a Second Language international students. The Judicial Council had ruled an earlier version unconstitutional, but after a revision in an emergency meeting the Senate passed it with only two votes against. Boka said it would make WKU's SGA the first student government in the state with an international senate seat. In the recordHerald, 12 Sep 2013
19 September 2013Fall election drew 564 voters, created international seat. A total of 564 voters cast ballots in the fall SGA election. A referendum creating the Navitas/ESL international student senate seat passed with 310 of 426 votes, or 73 percent. Six freshman senators were elected out of seven candidates, with Jay Todd Richey taking 27 percent of the vote, and most college senate seats went to unopposed candidates. In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2013
10 October 2013SGA finalized $125,000 budget. SGA finalized a $125,000 budget for the 2013-14 year, funded from student tuition at about $6.25 per student, after a planned funding increase did not come through. The organizational aid committee was allotted $30,000, with campus organizations able to receive up to $500 each. The executive discretionary fund held $5,900, part of which covered a Washington, D.C. higher education lobbying trip by Boka and Reeves. In the recordHerald, 10 Oct 2013
31 October 2013Priority registration complaints spurred open forum. Student complaints over new two-tier priority registration rules, including a 16-credit-hour cap during the priority period, pushed SGA to schedule a Nov. 12 open forum with Provost Gordon Emslie. Honors College seniors told senator Tyler Scaff some were considering dropping the honors major over the change. Boka said she had no official stance yet, though SGA had earlier approved the change through Reeves's vote at University Senate. In the recordHerald, 31 Oct 2013
5 November 2013Herald editorial faulted SGA over registration policy. A Herald editorial accused SGA of failing to represent students on the new priority-registration hour cap, saying executive vice president Mark Reeves voted for the policy at University Senate on Sept. 10 without SGA questioning or debating it first. The editorial argued SGA had one job, representing students, and had not done it on this issue. In the recordHerald, 5 Nov 2013
7 November 2013Thompson Complex North Wing set to close permanently. Boka announced at the Tuesday SGA meeting that Thompson Complex North Wing, home to the biology and chemistry departments, would close permanently the next semester because the building could not be maintained over the winter. The building had been labeled for demolition since 2005, and its demolition along with renovation of the Center Wing was the university's top capital priority before the Kentucky General Assembly. In the recordHerald, 7 Nov 2013
3 December 2013Judicial Council voided Talisman fee stance reversal. After the yearbook's budget was cut to $127,000, senator Chris Costa moved at the Nov. 19 meeting to revoke SGA's stance supporting a $9 student fee for the Talisman that students had approved on a 2005 ballot, and two-thirds of SGA voted to reverse the stance. The Judicial Council ruled Costa's motion unconstitutional on Nov. 21, and also ruled the original 2005 policy unconstitutional because it was never passed according to SGA policy. Talisman editors then met with Boka and SGA members to discuss long-term funding options. In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2013
6 February 2014SGA reconvened, planned Frankfort rally against budget cuts. At the first spring meeting, Boka announced a planned trip to Frankfort called "Rally for Retention" in response to WKU's $1.8 million state budget cut, with speeches and one-on-one meetings with legislators. Reeves warned that tough budget cuts were coming, and the body reviewed a proposal to revise the change-of-major advising process. Five members had resigned the previous semester, leaving the legislative research and public relations chairs among the vacant seats. In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2014
13 February 2014Executive Council nullified judicial appointment amendment. An amendment stripping the SGA president's sole power to appoint judicial council justices and raising the number of justices to seven passed at the Tuesday meeting, over Boka's objection that it bypassed presidential appointment and the senate. After the meeting the Executive Council reviewed the constitution and determined too few senators had attended for the vote to count, sending the amendment back to first read. The SGA office also temporarily moved to Garrett after flooding in Cravens. In the recordHerald, 13 Feb 2014
26 February 2014Mid-year budget report showed $46,883 surplus. SGA's mid-year budget report showed a $46,883.62 surplus on its $125,000 budget. The Senate approved Bill 3-14-S allocating organizational funds and suspended its bylaws to pass Resolution 3-14-S supporting WKU's participation in the Campus Pride Index, and approved Hannah Neeper, Elizabeth Gribbins and AJ Stewart as new senators as six senate seats remained open. In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2014
May 2014Final meeting passed Good Samaritan resolution, funding bills. At the last meeting of the semester, Boka announced students would face a 4.8 percent tuition increase, about $209 more per semester for most, alongside a $4.2 million increase in student financial assistance. The Senate suspended its bylaws to pass a slate of bills funding Summer Term assistance, student organizations, student research and an Earth Week planting party. Resolution 6-14-S passed in support of adopting a Good Samaritan Policy protecting students who call 911 during drug or alcohol overdoses. In the recordHerald, 1 May 2014
