2014-15Nicki Taylor (president)

28 August 2014SGA opened the year with a $21,000 scholarship program. SGA began the year under new president Nicki Seay, a Crofton senior, working alongside Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler and Executive Vice President Nolan Miles. The association expanded its summer and winter term need-based scholarship program from the previous year's $6,000 to $21,000, funded in part by an anonymous donation. Seay named student involvement, retention and graduation her first priorities. In the recordHerald, 28 Aug 2014
2 September 2014Downing Student Union celebrated its community opening. WKU held a ceremonial community opening for Downing Student Union after a two-year, $49 million renovation; the building had opened to students the week before. Students paid $36 million of the cost through a $70-per-semester fee, and the renovation began as an SGA initiative in 2011. SGA President Nicki Seay attended alongside President Gary Ransdell and other officials. In the recordHerald, 2 Sep 2014
25 September 2014Fall election drew 742 voters and seated 17 senators. SGA announced its fall election results around 12:20 a.m. in the Senate Chamber of Downing Student Union. There were 742 voters and 17 senators were elected, including three freshman senators led by Emily Pride with 281 votes. President Nicki Seay called the election very competitive, noting not everyone who ran won a seat. In the recordHerald, 25 Sep 2014
15 October 2014Senate defeated a nonsectarian prayer policy resolution. After more than 20 minutes of debate, the senate defeated Resolution 4-14-F, which would have supported adopting the University Senate's nonsectarian public prayer policy for university-sponsored events. President Nicki Taylor said the senate was split three ways among nonsectarian prayer, sectarian prayer and no prayer at all. The same night, senators passed Bill 9-14-F allocating $250 in organizational aid to the Phi Gamma Delta fraternity. In the recordHerald, 15 Oct 2014
20 November 2014Executive Cabinet vetoed the smoke-free campus resolution. The senate passed Resolution 11-14-F, supporting a smoke-free campus, on a 14-10 vote, but the SGA Executive Cabinet vetoed it after the meeting. Chief of Staff Seth Church argued it was unfair to ban smoking for students required to live on campus for two years. Senators retained the power to override the veto with a two-thirds vote. In the recordHerald, 20 Nov 2014
4 December 2014Veto override failed; alcohol policy resolution passed. At the final meeting of the fall semester, the senate failed to overturn the Executive Cabinet's veto of the smoke-free resolution, and President Nicki Taylor read the cabinet's official veto statement citing enforcement, housing requirements and practicality. The senate then passed Resolution 13-14-F, supporting amendments to WKU's alcohol policy and Student Code of Conduct to let students 21 and older purchase and possess alcohol on campus. Co-author Jody Dahmer called the existing policy ineffective and hard to enforce fairly. In the recordHerald, 4 Dec 2014
14 December 2014President Taylor addressed December graduates. SGA President Nicki Taylor spoke at WKU's December commencement, telling graduates to celebrate what they had accomplished: "You have the rest of your life to look forward to." She had opened the year in August under her previous surname, Seay, and was going by Taylor in Herald coverage by mid-October. In the recordHerald, 14 Dec 2014
3 February 2015Limited smoking campus resolution passed 13-11. SGA passed Resolution 1-15-S, supporting a limited smoking campus, by a 13-11 vote. The resolution would restrict tobacco use to 39 designated areas that the Administrative Council would gradually phase out over three years, while leaving electronic cigarettes and smokeless tobacco unrestricted. Co-author Seth Church said it was roughly the fifth version of the resolution since the smoking debate began the previous semester. In the recordHerald, 3 Feb 2015
4 February 2015President Taylor abstained on smoking vote as a sitting regent. The Bowling Green Daily News reported that Nicki Taylor, in addition to serving as SGA president, sat on the WKU Board of Regents, and abstained from an Executive Council vote on the smoking-campus proposal because of that seat. In the recordBowling Green Daily News, 4 Feb 2015
3 March 2015SGA backed a $10 million parking garage funded by a $30 fee. SGA passed a resolution supporting construction of a new parking structure on part of Creason Lot, funded by a $30-per-semester tuition increase. Authors Zach Jones, Brian Chism and Nathan Cherry estimated the roughly 500-car garage would take about 18 months to build. Chief of Staff Seth Church objected that the plan was rushed and left out regional campuses. In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2015
4 March 2015Ransdell formally responded to four SGA resolutions. President Gary Ransdell emailed faculty and staff his official response to four SGA resolutions on limited smoking, campus alcohol sales, a new parking structure and a student fee for WKU Student Legal Services. He announced a six-person ad hoc committee to implement a limited smoking campus by the end of 2017 and a restaurant in the Garrett Conference Center that could serve beer in the evenings. He said the parking and legal services fees would need Board of Regents and Council on Postsecondary Education approval. In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2015
2 April 2015Jay Todd Richey won the SGA presidency, 874 votes to 524. Jay Todd Richey defeated senator Brian Chism for SGA president, 63 percent to 37 percent, or 874 votes to 524, with results announced about 20 minutes after TopNet polls closed at 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. Nolan Miles ran unopposed for a second term as executive vice president, and Liz Koehler won the administrative vice president race with 66 percent over J. William Berry. Twenty of 34 senatorial candidates won seats. In the recordHerald, 2 Apr 2015
16 April 2015An election result challenged and upheld. Anonymous accusations alleged Jay Todd Richey had breached election codes on poster placement. The judicial council warned him against future violations and confirmed he had rightfully won. In the recordHerald, April 2015

2015-16Jay Todd Richey (president)

27 August 2015Richey outlined fall goals, MyCampusToo launch. Opening his first term, President Jay Todd Richey said he wanted more executive-cabinet and senate communication and more outreach to international students and regional campuses, and confirmed his campaign initiative MyCampusToo would launch that semester. Executive Vice President Nolan Miles said he would push senators to sit on university committees and revive the Dine with Decision Makers event. In the recordHerald, 27 Aug 2015
15 September 2015SGA budget fell by $19,500. SGA's budget dropped $19,500 from the previous year, largely because a $15,000 private donation was not repeated and the university cut another $4,500 in reallocations. Organizational funding took the hardest hit, losing $9,000, and scholarship pools for Academic Affairs and Student Affairs each fell by more than $5,000. Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reallocated $4,000 from organizational aid back into scholarships to soften the loss. In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2015
22 September 2015Senate voted to disapprove Confucius Institute approval process. The Student Senate voted overwhelmingly to pass a resolution disapproving of how the Confucius Institute building project was approved, after President Gary Ransdell signed the contract in China in December 2014 and the Board of Regents, including the Student Regent, voted on it more than a month later without full details disclosed. Richey said the vote was not meant to set a precedent beyond ensuring the Board had full information before acting. In the recordHerald, 24 Sep 2015
18 November 2015Senate backed meningitis vaccine requirement, amended bylaws. The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 6-15-F supporting a meningococcal meningitis vaccination requirement for incoming freshmen in on-campus housing beginning with the class of 2020, and unanimously passed Bill 10-15-F amending SGA's bylaws. Richey reported that his fall listening tours of the regional campuses had gone well and turned up how different those campuses were from main campus. In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2015
3 December 2015Chief Justice resigned after censure hearing backlash. The Judicial Council unanimously declined to censure senator John Winstead, whom it had investigated over an "impeach Ransdell" sign and a mocking Facebook post about President Ransdell, ruling his actions were protected free speech. Winstead called the fact he was investigated at all "the problem I'm objecting to." Chief Justice Kelsey Luttrell then announced she would step down at the end of the semester, saying the council had been publicly ridiculed and lacked support from fellow SGA members. In the recordHerald, 3 Dec 2015
28 January 2016Administration overrode student vote on pub name. Richey announced that administrators had renamed the future Garrett Conference Center pub "Topper Grill and Pub," setting aside the name students chose in SGA's "Dub the Pub" contest, Topper Tavern. Richey said Ransdell wanted to downplay the alcohol theme and called himself "very disappointed," saying the move made SGA question how much the administration listened to students. At the same meeting SGA introduced the RAVE Guardian campus safety app. In the recordHerald, 28 Jan 2016
2 February 2016Ransdell announced retirement amid state budget cuts. President Gary Ransdell announced he would step down as WKU's ninth president on June 30, 2017, triggering a presidential search. The announcement came the same week new Gov. Matt Bevin ordered an immediate 4.5 percent cut to WKU's state funding and proposed a 9 percent cut, with future funding shifted to a performance-based pool. The changes framed much of SGA's advocacy for the rest of the year. In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2016
17 February 2016Senate opposed state tuition-freeze bill. The senate approved Resolution 2-16-S opposing Kentucky Senate Bill 75, which would have frozen resident tuition at 2015-16 levels for four years. Richey argued such freezes were "dangerous risks" that could wreck universities and cost students more in the long run. At the same meeting, Administrative Vice President Liz Koehler reported an expected 4.5 percent cut to SGA's own budget, about $1,301. In the recordHerald, 17 Feb 2016
24 February 2016Senators lobbied legislators in Frankfort. SGA members traveled to Frankfort to lobby against state budget cuts that could slash WKU funding by as much as 9 percent, meeting with eight state officials. Senators pressed for smaller cuts and restoration of need-based aid, citing figures that about 15,000 students were denied need-based financial aid the prior year. Both chambers of the General Assembly recognized SGA for its participation. In the recordHerald, 24 Feb 2016
2 March 2016Ransdell declined SGA's meningitis vaccine mandate. Richey read aloud a letter from Ransdell responding to Resolution 6-15-F, passed the previous semester, which supported requiring meningitis vaccinations for incoming freshmen living on campus starting with the class of 2020. Ransdell wrote that the university would highly recommend vaccination but "stop short of requiring it," citing a $143.77 cost for uninsured students at the Graves-Gilbert Clinic. In the recordHerald, 2 Mar 2016
6 April 2016Senate passed guidelines for WKU's tenth president. The senate approved a resolution by John Winstead and Richey outlining what students wanted in WKU's tenth president, which Richey planned to use in his role on the presidential search committee. After debate, senators amended the sustainability clause to target improving WKU's AASHE STARS rating and voted to remove language about Jonesville "reparations" entirely, after disputing whether reparations or restitution was the right term. In the recordHerald, 6 Apr 2016
20 April 2016Richey reelected in one of highest-turnout elections. Students reelected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president with 64 percent of the vote over Braxton Powell, in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history with 2,442 voters. Kate Hart, an Academic Affairs chairwoman and Richey's running mate, won executive vice president. Richey called the win "verification of promises kept." In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016

2016-17Jay Todd Richey (president)

20 April 2016Richey re-elected SGA president in high-turnout election. WKU students re-elected Jay Todd Richey as SGA president and elected Kate Hart as executive vice president in one of the highest-turnout elections in the association's history, with 2,442 voters. Richey defeated opponent Braxton Powell with 64 percent of the overall vote. Powell was elected a junior senator and his running mate Zach Jones a senior senator. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2016
12 September 2016Ransdell condemns racist incidents after notes, vandalism. In the weeks before, racist notes had been left in a WKU assistant dean's office and a racial slur was scratched into a student's car following a parking dispute. President Gary Ransdell called the acts "cowardly" and "heinous," said they did not reflect the university's values, and called for campus dialogue on intolerance. In the recordWKMS, 12 Sep 2016
13 September 2016Senators raise campus racism at first fall meeting. At the third meeting of the 15th Senate, student speakers Jeb Veeck, Francisco Serrano and Spencer Wells addressed the recent racist incidents on campus. Veeck suggested a Q&A session on the issue and Serrano urged senators to help end racism on campus. In the recordSGA Senate minutes, 13 Sep 2016Read it here
12 October 2016Two SGA members resign amid racism complaint; investigation nullified. After Chief Justice Cody Cox told the Oct. 11 senate meeting he had received a complaint that several SGA members made racist remarks, senator Braxton Powell and justice John McKinney resigned the next morning, citing scheduling conflicts and personal reasons respectively; neither confirmed, denied, nor acknowledged any link between the resignations and the complaint. The Judicial Council's planned investigation was dropped because the students in question had already left SGA, and the organization never released the identities of the accused or the nature of the alleged remarks. President Richey and MyCampusToo chair Helen Vickrey issued a statement the next day condemning the alleged acts. In the recordHerald, 17 Oct 2016
26 October 2016Senate rejected 2.0 GPA bill, backed housing diversity. SGA rejected a bill that would have let students vote to lower the organization's GPA requirement from 2.5 to 2.0, a change supporters said would make the body more representative; a Twitter poll found 61 percent of respondents opposed it. The senate also approved a resolution asking Housing and Residence Life to address the lack of diversity in on-campus housing under the university's 10-year housing plan. In the recordHerald, 26 Oct 2016
30 November 2016SGA created Jonesville scholarship fund. The senate created a scholarship memorializing Jonesville, the African American community founded by freed slaves in the 1870s that stood on land now occupied by Smith Stadium, Nick Denes Field and Downing Student Union until WKU bought and demolished it in the late 1960s. Senators debated whether the award should go only to African American students as repayment for Jonesville's condemnation or be opened to all minority students. In the recordHerald, 30 Nov 2016
12 April 2017SGA backed prioritizing faculty raises over construction. The senate passed a resolution supporting future faculty salary increases, written to mirror a concurrent resolution headed to the Faculty Senate and proposed by Administrative Vice President Hannah Neeper and Chief of Staff James Line. The resolution urged that salary increases be prioritized over future construction or renovation projects, citing WKU's second-to-last ranking in faculty pay among its 19 benchmark institutions in 2015 and a survey in which 57 percent of faculty rated their morale as poor or very poor. In the recordHerald, 12 Apr 2017
18 April 2017Resolution 6-17-S passes 19-10-1. Senators Andrea Ambam and Brian Anderson wrote a resolution supporting reparations for Black students, calling for full and free access to WKU for all Black people and asking for a task force on test-optional and geographically weighted admissions. Modelled on a resolution passed at Wisconsin-Madison earlier that year. In the recordDaily News, Apr 2017 (archived copy)Read it here
19 April 2017Andi Dahmer elected to succeed Richey. Louisville sophomore Andi Dahmer, a senator and chair of the MyCampusToo committee, was elected the next student body president, winning 930 of 1,579 votes cast against Kenan Mujkanovic's 305 and Lily Nellans's 212. Her running mates Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry won executive vice president and administrative vice president. Dahmer said she would start with legislation on study abroad affordability and sensitivity training to improve retention among marginalized groups. In the recordHerald, 19 Apr 2017
21 April 2017President Ransdell rejects the resolution. National wire coverage followed, along with a Tucker Carlson interview with Ambam and a wave of fabricated headlines claiming WKU had granted free tuition. Ransdell stated within days that it was not a university position. Both authors described it as a conversation starter. In the recordFactCheck.org

2017-18Andi Dahmer (president)

17 August 2017Dahmer joined national solidarity letter after Charlottesville. President Andi Dahmer was one of more than 120 college student body presidents nationwide who signed an open letter backing the University of Virginia after the violent Charlottesville protests, and said developing campus-wide "cultural competency training" was a goal for the semester. In the recordHerald, 17 Aug 2017
31 August 2017First senate meeting passes constitutional amendments. SGA held its first senate meeting of the year and approved three of five proposed constitutional amendment bills, which then went to the student body for a vote in the fall elections. The passed bills added constitutional review duties to the Judicial Council, made the chief justice backup speaker of the senate, and required senators to post one office hour per week. Senators also debated Bill 5-17-F, which proposed limiting the legislative powers of the executive branch. In the recordHerald, 31 Aug 2017
26 September 2017Senate passed a required sexual assault education resolution, 29-1. Resolution 1-17-F, co-authored by public relations chair William Hurst, S.A.V.E.S. chair Ashlyn Jones and three senators, supported adding a one-credit-hour sexual assault education course to freshman colonnade requirements, arguing existing options like HAVEN and Green Dot carried no penalty for skipping them. The senate also funded a "No-Shave November" beard contest and fixed the timing of constitutional-amendment elections in the bylaws. In the recordHerald, 28 Sep 2017
24 October 2017Dahmer condemned a blackface Halloween incident at senate meeting. President Andi Dahmer opened the eighth meeting of the Senate by telling members that a student had worn blackface to a Halloween party the previous weekend and that it was not acceptable. She also hosted student body presidents from other Kentucky universities on campus that weekend and reminded senators that Herald reporters were allowed into all university committee meetings. In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 24 Oct 2017Read it here
9 November 2017SGA passes resolution supporting DACA students. At its Nov. 7 meeting the senate passed a resolution, co-authored by President Andi Dahmer and Francisco Serrano, standing in solidarity with WKU students who were DACA recipients. The measure passed 32-1 and was a revision of the clean DREAM Act resolution rejected the previous week, reframed to address only the WKU student community. Dahmer noted WKU was one of the last Kentucky schools to pass something of this nature. In the recordHerald, 9 Nov 2017
29 January 2018Judicial Council censured PR committee chair over election-discrepancy complaint. At an emergency meeting, the Judicial Council took up a complaint public relations committee chair Will Hurst had raised at the Jan. 23 senate meeting, alleging the executive board failed its constitutional duty to advertise the fall election and citing a discrepancy in vote totals between constitutional amendments that passed and failed. The council found the executive board had complied with the constitution and issued a censure against Hurst; Dahmer said she was pleased the council had upheld the board's conduct. The censure was confirmed at the Feb. 6 senate meeting. In the recordHerald, 29 Jan 2018
7 February 2018SGA members rally in Frankfort for higher education. About 20 WKU SGA members joined roughly 100 students from Kentucky's public universities at the Kentucky Board of Student Body Presidents' annual Rally for Higher Education on the Capitol steps in Frankfort on Feb. 6. Dahmer said the board of student body presidents had been working consistently since August to plan the rally. In the recordHerald, 7 Feb 2018
13 February 2018Senate backed LGBTQ health curriculum, chair swap on Diversity committee. The senate unanimously passed a resolution supporting integrated LGBTQ health curriculum in WKU's medical education programs, co-authored by diversity and inclusion chair Mark Clark, chief of staff Conner Hounshell and administrative vice president Kara Lowry. Clark was approved as the committee's new chair after Corey Newsome stepped down over scheduling conflicts. In the recordHerald, 14 Feb 2018
3 April 2018Dahmer announced she would not seek reelection. Citing tension in the senate that she called "almost toxic in nature" and that she attributed to partisan ideology in a body meant to be nonpartisan, Dahmer said in a Facebook post she would not run again and endorsed Conner Hounshell for president alongside Savannah Molyneaux and Kara Lowry, seeking reelection to their executive vice president and administrative vice president seats. In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018
4 April 2018LGBTQ activists address senate after senator's remarks. Several LGBTQ student activists spoke to the senate on April 3 after Senator Dallas McKinney had cited the Bible on March 27, reading verses saying the "wicked" deserved death, as his reason for voting against Bill 13-18-S, which funded $250 for stoles for the Lavender Recognition Ceremony honoring LGBTQ graduates. The bill passed in the senate, and speakers including SGA member Brigid Stakelum and Diversity and Inclusion Committee Chair Mark Clark called the remarks dehumanizing and discriminatory. In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2018
18 April 2018Mayer wins presidency after disqualification reversed. Stephen Mayer was elected SGA president and student regent, with Garrett Edmonds as executive vice president and Harper Anderson as administrative vice president. Their MEA ticket had been disqualified on April 16 after a complaint over a Pepe the Frog meme in a campaign chalk drawing, but the Judicial Council reversed the disqualification to a suspension before results were announced. Mayer won 35 percent of the 2,378 votes cast in the presidential race, ahead of Conner Hounshell with 33 percent and Kenan Mujkanovic with 32 percent. In the recordHerald, 18 Apr 2018
24 April 2018Dahmer details months of harassment. In a Herald investigation, Dahmer said members of SGA had cursed at her, called her derogatory names and exchanged group messages in a GroupMe called the "Justice Friends" wishing her harm over the fall and spring semesters, and that a profane note left on her car on Feb. 9 led her to file a WKU police report and avoid her residence hall for two weeks. Her case was reported to WKU's Title IX office, which told her the conduct did not meet the legal standard for harassment, and it was processed instead by the Office of Student Conduct, which issued no-contact orders against two senators. In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2018
May 2018Caboni announced Title IX review after Dahmer harassment report. University president Timothy Caboni said he would convene a faculty-staff-student committee, co-chaired by sociology professor Lauren McClain and counseling official Karl Laves, to review WKU's Title IX, Equal Employment Opportunity and Office of Student Conduct processes following the Herald's report on the harassment Dahmer said she experienced. President-elect Stephen Mayer called Dahmer "a super strong woman" and said he did not stand for harassment or sexual assault. In the recordHerald, 1 May 2018

2018-19Stephen Mayer (president)

11 September 2018Senate rejected first Judicial Council nominee of the term. The senate voted 8-7-1 against confirming Wood Brown, a Pike fraternity member and law clerk, as associate justice of the Judicial Council, after Mayer said his constitutional duty required him to appoint whom he judged best despite recusing himself from the interview process; senators argued the Judicial Council's own top-ranked applicant, not Brown, should have been chosen. Mayer's next nominee, Alex Rivera, was confirmed the following week. In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 11 Sep 2018
20 September 2018Senate asked WKU to cancel classes on Election Day. SGA unanimously passed Resolution 5-18-F asking the university to cancel classes on Nov. 6, 2018, so students could get to the polls, after a presentation by Francis Wilson of the get-out-the-vote campaign Reg 2 Vote, and approved $300 in support through Bill 7-18-F. The senate also passed Resolutions 1-18-F and 2-18-F, which asked WKU to strike code-of-conduct language barring students from refusing a direction from a university official and from audio recording student-faculty meetings. Mayer's nominee Alex Rivera was confirmed as associate justice of the Judicial Council 12-3 after an earlier nomination had failed. In the recordHerald, 20 Sep 2018
25 September 2018Academic and Student Affairs directorship filled after two failed tries. The senate confirmed Aubrey Kelly as Director of Academic and Student Affairs 24-3-4, three weeks into the term. Initial nominee Ashley Cox was not confirmed at the first meeting after senators questioned her committee attendance, then withdrew when a family member was hospitalized; her replacement, Anna McAvoy, failed confirmation 6-9-1 on Sept. 11 after a senator raised concerns about her scholarship-grading experience. In the recordSGA Senate meeting minutes, 25 Sep 2018
26 September 2018First Year Village housing plan presented to SGA. Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds presented plans for a freshman First Year Village of two new pod-style residence halls at the bottom of the Hill, replacing Bemis Lawrence and Barnes-Campbell halls on the site of the Pearce-Ford Tower parking lot. The senate also approved Bill 6-18-F, funding a sustainability film festival, by a 21-4 vote with one abstention. In the recordHerald, 26 Sep 2018
24 October 2018SGA created a first-generation student scholarship. The senate passed a bill by Campus Improvements Chair Matt Barr creating a recurring $2,000 scholarship for first-generation college students, approved 31-1. It also passed organizational aid Bill 11-18-F, sending $1,400 to Delta Sigma Theta, Phi Beta Sigma and the jump rope club, and allocated $100 to advertise the Campus Safety Walk. In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2018
6 December 2018Contested appointment and Identity Evropa denouncement ended the fall term. President Stephen Mayer's nomination of graduate student Emily Anne Pride, daughter of a former SGA adviser, to a vacated senate seat sparked about 90 minutes of debate before she was confirmed 17-9 with two abstentions. The senate then passed Resolution 10-18-F, supporting denouncement of the white nationalist group Identity Evropa and its attempts to recruit on campus, 28-0, and allocated $430 to the Black Leadership Academic Conference through Bill 24-18-F. In the recordHerald, 6 Dec 2018
27 February 2019Resolution passed to relocate Confederate marker. After lengthy debate, the senate passed Resolution 1-19-S by a 29-1 vote with one abstention, calling for the marker near the Kentucky Museum identifying Bowling Green as the Confederate capital of Kentucky to be relocated to a display inside the museum. Authors Kara Lowry, Conner Hounshell and Symone Whalin argued the marker was a reminder of oppression against people of color, and Mayer said the resolution would go to the WKU Administrative Council. The senate also allocated $1,000 to send the Mock Trial team to a national tournament. In the recordHerald, 27 Feb 2019
27 March 2019Mayer declined to seek re-election as election codes were set. Mayer announced he would not seek re-election because he was applying to medical schools, and the senate approved the spring 2019 election codes 31-1, with campaigning to begin April 1 and voting on TopNet April 15-16. Chief Justice Jacob McAndrews announced he would resign from the Judicial Council to run for elected office. The senate also passed four spending bills, rejected a change to senator office-hour rules and tabled a bill creating a first-generation senate seat. In the recordHerald, 27 Mar 2019
3 April 2019Transparency resolution passed after the dean's resignation. A week after Snyder's sudden resignation, the senate passed Resolution 4-19-S by a 30-2 vote, calling on top university officials to provide explanations for major decisions. In the same meeting it rejected Mayer's Judicial Council nominee Wood Brown 17-11, created a senate seat for first-generation college students 33-0, and passed a resolution 33-0 asking WKU to let students' preferred names appear on class rosters, IDs and email addresses, a measure brought by the Transgender Non-Binary student organization. In the recordHerald, 3 Apr 2019
9 April 2019No-confidence vote and provost's resignation shook the university. After Snyder was asked to resign as Potter College dean on March 26, protests from faculty, staff and students led the University Senate to an unprecedented vote of no confidence in Provost Terry Ballman on April 4, and she resigned the next day. Ogden dean Cheryl Stevens was named acting provost, and days later the Comprehensive Academic Program Evaluation committee recommended suspending 101 of WKU's 380 academic programs. In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2019
17 April 2019WGK ticket won the spring executive elections. The ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, defeating the ticket of Asha McWilliams, Jacob McAndrews and Symone Whalin. Harris was elected student body president to succeed Mayer, Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president, and Mujkanovic defeated Whalin for administrative vice president, with results announced at SGA's election party on April 16. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2019

2019-20Will Harris (president)

17 April 2019Harris-led WGK ticket wins SGA executive election. The WGK ticket of Will Harris, Garrett Edmonds and Kenan Mujkanovic won the spring SGA elections, with Harris defeating Asha McWilliams for student body president. Edmonds was re-elected to a second term as executive vice president and Mujkanovic defeated Symone Whalin for administrative vice president. Results were announced at SGA's election party, with the new officers set to take office at the annual banquet; the Herald's results story reported no turnout figures. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2019
4 September 2019First meeting of the year confirms five executive appointments. At its first official meeting of the semester, the senate confirmed all five of President Will Harris's executive branch nominees: Aubrey Kelley as chief of staff, Ashlynn Evans as chief of public relations, Abbey Norvell as director of academic and student affairs, Paul Brosky as director of information technology and Josh Zaczek as Legislative Research Committee chair. Appointees outlined plans including wider use of counseling center fee vouchers and a revival of the need-based Earn-a-Computer program. In the recordHerald, 4 Sep 2019
11 September 2019Senate blocks budget over special projects fund. The senate refused to pass the year's budget over a $6,500 special projects fund the executive branch wanted for a sand volleyball court and hammock space at the First Year Village green space. Senators including Anthony Survance objected that the allocation cut into scholarship money, with Survance calling the motion "slimy", and the senate voted to keep $3,000 in its discretionary fund and $35,000 in scholarships. The executive branch pulled the budget, forcing a week's wait before a revised version could be voted on. In the recordHerald, 11 Sep 2019
19 September 2019Budget passes unanimously with spending stipulations. All 13 senators approved the yearly budget after a compromise added stipulations restricting the special projects fund to the First Year Village plans and redistributing any money unspent by March 3 back to discretionary and voucher funds. The budget's passage let Bills 1-19-F (Greeks Go Green) and 2-19-F (funding for Bowling Green Pride) pass unanimously. The senate also amended its election codes to halve campaign spending maximums, which had been $300 for presidential candidates, $125 for vice presidential candidates and $50 for senate candidates. In the recordHerald, 19 Sep 2019
24 October 2019Senate passes Resolution 4-19-F against Alpha Xi Delta. The senate voted 24-7 to pass Resolution 4-19-F, authored by senators Symone Whalin and Anthony Survance, supporting disciplinary action up to suspension from Greek affairs against the Epsilon Kappa chapter of Alpha Xi Delta. The resolution followed an August Twitter video showing AXiD members singing a racial slur in a rap song, and the authors said administrative silence signaled the university did not care about minority students. Before passage the senate amended the title to drop a call for outright removal from campus. In the recordHerald, 24 Oct 2019
30 October 2019Executive board veto of Resolution 4-19-F upheld. The executive board vetoed Resolution 4-19-F by a 4-0 vote with two abstentions, and the senate confirmed the veto at its Tuesday meeting. President Will Harris, one of the abstainers, said the resolution's discrimination claim would have to come from the Student Code of Conduct and no violation had been noted by the Office of Student Conduct, while co-author Anthony Survance accused the executive branch of dragging the issue out. Senators also raised Harris's connection to Alpha Xi Delta as one of its knights, which he rejected as grounds for bias. In the recordHerald, 30 Oct 2019
12 February 2020Go With the Flow feminine hygiene bill passes unanimously. Bill 1-20-S, funding the Go With the Flow program that supplies feminine hygiene products in campus restrooms, passed the senate unanimously. The bill, carried forward by Campus Improvement Chair Matthew Barr, doubled the program's budget from $588, and a floor amendment from Senator Symone Whalin raised the final amount to $1,300 from senate discretionary funds. Products were to be placed in Grise Hall, DSU, Preston Center, Gary Ransdell Hall and Snell Hall, including gender neutral bathrooms. In the recordHerald, 12 Feb 2020
4 March 2020Senate approves $5,000 hammocks project. The senate voted to pass Bill 3-20-S, allocating $5,000 from the special projects fund to begin planning hammock poles across campus, after the sand volleyball court proposed earlier in the year was deemed too expensive. Planned locations included spots near most residence halls and the Valley, and Executive Vice President Garrett Edmonds said he and Harris ran so SGA would be known for more than "scantrons and greenbooks". Legislative Research Chair Josh Zaczek criticized having to vote without seeing budget numbers, and the senate retained power to halt spending during planning. In the recordHerald, 4 Mar 2020
11 March 2020WKU extends spring break, moves classes online amid COVID-19. WKU announced it would extend spring break by one week and transition to "alternative delivery formats" for classes amid growing coronavirus concerns, with President Tim Caboni recommending that students who could safely return home do so. The announcement came after the University of Kentucky and University of Louisville suspended in-person classes. In-person instruction never resumed that semester, upending the rest of SGA's spring calendar. In the recordHerald, 11 Mar 2020
20 April 2020Spring elections postponed until fall as SGA moves to Zoom. With campus closed by COVID-19, SGA postponed its spring elections until at least September so voting could happen in person, and added an "emergency clause" constitutional amendment allowing cabinet terms to be extended until the following election with judicial oversight. The cabinet continued meeting over Zoom every Tuesday. Harris said that after scholarships were awarded, the remainder of SGA's budget would be donated to the WKU Opportunity Fund and Emergency Relief Fund, and SGA gave its remaining food bank goods to the Office of Sustainability for redistribution. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2020

2020-21J. Garrett Edmonds (president)

24 September 2020Town hall debate pitted the sitting EVP against a senator. SGA held a town hall debate in the DSU auditorium between presidential candidates Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, and senator MJ Mayo. Edmonds's original running mate for administrative vice president, Nathan Terrell, had dropped off the Edmonds-Norvell ticket and was replaced by Abbey Norvell; the debate covered WKU's COVID-19 response and the summer's Black Lives Matter protests on campus. In the recordWKU Talisman, Voter's Guide, 28 Sep 2020
29 September 2020Edmonds elected president over Mayo. Garrett Edmonds, the sitting executive vice president, was elected student body president over senator MJ Mayo in balloting held on TopNet Sept. 28-29, succeeding Will Harris. Edmonds had campaigned on creating a Director of Outreach position to link campus organizations more directly with SGA. In the recordHerald, 6 Oct 2020
30 September 2020Norvell elected administrative vice president; EVP still open. SGA held a virtual election party over Zoom to announce results. The Edmonds-Norvell ticket defeated MJ Mayo for the presidency, and Abbey Norvell was elected administrative vice president alongside Edmonds. The Herald reported no official decision had yet been made on a separate executive vice president post, with an announcement expected at the next SGA meeting. In the recordHerald, 30 Sep 2020
7 October 2020Senate passed the annual budget 28-5 and elected Shelby Robertson speaker. At the first official senate meeting under the new leadership, Shelby Robertson defeated Brenna Matthews to become speaker of the senate and the budget passed 28-5. Edmonds emphasized a $6,000 Projects Fund, including $1,000 for Housing and Residence Life PPE and an expansion of the Go with the Flow menstrual products program into Pearce Ford Tower. Senator MJ Mayo challenged the balance of stipends; Edmonds said all senate stipends except the top three offices had been cut to feed the Projects Fund. In the recordHerald, 7 Oct 2020
13 October 2020Cabinet set office hours, an outreach committee, and pushed inclusive language. At the executive cabinet's first recorded meeting, Edmonds set up officer office hours and an ad hoc outreach committee for RSO leadership. Speaker Shelby Robertson pushed to connect senators with similar legislative interests, adopt inclusive pronoun language in the chamber, and find a parliamentarian. In the recordSGA Executive Cabinet minutes, 13 Oct 2020Read it here
21 October 2020Keller confirmed AVP 29-1; two new committee chairs elected. The senate confirmed Isaac Keller as administrative vice president 29-1 after Edmonds said he wanted a deputy willing to challenge him when they disagreed. Roderick Maul and Tess Welch were elected committee chairs, and senators voted to form a new Ad Hoc committee chaired by Me'Lon Craighead. In the recordHerald, 21 Oct 2020
11 November 2020Judicial nominations confirmed; senate revives a Pass/D/Fail request. The senate unanimously confirmed Edmonds's nominations of Derek Collins and Lexi Mayne as associate justices and Addison McCoun as senator at large. Senators passed a Tess Welch/Eric Barry bill to increase campus accessibility and split funding for SGA-branded masks and hand sanitizer between the senate and SGA's PR team. A closing bill by Tate McClard and Jacob Congleton, with every senator listed as a co-author, asked WKU to restore the Pass/D/Fail grading option it had offered in spring 2020 but declined to bring back that fall. In the recordHerald, 11 Nov 2020 (corrected)
16 November 2020Edmonds launched a P/D/F petition. President Garrett Edmonds released a student petition asking WKU to offer a Pass/D/Fail grading option for the fall semester, citing inconsistent course modalities and the strain of quarantine on students without an online-learning fallback. The petition reached half its 1,000-signature goal within an hour and the target was raised to 5,000. In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2020
18 November 2020Associate provost rebuffed SGA's P/D/F request; computers bill passes 28-3. Edmonds told senators that Associate Provost Rob Hale had defended the university's decision to extend the drop deadline rather than restore Pass/D/Fail grading, and said he was "deeply disturbed" by the response; senator Brenna Mathews argued the policy left students choosing between attending in person or paying for an extra semester. Edmonds urged senators to keep circulating his petition, which had passed 3,000 signatures, and the senate voted 28-3 to fund recycled computers for the SGA office, a number scaled back to meet CDC guidelines. In the recordHerald, 18 Nov 2020
December 2020WKU relented and allowed pass grades after SGA's P/D/F campaign. Provost Cheryl Stevens told faculty that students who faced COVID-related problems could opt for a pass grade instead of a B or C, reversing the university's earlier refusal. The Faculty Senate had voted 40-9 in favor and SGA voted unanimously for the option, presenting nearly 20 pages of student testimony; SGA's petition had drawn over 3,500 signatures in three days. Students had to email their professor by Jan. 13, with the final decision left to the faculty member. In the recordHerald, 1 Dec 2020
2 December 2020Fall semester closed with a safe-driving pledge and organization funding. At the last meeting of the fall semester, Edmonds thanked senators for the work that led to the new P/D/F option. Senators unanimously passed a Matthew Thomas bill committing SGA's social media to a "Drive Safe Hilltoppers" safety campaign, and unanimously funded a bill supporting HonorsToppers, College Republicans, Zeta Phi Beta and the Sociology and Criminology Club. In the recordHerald, 2 Dec 2020
20 January 2021Spring semester opened over Zoom with a late-fee pledge. At its first meeting of the spring semester, held on Zoom, SGA heard Edmonds say the provost search was in its final stage with interviews starting within weeks, and that he planned to look at changing or removing the late fees charged when a student's financial aid arrives late. Senators unanimously nominated Jamison Moorehead as director of IT and funded Dance Big Red and a Delta Sigma Pi virtual leadership conference. In the recordHerald, 20 Jan 2021
26 January 2021Committee chairs set spring priorities. Legislative Research Chair Dawson McCoun said the shift to remote meetings after March 2020 had made it harder to connect with students and pass legislation. Diversity and Inclusion Chair Fatin Yaro announced a Feb. 24 diversity event and legislation to set consequences for discrimination within student organizations, and Chief of Staff Matt Barr said he would continue the "Go with the Flow" program installing free menstrual-product dispensers on campus. SGA planned a return to masked, socially distanced in-person meetings that semester. In the recordHerald, 26 Jan 2021
2 February 2021Presidential task force sought input on slaveholding college namesakes. WKU's Presidential Task Force on Naming and Symbols, formed by President Timothy Caboni in fall 2020, collected input from students and the community on the namesakes of Potter College and Ogden College, both built on wealth from slave labor. Two Potter descendants said it was time to find a new name. The task force planned to audit names and send recommendations to the administration. In the recordHerald, 2 Feb 2021
3 February 2021New senator seated; rally with Gov. Beshear announced. SGA nominated pre-law sophomore Will Dykeman as a new senator and Edmonds announced a virtual Student Body President rally for March 26 featuring Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, with Edmonds working to add state Rep. Charles Booker. Senators unanimously funded a bill by AVP Isaac Keller supporting Amazing Tones of Joy, Black Women of Western, Queer Student Union and the Business Association for Development, and voted $2,500 for ISEC's Black Magic Masquerade Ball on a bill by Me'Lon Craighead. In the recordHerald, 3 Feb 2021
11 February 2021Outreach signage and safe-driving bills pass. Guest speaker Ethan Logan, vice president of enrollment and student experience, briefed senators on how his office could help SGA. Edmonds pointed senators toward an upcoming provost-search update and urged them to consider running in the April officer elections. Senators unanimously passed a Me'Lon Craighead bill funding 50 laminated, QR-coded outreach signs for campus and a Matthew Thomas bill adding 12 safe-driving signs to campus parking lots; a bill on WKU's Naming and Symbols Task Force was held for the following week. In the recordHerald, 11 Feb 2021
3 March 2021SGA backed renaming buildings tied to racism and funded a community garden. The senate passed legislation by Brenna Matthews and Tess Welch offering SGA's support to the Naming and Symbols Task Force in changing the names of WKU buildings with ties to racism or injustice. Matthews said ties to slave owning and the Confederate army did not belong on a campus committed to diversity. Senators also unanimously funded a community garden outside the Office of Sustainability and allocated $3,500 to four student organizations. In the recordHerald, 3 Mar 2021
18 March 2021Constitution amended; Caboni's contract extended. Edmonds told senators the WKU Board of Regents had extended President Timothy Caboni's contract four years. The senate elected Addison McCoun to head the Legislative Research Committee after Dawson McCoun's resignation, passed a Tess Welch/Erika Puhakka bill amending constitutional wording 19-4, and funded a Sustainability Committee spring photo contest on a bill by Matthew Waninger and Elizabeth DeLozier. In the recordHerald, 18 Mar 2021
31 March 2021Largest organizational aid bill passed; chief justice resigned before elections. Edmonds announced that Chief Justice Erika Puhakka had stepped down and declined to nominate a replacement so close to elections, and warned that only 13 people were running for senate. The senate passed its largest organizational aid bill ever, funding five student groups, and passed 16-0 with two abstentions a bill by Kyle Phillips asking WKU to support a codified vetting process for campus dining vendors after a controversial social media post by the owner of Lost River Pizza. In the recordHerald, 31 Mar 2021
May 2021Edmonds addressed the Class of 2021 at the delayed commencement. As SGA president, Edmonds spoke at WKU's Fall 2020/Spring 2021 commencement ceremony, telling graduates that the class's perseverance through the pandemic year had brought them to their day of celebration. In the recordWKU News - Class of 2021 Commencement

2021-22Matthew Wininger (president)

6 August 2021Northeast Hall renamed for Margaret Munday. Student Regent Matthew Wininger was sworn in at the Board of Regents meeting that renamed Northeast Hall for WKU's first African American student to enrol - the first building on campus named after an African American. In the recordWKU News
September 2021SGA opened the fall term with confirmations and new election codes. SGA held its first meeting of the fall semester, the second meeting of the 21st Senate, with President Matthew Wininger welcoming new and returning senators. All senators present were confirmed by unanimous consent and sworn in by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, along with executive appointments Jamison Moorehead as IT director, Alexis Courtenay as public relations director and Parker Raybourne as chief of staff. New election codes for the next semester also passed with unanimous consent. In the recordHerald, 1 Sep 2021
10 September 2021Senate confirmed the year's budget. At the third meeting of the 21st Senate on Sept. 7, SGA passed Bill 1.21f, confirming its budget for the year. Dean of Students Martha Sales spoke on leadership, and Wininger announced a planned donor drive in partnership with at least four other student organizations. Chief of Staff Parker Raybourne announced a Hilltopper Hangout event for Sept. 24. In the recordHerald, 10 Sep 2021
15 September 2021New senators seated and freshman election results announced. The senate unanimously voted in four new senate members, two judicial council members and Trib Singh as director of academic and student affairs. Speaker of the Senate Tess Welch introduced committees on legislative operations, student experience, mental health, sustainability, campus improvement, diversity and student outreach. That night the fall election results named Addison Falkner, Sam Kurtz and Jenna Wells freshman senators and Arivumani Srivastava the Gatton Academy senator. In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2021
6 October 202121st Senate passed its first resolution, on advisor evaluations. At its Oct. 5 meeting SGA passed Resolution 1.21f, addressing the lack of an advisor evaluation system, by a 21-2 vote, the first resolution of the 21st Senate. Bill 2.21f, barring the speaker of the senate from voting on legislation, passed 21-2, and two bills scrubbing outdated 2007-era bylaws passed by unanimous consent. Parking director Jennifer Tougas discussed a possible monthly parking tag subscription and campus bookstore operations. In the recordHerald, 6 Oct 2021
December 2021Resolution condemning critical race theory bans passed 16-15. After weeks of debate, the senate passed Resolution 7.21f, which condemned the banning of critical race theory teachings in postsecondary education ahead of an anticipated bill in the Kentucky legislature. The vote was 16 in favor, 15 against, with two abstentions. Sponsor Olivia Blackmon said the measure was meant to ensure intellectual freedom in the curriculum. In the recordHerald, 1 Dec 2021
12 December 2021EF-3 tornado struck Bowling Green, killing 11 in Warren County. An EF-3 tornado with 150 mph winds slammed into Bowling Green early on Dec. 11, killing 11 people according to the coroner and destroying homes and businesses across Warren County. Gov. Andy Beshear signed a state of emergency and President Biden signed an emergency declaration. The disaster shaped SGA relief efforts the following semester. In the recordHerald, 12 Dec 2021
18 January 2022First 2022 meeting funded tornado-drained food pantry. At its first meeting of 2022, SGA passed Bill 1.22s by unanimous consent, providing $1,000 to restock the WKU Office of Sustainability food pantry, whose food and toiletries had been drained by the tornado recovery effort. Wininger announced an initiative to create a student resource handbook for underclassmen. Speaker Tess Welch announced spring election dates of April 18-19. In the recordHerald, 18 Jan 2022
16 February 2022Syllabi clause, crosswalk resolutions and Title IX meetings passed. At its Feb. 15 meeting SGA unanimously passed Resolution 6-22-S to add an SGA-related clause to course syllabi, which the Herald reported would be the first of its kind in SGA history. Three resolutions supported new crosswalks below the Van Meter green space and on Chestnut and Normal streets, and Bill 6-22-S required a committee chair or delegate to meet with the Counseling Center director and Title IX coordinator each semester. The senate also approved a task force for the iWKU app and funding for a financial success workshop. In the recordHerald, 16 Feb 2022
14 April 2022Judiciary Council cleared Bornefeld's campaign over student-all email. After several SGA members complained that presidential candidate Cole Bornefeld's student-wide email about the Swipe Out Hunger initiative violated the election code's ban on self-promotion, the Judiciary Council held a roughly hour-long Zoom hearing on April 13 and voted in favor of his campaign. Speaker Tess Welch argued the signed email constituted self-promotion, while a statement from President Wininger, read by Chief Justice Holden Schroeder, said nothing in the code required executive approval for a student-all email. Senators said the initiative saw a record number of donations after the email went out. In the recordHerald, 14 Apr 2022
20 April 2022Cole Bornefeld elected with 49% of 1,448 votes. Alexis Courtenay took 40% and Olivia Feck 11%. Sam Kurtz and Garrison Reed were elected to the two vice presidencies. In the recordWKU News
20 April 2022End-of-year allocations funded scholarships, organizational aid and planetarium donation. Hours before the 2022 election results were announced, the senate passed a slate of funding bills: $8,000 in organizational aid at $500 per applicant, and $15,500 across five scholarship programs including summer class, study abroad, ISEC book and Scholar Level scholarships, plus $500 to Black Student Alliance scholarships for the first time. The senate also approved $325 for the Hardin Planetarium, $500 for a student worker appreciation event, $300 for the CEC Run/Walk for Autism and $570.02 for an e-waste recycling bin on main campus. In the recordHerald, 20 Apr 2022

2022-23Cole Bornefeld (president)

30 August 2022Executive retreat set the year's goals. SGA's executive team held a formal retreat dinner on Aug. 29 at the Cliff Todd Center to set its agenda for the year. President Cole Bornefeld said the group was building a one-stop resource guide for students and trying to promote SGA at WKU's regional campuses in Elizabethtown, Fort Knox, Glasgow, Owensboro and Somerset. Speaker Julie Mishchuk said the underlying goal of the year was financial assistance for students. In the recordHerald, 30 Aug 2022
31 August 2022WKU dedicated the Commons at Helm Library. WKU formally dedicated the $35 million Commons at Helm Library, a renovation funded through a partnership with Aramark, and President Timothy Caboni announced early plans for a similar makeover of Cherry Hall. SGA President Cole Bornefeld spoke at the ceremony, saying the building had been full of excitement and community since it opened. In the recordHerald, 31 Aug 2022
September 2022First meeting filled senate and cabinet vacancies. At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 30, the senate approved all of President Bornefeld's nominees, including Juan Thomas, Will Hemenover and Sydney Denney as senators-at-large, Aniya Johnson as director of information technology, Donte' Reed as director of enrollment and student experience, and Isaac Kind and Garrett Baum to the judicial council. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz spoke on the budget and Chief Justice Holden Schroeder swore in the new members. In the recordHerald, 1 Sep 2022
21 September 2022Fall election turnout doubled; Reed appointed to state council. Fall 2022 election results announced at midnight seated Rush Robinson, Callison Padgett and Rhett Helland as freshman senators, plus Neel Patel for Gatton Academy, Shy'Ante Williams as graduate senator and Salvador Leon Golib as international student senator. President Bornefeld said the vote total rose from 398 the previous fall to 805. SGA also announced that Vice President Garrison Reed had been appointed student representative on Kentucky's Council on Postsecondary Education, with a term running through June 30, 2023. In the recordHerald, 21 Sep 2022
25 January 2023Senate approved five nominations and reviewed a shrinking budget. The senate unanimously confirmed five nominations, including Adan Canizalez as chair of student enrollment and experience and Miles Huff, a track athlete, to the judicial council. Administrative Vice President Sam Kurtz urged senators to sponsor more resolutions, which use university funds, because only about $39,460.76 remained of SGA's $100,000 annual budget for bills. Speaker Julie Mishchuk floated a constitutional amendment requiring every senator to sponsor at least one bill or resolution. In the recordHerald, 25 Jan 2023
February 2023Voucher bills funded dental clinic, ID center and Preston Center. The senate unanimously passed Bill 28-23-S, putting $500 toward free teeth cleanings at the WKU Dental Health Clinic after voucher use rose 660 percent in the fall, and Bill 27-23-S, allocating $2,000 in discount vouchers split 60/30/10 among the Preston Center, the ID center and the dental hygiene clinic. A $260 bill funding a poetry mic night with the Talisman also passed with one nay vote. Former SGA President Matthew Wininger opened the meeting as guest speaker. In the recordHerald, 1 Feb 2023
15 February 2023Narcan resolution aimed to put overdose spray in residence halls. SGA unanimously passed Resolution 2-23-S on Feb. 7 supporting placement of Narcan, an opioid overdose reversal spray, in WKU residence halls. SGA had planned to spend about $1,000 of its own budget, but a University of Kentucky harm reduction specialist helped secure the product through a government grant instead. Housing and Residence Life planned to install the spray in AED-style boxes across its 15 dorms by Aug. 1 to allow time for staff training. In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2023
17 February 2023The Speaker takes the President to the Judicial Council. Speaker of the Senate Yulia 'Julie' Mishchuk requested a censure hearing against President Cole Bornefeld over anti-transgender posts he had liked on Instagram. Members of the Queer Student Union and both vice presidents attended. The Judicial Council voted unanimously against censure. In the recordHerald, Feb 2023
19 February 2023A Title IX report seeks the President's removal. Filed with Student Conduct. Under the constitution, removing an executive who will not resign requires written endorsement from at least 20% of the Senate, a wait of at least fourteen days and a two-thirds vote of the full Senate sitting as a court. In the recordHerald, March 2023
22 February 2023Menstrual product legislation passed as QSU protested. At its Feb. 21 meeting SGA passed a resolution supporting menstrual product dispensers on the first floor of every academic building, a $200 bill to distribute 35 menstrual cups at tabling events, and $100 for a community relations survey. Queer Student Union president Alistar Flowers announced QSU had removed SGA meetings from its list of campus safe spaces after the judicial council declined to censure President Bornefeld, and said QSU would not associate with SGA until a public apology was released. In the recordHerald, 22 Feb 2023
22 March 2023Election reform bill failed 19-15. Bill 39-23-S, which would have moved the transfer, non-traditional and first-generation senate seats to the fall election and required a two-thirds senate vote to convert vacant seats to at-large seats, failed 19-15, short of the two-thirds needed. Sponsor Neel Patel called the growing reliance on presidential appointments a dangerous practice for a government organization. The same meeting unanimously funded the April 3 Afro-Latinidad cultural event and rejected funding for Dance Big Red. In the recordHerald, 22 Mar 2023
13 April 2023Senate merged committees and funded Mental Health Awareness Week. At the April 11 meeting the senate passed Bill 44-23-S, a constitutional amendment merging the Community Relations and Outreach committees starting in 2023-24, which Speaker Mishchuk said would create a stronger committee amid low membership. Senators also unanimously funded a slate of Mental Health Awareness Week events for April 23 through 28, including an Out of the Darkness suicide prevention walk, and passed a $62 terrarium tabling bill. President Bornefeld reported 44 applicants for the upcoming SGA elections. In the recordHerald, 13 Apr 2023
19 April 2023Sam Kurtz elected on an unopposed ticket. With Salvador Leon as administrative vice president and Annalise Finch as executive vice president. In the recordHerald, April 2023
