2023-24Sam Kurtz (president)

30 August 202323rd Senate seats Judicial Council and committee heads. At its first meeting of the fall semester, SGA approved President Sam Kurtz's nominations of Ashley Ranger, Anna Kate Hardin, Ellen Henderson, Morgan Gammons and Garrison Reed to the 2023-2024 Judicial Council after what Kurtz called a record number of applicants. Kurtz also announced seven committee heads, including Rush Robinson for Campus Improvements and Sustainability and Karley Solorzano for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion. The new appointees took the oath of office at the meeting. In the recordHerald, 30 Aug 2023
20 September 2023First bill of the year funds the Pink Walk. The 23rd Senate passed its first piece of legislation, Bill 1-23-F, at its fifth meeting. The bill allocated $500 from SGA's scholarship budget for the SGA Pink Walk, an October breast cancer awareness event for students and the Bowling Green community. It passed unanimously with 28 votes. In the recordHerald, 20 Sep 2023
27 September 2023Fall election winners sworn in. SGA announced its fall election results on Sept. 20 over an Instagram livestream, electing Savanna Kurtz, Malick Ibrahim and Chloe Ralston as freshman senators, ShyAntye'e Williams as graduate senator, Sim Guan Zhou as international senator and Livi Ray as Gatton Academy senator. Five of the six were sworn in at the following Tuesday meeting. Sophomore senator Rush Robinson received the year's first Senator of the Month award. In the recordHerald, 27 Sep 2023
14 November 2023Senate backs a later fire-drill time, funds a toy drive. At the 23rd Senate's 11th meeting, senators unanimously passed Resolution 6-23-F, backing a change to DSU fire-drill timing from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. after the Mental Health and Wellness Committee argued the earlier hour caused sleep problems and anxiety for students on early schedules or with accommodations. They also unanimously passed Bill 12-23-F, allocating $200 from the legislative discretionary fund for a Boys and Girls Club of Bowling Green toy drive, and swore in newly elected ISEC senator Ashlee Potter. In the recordHerald, 15 Nov 2023
28 November 2023The 23rd Senate corrects its own governing documents. Three bills from the Legislative Operations Committee: fix references to a 'University Senate' that had since split into separate Faculty and Staff senates, reconcile bylaws language about expelling senators with a constitution that only provides for impeachment, and update committee names that had drifted. In the recordHerald, Nov 2023
23 January 2024Spring committee heads sworn in. At the spring semester's first meeting, Kurtz appointed Madison Parker Payne as Outreach Committee chair and Sophia Bryant as Mental Health and Well-Being Committee chair; both were approved without contested debate. Executive Vice President Annalise Finch appointed Jaden Marshall to chair the Graduate Advisory Council campus committee and Chloe Ralston to chair the Colonnade General Education committee. Kurtz urged senators to spend down the senate's still-large discretionary budget before the semester's end. In the recordHerald, 31 Jan 2024
24 January 2024Midyear resignations reshuffle the executive cabinet. President Sam Kurtz announced the resignations of Chief of Staff Lindsey Kelly and of Donte Reed as director of enrollment and student experience. The senate approved Kurtz's nominations of Reed as the new chief of staff and Sarah Vincent as director of enrollment and student activities. Kurtz also filled vacant transfer/non-traditional, sophomore and graduate senate seats with Sawyer Edmonds, Gabe Jerdon and Elizabeth Gannon. In the recordHerald, 24 Jan 2024
6 February 2024Cabinet requests censure hearing against León. Kurtz told the senate the Executive Cabinet had filed a formal report seeking a Judicial Council censure hearing against Administrative Vice President Salvador León. Chief Justice Isaac King said the cabinet's complaint was that León spent project funds before President Kurtz or EVP Finch consented, that he had done so after Kurtz conditioned permission on Bill 22-23-F first passing, and that he pushed PR Director Preston Romanov to promote Neurodiversity Week on SGA social media before the funding bill passed, effectively forcing the Senate's hand. The Executive Cabinet, excluding León, asked for a censure; the hearing was set for Feb. 7. In the recordHerald, 6 Feb 2024
9 February 2024Judicial council censures Salvador León. The SGA judicial council voted 6-0 to censure Administrative Vice President Salvador León after a Feb. 7 hearing on allegations that he spent funds, including a $425.25 Preston Center deposit for Neurodiversity Acceptance Week, before the senate passed the funding bill. León argued text messages showed President Sam Kurtz had accepted the spending, while Kurtz said he asked León multiple times not to spend before the bill passed. The council recommended no further disciplinary action beyond the censure. In the recordHerald, 9 Feb 2024
15 February 2024Uber voucher program and parking fee measures. President Sam Kurtz and Chief of Staff Donte Reed announced a program of 450 Uber vouchers worth $10 each, distributed through social media giveaways, meeting attendance and SGA events. The senate also passed Resolution 18-23-S supporting a cap on student parking fees at $50 and Bill 19-23-S allocating $700 to help financially vulnerable students pay parking fines, along with $1,045 in Dental Hygiene Center and ID Center vouchers. In the recordHerald, 15 Feb 2024
5 March 2024Rally trip to Frankfort, new voucher and cleanup plans. Kurtz previewed a senate trip to Frankfort for the Rally for Higher Education, where SGA planned to meet state Rep. Kevin Jackson and other Kentucky campus governments, and urged senators to seek re-election to preserve institutional knowledge. Chief of Staff Donté Reed introduced a need-based scholarship awarding four Uber vouchers and the Community Builder Excellence Scholarship for incoming Bowling Green-area freshmen. Campus Improvements and Sustainability chair Rush Robinson moved Earth Day from April 22 to April 19 and set a tentative Bowling Green cleanup for March 28. In the recordHerald, 6 Mar 2024
13 March 2024Funding for DEI Week and Spring Fling. At its 20th meeting the senate funded SGA Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Week, four days of themed tabling from March 25 to 28 covering mental health, campus demographics, sexual health and deaf awareness. A $450 bill for the SGA Spring Fling, whose proceeds went to the Kids Cancer Alliance, passed 28-2 after debate among senators over the amount being spent. A $280 bill funded a Hope Harbor Denim Day event for Sexual Assault Prevention Month. In the recordHerald, 13 Mar 2024
9 April 2024SGA closed the year with a Red Wave tailgate. SGA partnered with WKU Red Wave for the school year's last tailgate before a baseball game against Louisville, featuring winners of a "Battle of the DJs" social-media poll; sophomore Wilson Patterson won the $500 top scholarship prize as "DJ WLZN." Kurtz called the crowd to "savor one last tailgate of the 2023-2024 school year," with SGA grilling food for attendees. In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2024
16 April 2024Spring general election opened with over 60 candidates. Voting for the spring 2024 general election opened on TopNet with more than 60 students on the ballot for legislative seats. Kurtz, Chief of Staff Donté Reed and junior senator Ethan Taylor ran unopposed for student body president, executive vice president and administrative vice president respectively; the legislative council ballot included three senior, three junior and three sophomore senator seats, six college seats, an ISEC senator, a first-generation senator, a transfer/non-traditional senator and 14 senator-at-large seats. In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2024
17 April 202423rd Senate holds its final meeting. The 23rd Senate met for the last time with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on senators' final remarks. Kurtz thanked the senate and said in his final report, "We've done a lot of great things this year." Executive Vice President Annie Finch and Administrative Vice President Salvador León also gave closing reports before the 24th Senate's first meeting on April 23. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2024
17 April 2024Kurtz re-elected unopposed to a second term. Running with Chief of Staff Donté Reed for executive vice president and junior senator Ethan Taylor for administrative vice president, Kurtz was re-elected without opposition as the 24th Senate's 34 members were announced the same night. More than 60 students had appeared on the ballot for the spring 2024 general election. In the recordHerald, 17 Apr 2024

2024-25Sam Kurtz (president)

23 April 202424th Senate installed: Vincent elected speaker, Henderson named chief justice. At the 24th Senate's first meeting, newly elected senators were sworn in and Sarah Vincent, College of Health and Human Services senator, was elected Speaker of the Senate over Sophia Bryant. Senior senator Anne-Marie Wright was appointed Chief of Staff, and Associate Chief Justice Ellen Henderson was appointed Chief Justice. Outgoing Chief Justice Isaac King swore in the new officers, officially opening the 2024-25 term. In the recordHerald, 24 Apr 2024
27 August 2024Committee chairs and Judicial Council approved at fall opener. At the 24th Senate's first fall meeting, the Senate unanimously approved Kurtz's nominations of Aziz Umarov, Madison Payne, Neill Kane and Sam Dorris to the 2024-25 Judicial Council, and confirmed six committee chairs: Hannah Evans (Legislative Operations), Savanna Kurtz (Student Experience and Enrollment), Ryan Dilts (Outreach and Public Relations), Megan Farmer (DEI), Sophia Bryant (Student Mental Health and Wellbeing) and Annie Finch (Community Relations). President Timothy Caboni addressed the Senate on campus building renovations, the Mahurin Honors College restructuring and WKU's push for R2 research status. In the recordHerald, 27 Aug 2024
28 August 2024Senate passed $100,000 budget at first meeting. At its first meeting of the year on Aug. 27, the SGA Senate passed a $100,000 budget for 2024-25, including $20,000 for organizational aid, $23,500 for scholarships and $10,705 in legislative discretionary funding. Executive leaders told the Herald editorial board they intended to spend the full allocation, and President Sam Kurtz credited WKU President Caboni with keeping the budget level for several years. In the recordHerald, 28 Aug 2024
2 October 2024Fall election winners sworn in, school safety bill passed. Five senators elected in the fall election, three freshman senators plus an international and a Gatton Academy senator, were sworn in at the Oct. 1 meeting. The Senate passed three bills, including Bill 4-24-F to make school safety training mandatory for WKU professors and require posted emergency exits in classrooms, and two bills backing a Spooktober fundraiser for the Potter Children's Home Initiative. In the recordHerald, 2 Oct 2024
22 October 2024Senate backs Myanmar flag, funds organizational aid and calculators. The Senate unanimously passed Resolution 5-24-F backing a Myanmar flag on the empty pole outside the Mahurin Honors College, sought by senators after students said Burmese and Chin students had no flag representing them; Bill 9-24-F distributed $10,000 in fall Organizational Aid funding across 58 graded applications; and Bill 10-24-F added $540 to buy five more calculators for the Borrow-a-Calculator program, which had lent 28 calculators that semester. Kurtz appointed freshman Emaun Riley as ISEC senator and Mahurin Honors College senator Caden Lucas as the Senate's parliamentarian. In the recordHerald, 23 Oct 2024
7 November 2024Three senators removed for excessive absences. Senators Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty were removed from their seats at a Nov. 6 censure meeting after each accumulated at least six unexcused absences from weekly senate meetings. The Judicial Council voted 7-0 to remove them under a constitutional provision requiring removal of any senator censured twice, calling the decision a matter of accountability rather than an attack on character. In the recordHerald, 7 Nov 2024
5 February 2025Trump DEI order prompted constitutional review. Chief Justice Morgan Gammons said the SGA Constitution might require amendment to its diversity, equity and inclusion provisions after President Trump's executive order directing federal agencies to end DEI mandates. Gammons said the Judicial Council would meet to decide whether an amendment was needed, noting that WKU receives federal funding as a public university. The Senate also filled several appointed positions at the same meeting. In the recordHerald, 5 Feb 2025
11 February 2025A mental health survey, and a warning about the election. The Senate passed Bill 4-25-S funding a DEI Committee tabling event to gather anonymous mental health survey responses. Dean of Students Martha Sales told the Senate 'you cannot isolate and educate at the same time'. Kurtz warned repeatedly that an unusually senior chamber made the spring election matter more than usual. In the recordHerald, Feb 2025
26 February 2025Resolution backed Gordon Wilson Hall elevator. The Senate passed Resolution 2-25-S supporting installation of elevators in Gordon Wilson Hall, prompted by wheelchair user Kiersten Washington, whose dance appreciation class was scheduled on the building's third floor. It also passed Resolution 1-25-S supporting 24/7 hours at The Commons at Helm Library during finals week, and Kurtz announced a POLLapalooza effort with a goal of 3,000 voters in the April election. In the recordHerald, 26 Feb 2025
26 March 2025Resolution supported mental health advisory board. The Senate passed Resolution 4-25-S supporting the formation of a Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Advisory Board to advise upper-level administration on student mental health policy, with Dean of Students Martha Sales planned to oversee its creation. Co-author Emma Harris, the Resident Staff Association president, said Counseling Center staffing shortages had pushed students to rely on resident advisors. The Senate passed eight bills at the same meeting. In the recordHerald, 26 Mar 2025
4 April 2025Senate voted to rename DEI Committee. Senators unanimously passed Bill 21-25-S, a constitutional amendment restructuring the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee and renaming it the Action and Opportunity Committee, following President Trump's executive order dismantling DEI mandates. The meeting initially lacked the 21 members needed for a two-thirds vote, so absent members were called onto Zoom to reach quorum. The amendment then went to a student referendum during the April 13-15 election. In the recordHerald, 4 Apr 2025
15 April 2025Rush Robinson elected on a turnout of 966. Elected alongside class, college, transfer, first-generation, Intercultural Student Engagement Center and Honors College senators - constituencies the 1966 constitution had no concept of. In the recordWKU News
16 April 2025Students ratified DEI amendment with 88% of vote. In the spring election, the student body approved Bill 21-25-S, the constitutional amendment renaming the DEI Committee to the Action and Opportunity Committee, with 88% of votes in favor. Committee chair Megan Farmer said the committee at its core was not changing and the rename was meant to better communicate its actions. Results for 31 senate seats were announced the same night. In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2025
16 April 202524th Senate held final meeting. The 24th Senate met for the last time on April 15 with no legislation on the agenda, spending the meeting on farewells. President Sam Kurtz, Vice President Donte Reed and Chief Financial Officer Ethan Taylor each received a standing ovation, and the Senate recorded 295 spring scholarship applications, far above the roughly 40-applicant average of past years. In the recordHerald, 16 Apr 2025

2025-26Rush Robinson (president)

22 April 2025Robinson reappoints Jenkins chief communications officer. In one of his first acts after taking office, Robinson reappointed Preston Jenkins as chief communications officer; the Senate later confirmed the pick unanimously. In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2025
8 August 2025Robinson sworn in as student regent, succeeding Kurtz. The Board of Regents administered Robinson's oath of office as student regent, succeeding graduating president Sam Kurtz. At the same meeting the board elected Jan West chair, Doris Thomas vice chair and Melissa Dennison secretary for 2025-26. In the recordWKU News - Board of Regents, 8 Aug 2025
18 August 2025Chandler Hall opened for the fall semester. The new Gordon Ford College of Business building, named Amy and David Chandler Hall after a $7.5 million gift and funded largely by a Kentucky General Assembly appropriation, opened to students on the first day of fall classes. In the recordWKU News - Board of Regents, 8 Aug 2025
19 August 2025SGA commissioned a student-painted mural for the chambers. Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins announced a plan to have four student artists each paint one side of a column in the SGA chambers, incorporating WKU campus elements, with selections due by 19 September. In the recordHerald, 15 Sep 2025
25 November 2025Senate revived the transcript voucher program. The senate passed Bill 24-25-F, authored by Legislative Operations Committee Chair Caden Lucas, allocating $195 to reestablish the transcript voucher program, giving students one free official transcript a semester. It also funded a new "Professor of the Month" award and ping pong equipment for the DSU recreation area. In the recordHerald, 27 Nov 2025
10 February 2026WKU Restaurant Group answered senators' questions. Restaurant Group representatives fielded senator questions on the removal of Steak 'n Shake seasoning, kiosks in Subway and adding spicy chicken sandwiches to Chick-fil-A's meal-swipe menu, and said the service handled about 60,000 meal transactions a week. In the recordHerald, 11 Feb 2026
17 February 2026CPR-voucher bill and Grise Hall accessibility resolution passed. The senate unanimously passed Bill 2-26-S, funding six vouchers for free CPR certification, and Resolution 7-25-F, supporting additional handicapped-accessible restroom stalls in Grise Hall after a student's father said the building had only one large stall. In the recordHerald, 17 Feb 2026
24 February 2026Senate adopted a fully codified rewrite of its bylaws. The Senate adopted an official codified version of the SGA Executive and Legislative Bylaws, superseding all prior versions, effective 24 February 2026. In the recordWKU SGA, Executive and Legislative Bylaws, as amended 24 Feb 2026Read it here
24 March 2026SGA funded a tailgate to boost turnout at a baseball game. SGA used its projects fund to host free hot dogs, giveaways and a scholarship drawing before WKU baseball's home game against Louisville, an effort Robinson said answered Athletics Director Todd Stewart's call for more student engagement at games. In the recordHerald, 25 Mar 2026
2 April 2026Senate learns the Gilbane housing partnership cleared the legislature. At its Thursday meeting SGA senators learned that the Kentucky Legislature had approved WKU's public-private partnership with developer Gilbane, which the Board of Regents had provisionally approved 11 December 2025 to design and build a new residence hall replacing Douglas Keen and Hugh Poland Halls. "WKU is now in the clear to start building the new residence halls," said Senator Jakob Barker, who with Senator Ethan Vietze also sponsored Resolution 7-26-S, backing a crosswalk at Alumni Avenue and Kentucky Street for residents of the 1355 Kentucky Street apartments who Barker's resolution said had to "step into oncoming traffic" to reach the Alumni Square parking garage. The same meeting passed legislation funding textbooks, exam supplies and lab goggles and authorizing a student-experience survey. In the recordHerald, 5 Apr 2026
7 April 2026Weekly meeting funded a senior cookout, transfer cords and spikeball nets. SGA allocated $602.58 through three bills and a resolution: a senior sunset cookout, 240 transfer-student graduation cords, borrowable spikeball nets, and DSU signage improvements. CFO Gabriel Jerdon said the legislative discretionary fund would have $71.17 left if the following week's final bills all passed as written. In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2026
7 April 2026Two tickets take questions in the DSU auditorium. Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry against Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated questions submitted by the student body. In the recordHerald, April 2026
14 April 202625th Senate closes the year having passed 56 bills, the most since 2018-19. The 25th Senate's final meeting passed its last three bills of the year - funding an NPHC preview day, the Office of Sustainability's food pantry, and massage-therapy vouchers for finals week, the latter two amended to spend down the year's remaining $71.17 budget - bringing the year's total to 56 pieces of legislation. Chief Communications Officer Preston Jenkins reported that WKU's new Artificial Intelligence Committee, which he sat on, was in early talks about bulk subscriptions to AI products such as ChatGPT Pro for all students and a possible introductory AI course for freshmen. Guest speakers included a Parking and Transportation representative, who said the bus system's diesel bill had roughly doubled amid rising fuel prices. The Herald identified her as "Ginny Griffin"; the official senate minutes give her name as "Jenny Griffith" - unresolved which is correct. In the recordHerald, 14 Apr 2026Read it here
15 April 2026Turnout jumps 66% in a contested race. 1,601 students voted, 635 more than the year before. Lucas won. The clearest evidence in the whole record that WKU turnout tracks whether there is an actual contest. In the recordWKU News - Lucas elected
16 April 2026Robinson tells the Faculty Senate to look at the dorms. Sitting next to Faculty Regent Shane Spiller during a discussion of WKU housing, Robinson told senators to 'take a field trip' and see the state of the residence halls. In the recordHerald, April 2026
18 April 2026Year-long mental health push closed with the Out of Darkness Walk. Robinson and Mental Health and Wellbeing Committee chair Veronica Butler spent the year pressing WKU on student mental health, citing data from social work professor Jay Gabbard that 44 percent of students reported depression symptoms and 10 percent had considered suicide in the past year. SGA co-ran Mental Health Week with the WKU Counseling Center and campus NAMI chapter, launched a Toppers Talk About It campaign, and forwarded student recommendations - including moving counseling services out of Potter Hall - through the Counseling Center Review Committee. The year closed with an Out of Darkness suicide-remembrance walk on April 18; incoming president Caden Lucas said the focus would continue. In the recordHerald, 29 Apr 2026
28 April 2026The red suit jacket changes hands. At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, Robinson handed Lucas the red suit jacket, "the one that Sam (Kurtz) gave me." The same night, Gabby Pace, Cayden Bailey, Maggie Phelps and Jaden Marshall were sworn in to their new roles. In the recordHerald, April 2026
5 June 2026Robinson cast the lone dissenting vote on a tuition increase. At his last meeting as student regent, Robinson voted against a $204, 1.69 percent tuition increase that the rest of the Board of Regents approved, saying the board had to do everything it could to preserve affordability. In the recordHerald, 5 Jun 2026

2026-27Caden Lucas (president)

8 April 2026Executive candidates face off at SGA town hall. SGA held a town hall in the Downing Student Union Auditorium for the two executive tickets: Caden Lucas with Jakob Barker and Will Derryberry, and Jaden Marshall with Kaden Blankenship and Miles VanRude. Chief Justice Sophie Stirling moderated as the candidates answered 27 questions submitted by students. Both tickets made increasing awareness of SGA operations and outreach to the student body their central campaign promise. In the recordHerald, 8 Apr 2026
9 April 2026Herald and Revolution Radio hosted a presidential debate. College Heights Herald Editor-in-Chief Jake McMahon and Assistant News Editor Kane Smith sat down with presidential candidates Caden Lucas and Jaden Marshall for a debate co-hosted with campus station Revolution Radio, ahead of voting opening the following Monday on TopNet. In the recordHerald, 9 Apr 2026
15 April 2026Caden Lucas wins SGA presidential election. Caden Lucas and his ticket of Vice President-elect Jakob Barker and Chief Financial Officer-elect Will Derryberry won the spring election to serve during the 2026-27 academic year, defeating Jaden Marshall's ticket. Lucas, a junior senator, WKU Spiritmaster and chairman of the Hilltoppers Vote Coalition, ran on the motto "Lead, build, deliver" and a promise to make SGA operations more visible to students. The Herald did not publish vote totals or turnout figures; the story also listed the full slate of senators elected to the incoming 26th Senate. In the recordHerald, 15 Apr 2026
24 April 2026Lucas named a 2026 Truman Scholar. Days after taking SGA's top office, President Caden Lucas was named a 2026 Truman Scholar, WKU's second in the scholarship's history and Kentucky's only recipient that year. The award, chosen from 781 candidates at 305 colleges nationally, provides $30,000 toward graduate or professional study and recognizes commitment to public service. In the recordWKU News, 24 Apr 2026
28 April 202626th Senate seated; tie vote for speaker resolved in Butler's favor. At the first meeting of the 26th Senate, outgoing president Rush Robinson passed the traditional red suit jacket to Caden Lucas, and the body swore in Gabi Pace as chief of staff, Cayden Bailey as chief communications officer, Maggie Phelps to the judicial council and defeated presidential candidate Jaden Marshall as an at-large senator. The race for speaker of the senate ended in a 9-9 tie between Amelia Tucker and Veronica Butler, and Chief Justice Sophie Sterling confirmed that neither the constitution nor the bylaws addressed a tie. Outgoing speaker Hadley Whipple ordered a re-vote, which elected Butler as speaker. In the recordHerald, 28 Apr 2026
11 May 2026Lucas named ODK Circle Leader of the Year. WKU's Omicron Delta Kappa circle named President Caden Lucas its Heather Strode Circle Leader of the Year, an award for a student demonstrating leadership and dedication to the campus community across ODK's five core values. In the recordWKU News, 11 May 2026
2 June 2026Lucas voices concern over proposed tuition increase. WKU released a proposed 2026-27 budget that would raise tuition by $210 to $6,246 per semester within a $405.1 million operating plan. Lucas, identified as SGA president and soon-to-be student regent, said he was "generally concerned" by a proposal that would raise the cost of attending WKU. He said students deserved both a high-quality education and an affordable way to achieve it. In the recordHerald, 2 Jun 2026
5 June 2026Regents approve tuition increase over student regent's lone no vote. The Board of Regents approved a $204 tuition increase to $6,240 per semester, the sixth consecutive yearly increase, along with a 5% housing rate increase and a 2% meal plan increase as part of a $405 million operating budget. Every regent voted in favor except outgoing SGA president Rush Robinson, casting his final vote as student regent before Lucas took the seat. The board also suspended several majors, including kinesiology and geological sciences, for reworking and mergers. In the recordHerald, 5 Jun 2026
7 July 2026SGA got a new adviser in Student Activities leadership change. Andrew Rash, who had served as SGA's faculty adviser and Associate Director of Student Activities and Greek Life since 2022, became interim director of the Department of Student Activities on July 1 following the retirement of longtime director Charley Pride. Assistant Director of Student Activities and Leadership and Volunteerism Amelia Kolb took over as SGA's adviser going forward. In the recordHerald, 7 Jul 2026

What this is

A year-by-year record of student government at Western Kentucky University, from the ratification of the Associated Students constitution in April 1966 to the present. Every entry names the source it came from.

Corrections

The names here start with the plaque in the SGA Chambers, and the plaque is known to be wrong in places. Where the archive disagrees with it, this site follows the archive and records the change on the corrections page. If you served, or you know that a year here is wrong, the project wants to hear from you through the Student Government Association office.

Reuse

Text on this site is the work of the project. Photographs, documents and legislation are reproduced from Western Kentucky University's own open archives and from the College Heights Herald and the Talisman; each item names the collection, issue and page it came from and links to the original.

Built 4 August 2026. The whole record is readable as data: years.json. Method and scope are set out on the about page.
